terms.meaning: The lowest of man's lives, in which fallen man is; its release is what the magic of the self-will exploits; reached from present life through the clairvoyant life by repeated fermentation; it 'moves in and with the creative Essence'; to be raised through the medial life; the seeker in it shows the Golden Fleece. By the ordering of ¶32-35 it corresponds to the Infernal (lumbar, voluntary) life, but the text does not state the identity.

quotes.text: that third life which moves in and with the creative Essence
Man is fallen; he is in the third or lowest life

terms.meaning: Will acting for itself rather than under God's law; its magic is the Egyptians' enchantment; power taken into it becomes diabolical.

quotes.text: The magic of the self-will is that which the Egyptians practiced in the days of Moses
taken into the self-will and used accordingly it becomes diabolical

terms.meaning: The intermediate state through which present life is led into the third life.

quotes.text: this present life may be led through the clairvoyant life into it

terms.meaning: The sleep-walkers' entranced life, produced by fermenting present life by its similar; the third life is not known in it.

equivalences.quote: the common entranced life, i.e., the life of the sleep-walkers

quotes.text: leads into the common trance, or is entranced

terms.meaning: The core operation: a life fermented by its similar passes into a further state; repeated over and over; the word best conveys perfecting, transmutation, fixation and immortality.

quotes.text: The word fermentation conveys an idea of the perfecting principle and of the possibility of transmutation beyond any other word
it is the best image of the Divine Art which earthly processes give

terms.meaning: That in and with which the third life moves.

quotes.text: that third life which moves in and with the creative Essence

terms.meaning: The power to which the mind becomes related on entering the third life, so that it can act Its will.

quotes.text: related to the Universal Vitalizing Power, and so can act Its will

terms.meaning: In one form the Principle of all growth; can be collected and brought to bear on a germ.

equivalences.quote: The Universal Spirit is in one form the Principle of all growth

terms.meaning: A universal art of vital chemistry that ferments, purifies and dissolves the human spirit into new life; the transmutation of Life; the fermenting of the vital Spirit in and by its own Light; brings man into relationship with God.

equivalences.quote: Alchemy is Divine Chemistry, and the transmutation of Life
hence it is called by the Adepts Holy Alchemy

quotes.text: Alchemy is an universal art of vital chemistry
Alchemy is a process of fermenting the vital Spirit in and by its own Light.

terms.meaning: The efflux of the regenerated life, drawn to a focus and made manifest as a concrete Essence of Light.

equivalences.quote: the Philosopher’s Stone is the efflux of such a life, drawn to a focus and made manifest as a concrete Essence of Light

terms.meaning: What the Stone is made manifest as; it is the true Form or Idea of Gold.

equivalences.with: true Form or Idea of Gold
equivalences.quote: which Essence is the true Form or Idea of Gold

terms.meaning: The true Source of consciousness and of all things, which consciousness drawn centrally comes to know.

equivalences.quote: its own true Source, which is the Universal Center and source of all things

terms.meaning: The cause of a being's existence, which each has in himself; knowing it is knowing the cause of all, since Existence is one.

quotes.text: the consciousness can be brought into contact with its First Cause

terms.meaning: In higher states moves from its own center; in act effervesces its own substance; the only substance; its efflux is chaotic and must be taken up by an external mind.

equivalences.quote: it is the Universal Loadstone of Existence

quotes.text: for Will has substance, nay, is the only substance

terms.meaning: The vital power, at a certain time seated in the lumbar region and sent back.

equivalences.quote: the power, the vital or willing-power

terms.meaning: A law that must move through Love in the will and act on the will-moved mind, which must be subservient to it or become demoniacal.

quotes.text: there is a law of Light, which must move through Love in the will

terms.meaning: The Divine line in all things; in mesmerizing it withdraws from sense; were it stronger in us than the transverse, we would no longer be in sense.

equivalences.quote: The perpendicular line is the Divine line in all things

terms.meaning: The contrary of the Divine line; restores to sense; united with the perpendicular it forms a cross.

quotes.text: the transverse line is the contrary; the two united form a cross +

terms.meaning: Where the Ideas are; appears to the spirit in the medial life as its azure sky.

quotes.text: the Upper Ether, where the Ideas are

terms.meaning: The middle life, through which the third life is raised and born; the exalted spirit is the spirit in it; the medial spirit is what is changed when life is attracted inward.

equivalences.quote: born through the medial or celestial life

equivalences.with: exalted spirit (the spirit in this life)
equivalences.quote: the exalted spirit, i.,e., the spirit in the medial life

quotes.text: the medial spirit is changed; life is attracted in, instead of out

terms.meaning: Swedenborgian term for the relation between the brain (to outward life) and the spiritual head (to the spirit).

quotes.text: There is, as the Swedenborgians would say, a correspondence between them.

terms.meaning: Man, who comprehends and represents the whole and each of the three Lives; its limbs are a laboratory for the spirit.

quotes.text: man, being a microcosm, comprehends and represents the whole and each

terms.meaning: An image thrown forth, macrocosmic, passive and ephemeral for want of consubstantiality; its perfect beauty attracts the soul and, united to it, brings the ideal forth as actual offspring.

equivalences.quote: The macrocosmic image of the microcosm is the downward-born nature
It is the Eve which Adam brought forth

terms.meaning: The vehicle of the dead Divine Life within us, and at the same time the death of itself.

quotes.text: The Hermetic sepulcher is the vehicle of the dead Divine Life within us

terms.meaning: The first conceived Paternal Light; the metaphysical seed of mineral gold.

equivalences.quote: The Gold Alchemical is the first conceived Paternal Light
it is the seed metaphysical of mineral gold

terms.meaning: The animal (that is, opposite) will clothed in Light; the third which rises in opposition to the first.

quotes.text: The ‘orient animal’ means the animal (that is, the opposite) will which is clothed in Light
the third which rises in opposition to the first

terms.meaning: The outward appearance, of a purplish luster, of the light of Life diffused over the seeker's body in the third life.

quotes.text: The Golden Fleece is the outward appearance presented by the light of Life diffused over the body of the seeker in the third life

terms.meaning: The seeker at the point of relation where the Golden Fleece appears: the discoverer, the finder.

equivalences.quote: The seeker, however, in this point of relation, is the adept, the discoverer, the finder.

terms.meaning: Spherical 'world forms' that successively form in the lower development of the Hermetic life but, lacking the Light Essential, resolve and die.

quotes.text: these world forms are unstable and, uninformed with the Light Essential, resolve and die

terms.meaning: That which the quintessences lack, so that they die; not further defined here.

quotes.text: uninformed with the Light Essential, resolve and die

terms.meaning: The three principles of the vital force in the blood.

equivalences.quote: Attraction, Circulation, Repulsion --- the Alchemical Salt, Mercury, Sulphur

terms.meaning: Where the principle of body is preserved; from that one principle the whole life is restored.

equivalences.quote: what they call the ashes or Caput Mortuum

equivalences.with: our pigmy / diadem of the body (Khunrath)
equivalences.quote: Khunrath call it ‘our pigmy’, also the ‘diadem of the body’
I think he refers to it under the term Duanach

terms.meaning: In Boehme's language the sidereal and elementary birth; the medium of perceiving the First, which is hidden in its mineral life; that life is full of defilement and temptation.

equivalences.quote: the Third Principle, i.e., the sidereal and elementary birth, to use Boehme’s language

quotes.text: is the medium of perceiving the First, which is hidden in its mineral life

terms.meaning: What Alchemy ferments in and by its own Light; present in the Universal as well as the individual.

quotes.text: The Vital Spirit is in the Universal as well as in the individual.

terms.meaning: The sensuous life; represents the Animal Kingdom; dominates the head in man; typifies the highest life man must not aspire to.

quotes.text: The Terrestrial is the sensuous and represents the Animal Kingdom. In man it is dominating the head.

terms.meaning: The emotional, receptive, instinctive life; represents the Vegetable Kingdom; resides in the epigastric region, its workshop the solar plexus; identified with the medial life, through which the third life must be born.

quotes.text: The Celestial is the emotional, receptive, instinctive life, and represents the Vegetable Kingdom.

terms.meaning: The voluntary agent in life; represents the Mineral Kingdom; resides in man in the lumbar region.

quotes.text: The Infernal is the voluntary agent in life, and represents the Mineral Kingdom.

terms.meaning: Paracelsus' term, set in apposition to the solar plexus, the workshop of the Celestial life.

equivalences.quote: the solar plexus, the Archaeus of Paracelsus, is its workshop

terms.meaning: The beginning/principle of the work, identified with the intention; hard to find because the rational ferment is hidden in our life.

equivalences.quote: The difficulty is to find this principium, the intention

terms.meaning: Hidden in our ordinary life; given as the reason the principium is hard to find.

equivalences.quote: the rational ferment, the pure aurific seed of Light, is hidden in this life of ours

terms.meaning: The practitioner who begins, ends and repeats the experiment.

quotes.text: as the Artist begins, ends, and repeats the mysterious experiment

terms.meaning: The third or lowest life in man, mineral in origin; the subject the Hermetic Art perfects; brings one into contact with the Macrocosmic mineral life; lower than the Vegetable and Animal lives in us; first seen by introspection as a dark vapour.

equivalences.with: third life; lowest life in man
equivalences.quote: The third life, the mineral or lowest life in man

equivalences.with: mineral soul; lowest form of life in us
equivalences.quote: The mineral soul or the lowest form of life in us

quotes.text: The Vegetable and Animal lives are higher than the mineral life in us.
a perfectioning of the third or lowest or the mineral life in man

terms.meaning: The one life we presently live; we have no right to be efficient in it; the Hermetically regenerated give it up.

equivalences.quote: the Head life or the animal, the rational life

quotes.text: We live in but one life, the head life, but there are three possible lives

terms.meaning: The life in which we ought to be efficient; through it we are efficient for the divine life immediately over us.

equivalences.quote: efficient in the medial life --- in faith

terms.meaning: One of three modes of consciousness (with the sensible and the perceptive); conjoined to the other two it makes them efficient.

quotes.text: either in the sensible, the perceptive, or the power life; this last conjoined to the other two makes them efficient

terms.meaning: Our present state.

quotes.text: Our present state is one of inversion.

terms.meaning: The perfected lowest life, its true consummation, mineral in origin; analogous to Christ the Head Corner Stone.

equivalences.quote: the Stone of the Wise is the perfected lowest life, its true consummation

terms.meaning: The perfecting of the mineral life in man, typifying the celestial and Divine; a question put to Nature respecting the first cause.

quotes.text: The Art is a question put to Nature respecting the first cause

terms.meaning: Experimentation into the Universal Spirit through man; the art by which a particular spirit is allied to the universal.

quotes.text: a development of the art by which a particular spirit (to use Vaughan’s words) is allied to the universal

terms.meaning: The magnetism of Light according to its own law; that Law is its emanating spirit, called wisdom.

equivalences.quote: Hermetism is the magnetism of Light according to its own law

terms.meaning: The Law of Light, its emanating spirit; in its Spirit one may see the nature and virtues of all things.

equivalences.with: Law of Light; its emanating spirit
equivalences.quote: which Law is its emanating spirit called wisdom, for it is the Wisdom

quotes.text: If you find the Wisdom, and coming out in the Spirit of Wisdom, look into the world

terms.meaning: The art of fermenting the human vital spirit to purify it and finally dissolve it, so that the principle is reconstructed through a regeneration.

quotes.text: Alchemy is the art of fermenting the human vital spirit

terms.meaning: The throwing down of the walls of the harmony-ensphered life; accompanied with noise.

equivalences.quote: The throwing down of the Walls of this is harmony-ensphered life is the Alchemical solution

terms.meaning: The enclosing of the lower life, figured by the Walls of Troy, done in a great resonance.

quotes.text: of the insphering of the lower life; it is done in a great resonance

terms.meaning: The flashing center of the lower life (Apollo); its setting free produces harmony.

quotes.text: Apollo is that life, and it is coruscant

terms.meaning: Behmen's term for what is evolved in the harmony when the coruscant center of the lower life is set free.

equivalences.quote: what Behmen calls the Mercurius, or spirit of the Sound, is evolved

terms.meaning: The impure natural-born vital spirit.

equivalences.quote: The body of brass is the impure natural-born vital spirit.

terms.meaning: Man's life-spirit; impure as naturally born; what Alchemy ferments, purifies and dissolves.

quotes.text: the human vital spirit

terms.meaning: The life passed between fermented lives; it progresses by transmission from agent to patient.

quotes.text: That is the law of progression of the Vital force

terms.meaning: The growth-causing spirit, predominant in the vegetable kingdom.

equivalences.quote: The Vegetable spirit is the growth-causing spirit

terms.meaning: The vital fire of the natural life; fermented by the same life from another, it is opened and frees the celestial Life and Light.

quotes.text: sets free the celestial Life and Light

terms.meaning: The action of one life on another (or on the vital spirit) that opens it and frees a higher life; also the action of the Vitalizing or Divine principles, from which seven is a rest.

quotes.text: When one life being fermented throws its life to another equally fermented
a Rest from the ferment or action of the Vitalizing or Divine principles

terms.meaning: The imparted spirit whose reception gives wisdom by awakening a consciousness related to the universal.

quotes.text: the wisdom imparted by the reception of the Afflatus

terms.meaning: To give specific quality and form; essence is qualitated by Ideas, and the speech of Mind qualitates in the pure Ether.

equivalences.quote: essence is qualitated, i.e., specificated, and receives form from Ideas

quotes.text: The speech of Mind uttered into the pure Ether qualitates and specificates.

terms.meaning: That from which essence receives form.

equivalences.quote: Ideas or the universal forms of Nature

terms.meaning: Something humanly producible, which may be unlawfully formed finitely for a particular end.

quotes.text: it is a taking the First Mater which is humanly producible

terms.meaning: In a special sense: man specificating and qualitating from his own mind, forming the First Mater for a particular end.

quotes.text: in this consists the true idolatry against which the Bible so strongly protests

terms.meaning: The receiving medium through which universal principles are conceived; nature lacks a true one; it must be pure and simple for truth.

quotes.text: There is no such thing as truth absolute in nature, because she has no true conceptive vehicle
Thus everything depends on the purity of the receiving power.

terms.meaning: Not to be found on earth (Lully); Plotinus shows how it is generated.

quotes.text: You may find out in Plotinus how that pure matter is generated.

terms.meaning: Two-fold: the mundane, full of false forms, and the pure, not of this world, connected with the supersensual life. The Universal Ether is the quintessence of the four elements and the Quintessence of both worlds.

equivalences.with: quintessence of the four principles called elements
equivalences.quote: This Ether is a quintessence of those very four principles, which they call elements.
It is the Quintessence of both worlds.

quotes.text: The Ether is two-fold: the mundane, which is full of the false forms; the pure, which is not of this world

terms.meaning: In alchemical usage, the four elements (principles) of the Universal Ether.

equivalences.with: four elements of the Universal Ether
equivalences.quote: Alchemists refer to the four elements of the Universal Ether

terms.meaning: The essence of a whole: the Ether of the four elements and of both worlds; man of the whole creation; woman of man.

quotes.text: As man was the Quintessence of the whole creation, so woman was the Quintessence of man --- the love-spirit was in her.

terms.meaning: The principle of the body, which is Will.

equivalences.quote: There is no true body but Will; it is the principle of the body --- the Salt.

terms.meaning: Creates an image, not a being; passing into desire for the image it unites with it into a being. The only true body.

quotes.text: Will creates an image, not a being.

terms.meaning: Paracelsus's term, applied to the dream of its whole afterlife with which the soul enters the body, its destiny, which moves a will that does not see beyond it. God's grace is called 'the Divine evestrum, relatively to man', by which we overcome it.

quotes.text: the soul comes into this body with the dream of its whole afterlife presented to it
God’s grace (the Divine evestrum, relatively to man)

terms.meaning: The self-willed life; entraps the Light and craves more; overcome by satiation and then transmuted.

equivalences.quote: Saturn or the self-willed life

quotes.text: the selfish Saturnine life in man

terms.meaning: What must be given from without, in plenty, to satiate Saturn.

equivalences.with: honey of the bees; aurific seed
equivalences.quote: plenty "of the honey of the bees", the aurific seed, the Rational Light

terms.meaning: Hidden in the self-begotten life, which appropriates the Divine Life instead of serving it.

equivalences.quote: The Divine Light, the Essence of Gold

terms.meaning: 'This life of ours', in which the Divine Light is hidden and which appropriates it.

quotes.text: This life of ours, instead of administering to the Divine Life, appropriates it.

terms.meaning: That in which the whole image of the macrocosm is formed and typically represented.

quotes.text: The whole image of the macrocosm is formed, and has consequently its typical representation, in the Microcosm

terms.meaning: The recreative process in which the principle of the vital spirit is reconstructed and the macrocosm's image is evolved before the mental eye; the Hermetically regenerated give up the head life.

quotes.text: so that the principle be reconstructed through a regeneration
the recreative process of the regeneration

terms.meaning: That into which an entrance clears the understanding to know things in their roots; not further defined here.

quotes.text: the knowledge of things in their roots

terms.meaning: The whole doctrine of ontological infolding: emanation from the superstantial Light or will; the darkness is the emanation; the qualitated and flat becomes cubic by multiplication into itself.

equivalences.quote: The darkness is the emanation

quotes.text: emanation from the superstantial Light or will

terms.meaning: Used for the emanation's passage from flat to cubic: 'Mathesis becoming geometric'.

quotes.text: It is Mathesis becoming geometric.

terms.meaning: That into which the Hermetic Philosophy experiments through man; the Universal must be developed in one to be understood.

quotes.text: you must have the Universal developed in you before you can understand the Universal

terms.meaning: Nature's being taken from the primal source into a will (sentence garbled as printed).

quotes.text: Nature has taken from the primal source into a will is the history of the Fall.

terms.meaning: Our life now goes forth into a line; it must be taken up into a circle (the circular life), back into its first source.

quotes.text: Our life goes forth into a line at present, it has to be taken up into a circle

terms.meaning: Its great principle is a Rest from the ferment of the Vitalizing or Divine principles.

quotes.text: The great principle of the number seven is a Rest

terms.meaning: The impure atmosphere surrounding each individual life, perceived by clairvoyants, where all thoughts and desires are imaged; its density or lightness causes darkness or brightness in men. Purifying it is the aim of the Mystery.

quotes.text: all the thoughts and desires of life are imaged there

terms.meaning: Loosening the bond between spirit and its corporeal media; Paracelsus speaks of it; mesmerism imitates it externally.

quotes.text: an imitation of the Divine Art of the separation of which Paracelsus speaks

terms.meaning: A very external imitation of the Divine Art of separation; by vertical passes it loosens spirit from its corporeal media for the moment.

quotes.text: The action of mesmerism is a very external way

terms.meaning: Expressed by Behmen: an Eternal Will arises in the No Thing to bring it into Something, that the Will might behold itself. The Hermetic Work images this order.

quotes.text: The Law of Divine Manifestation is expressed in those striking words of Behmen

terms.meaning: That in which the Eternal Will arises; that which is before all things; Wisdom's end is a return into it.

quotes.text: bringing back into the Nothing which is before all things

terms.meaning: Early results of the work: real but not permanent, to be sacrificed for the promise they contain.

quotes.text: The first-fruits, tough perfectly real, should not be accepted as permanent

terms.meaning: Experimental contact of mind with mystery: the mind consciously enters the Universal and knows itself in its principle, with an efflux of life.

quotes.text: True Knowledge is experimental contact of mind with mystery

terms.meaning: The voluntary substance, bound in the generative mineral life; drawn up into the medial life it becomes Light and grows. Also named among the principles (Sulphur, Salt, Mercury).

equivalences.quote: The Slat is the voluntary substance

quotes.text: the Salt thus transplanted becomes Light and grows

terms.meaning: Wisdom, the Universal Will, which dissipates the impure sulphurs in the individual will.

equivalences.quote: The great Salt Sea (Wisdom, the Universal Will)
The great Salt Sea (Wisdom, the Universal Will)

terms.meaning: The middle level of life, between the mineral and the higher; the heart center is that of the celestial medial vegetable life. The Salt is drawn up into it.

quotes.text: must be translated or drawn up into the medial life
the heart of the celestial medial vegetable life

terms.meaning: Theosophy on its physical side: a change in the circulatory system of the blood wrought by reiterative contritions; distinguished from what the world has sought without finding.

quotes.text: True Alchemy (not that which the world has run after without finding) is related to Theosophy on its physical side

terms.meaning: Stirred in the surrounding spirit by the growing Light of the Salt; reiterated, it absorbs the sensuous medium and changes the circulation of the blood.

quotes.text: reiterative contritions absorbing the sensuous medium

terms.meaning: An entity of light: the purer conscious ens of light carried back to God; the Philosophic Matter (excruciated); the Stone (real).

quotes.text: the purer conscious ens of light

terms.meaning: Bringing the whole of life into the Sonship; the death to sin with a new birth. Begun by the pure earth; highest when the spirit, dead to its identity, re-arises as the Divine image.

quotes.text: It is the death to sin with a new birth awakened in us
that is the condition of the highest regeneration

terms.meaning: A mid-point between mind and matter, by which mind is moved into matter.

quotes.text: Emotion is a mid-point between the two

terms.meaning: What the Hermetic names (Sulphur, Salt, Mercury, water, air, fire) relate to, as opposed to qualities; in the spirit they become qualities.

quotes.text: in the spirit they become qualities

terms.meaning: Forms; the false or impure sulphurs are the desires and phantasms of mundane life in the individual will, to be purified or extirpated. 'Sulphur' is also named as a principle.

equivalences.quote: by sulphurs I mean forms
the impure sulphurs (desires, phantasms)

terms.meaning: Named with Sulphur and Salt as a principle. In Eirenaeus's quotation, a bottomless Mercury into which the matter that is gold is thrown. Not decoded further here.

quotes.text: such a Mercury as is bottomless, whose center it can never find but by discovering its own

terms.meaning: A point in the process with no attraction but indifference to both life and death, when the Artist must stir up the Motion.

quotes.text: there is a point of passivity

terms.meaning: A pure exemplar from the first Light or Life, showing man what he ought to be. The Wisdom-life is that toward which all desire of life tends; it needs nothing of itself but, if stirred, is taken by self-will. It must be born in us repeatedly.

equivalences.quote: The great Salt Sea (Wisdom, the Universal Will)

quotes.text: it is a pure exemplar from the first Light or Life, showing man what he ought to be, and offering to conform him to it

terms.meaning: The individual will: it takes the stirred Wisdom-life, wars with the Universal Will, and as patient has its false forms dissolved.

quotes.text: what takes it is the self-will

terms.meaning: The agent of the Work, at war with the self-will; it destroys the faculties and false forms, then reproduces them transmuted.

equivalences.quote: The great Salt Sea (Wisdom, the Universal Will)

quotes.text: The Universal Will being represented as agent dissolves the false forms in the self-will represented as patient.

terms.meaning: What the whole mystery is: consciousness, now drawn out to sense, thrown backwards and upwards into its First Source.

quotes.text: The whole of this mystery is a translation of the consciousness

terms.meaning: Light extracted through anguish from Life.

equivalences.quote: The Philosophic Matter is an excruciated ens of Light

quotes.text: alight extracted through anguish from Life

terms.meaning: The foundation and only true substance of everything, body included; all is held in potentiality in it. It subsists in one will, then two, exists in the third, then becomes self-assertion.

quotes.text: All in the beginning is Will; it is the foundation of everything, and is everything

terms.meaning: What the spirit, having died to all including its identity, receives as a simple receptacle and magnet.

quotes.text: a simple receptacle and magnet for the Divine Seed

terms.meaning: Not to be spoken by us; if it speaks in us it works its own change.

quotes.text: We have no business whatsoever to speak The Name.

terms.meaning: Found in oneself at one's own center; the pure earth of the air or vegetable life that commences Regeneration; contrasted with the mineral earth of the lower life.

equivalences.quote: you find that which is in the air or the vegetable life, that pure earth which commences the Regeneration

quotes.text: nascitur in aere terra magica; in aethere clarificatur

terms.meaning: The end of Wisdom: a 'so-called' annihilation bringing back into the Nothing before all things.

quotes.text: that so-called annihilation bringing back into the Nothing which is before all things

terms.meaning: The spirit in the blood through which life acts; to be taken up into the will so that new life grows from its death; the Phoenix arises from its ashes.

quotes.text: Out of the ashes of this present sensuous spirit arises the Phoenix.

terms.meaning: Absorbed by reiterative contritions; dissolved by magnetizing.

quotes.text: it dissolved the sensuous medium and opens the consciousness to the Divine life

terms.meaning: The Aurific Light; not explained further here.

equivalences.quote: The Solar Tincture (Tinctura Solaris) is the Aurific Light.

terms.meaning: Kirchberger's term: making visible the invisible spirit; a taking of the infinite Light-nature into bound by hypostatic multiplication of its image.

quotes.text: the making visible the invisible spirit

terms.meaning: A real entity produced by spiritual generation; both objective and subjective, an actuality as well as a theory.

equivalences.quote: it is a real ens of light

quotes.text: The Philosopher’s Stone is a real entity produced by spiritual generation

terms.meaning: The Paradisiacal Life, lived under the Cross; the heart life below the extended arms represents and is it.

equivalences.quote: Living in the Second Principle means living the Paradisiacal Life

terms.meaning: Three centers in man: head (the eye of the Divine, animal rational life), heart (celestial medial vegetable life), lumbar region (inferior mineral life).

quotes.text: There are three microcosmic centers in man

terms.meaning: Obtainable at the focus of any of the three microcosmic centers.

quotes.text: The universal matter is obtainable at the focus of either center.

terms.meaning: Soul and spirit separate from the breathless body, joined to it as by a thread until refixation.

quotes.text: In the Philosophical dissolution of the body, soul and spirit are separate

terms.meaning: What ends the philosophical dissolution.

quotes.text: this continues until the refixation takes place

terms.meaning: The medium through which the Divine Will conducts Light; here our chaotic will in potentiality, basis of microcosmic recreation.

equivalences.quote: the fire here is our chaotic will in potentiality

quotes.text: it is the basis of our microcosmic recreation

terms.meaning: The inner re-creation whose basis is the will as fire.

quotes.text: it is the basis of our microcosmic recreation

terms.meaning: Entry into the work or into another life, obtained from the desire of the lower life opening into the heart life by exstasis.

equivalences.with: Key of the House of David
equivalences.quote: The Key to the Work, or into another life, the Key of the House of David

terms.meaning: The means by which the desire of the lower life opens into the heart life.

quotes.text: opening up into the heart life, or the medial life, or the celestial life, or the vegetable life, by exstasis

terms.meaning: The generative, fallen life whose desire, opened upward, yields the Key.

equivalences.quote: the desire of the lower life, the generative, the fallen life

terms.meaning: The higher life into which the lower opens; 'that which is above', which attracts (whether medial/celestial/vegetable life are synonyms is uncertain: see ambiguities).

equivalences.quote: that which is above (the feminine principle, --- Wisdom, --- the heart life)

quotes.text: the heart life, or the medial life, or the celestial life, or the vegetable life

terms.meaning: That which is above, drawing the self-willed source upward by love; cause of the Fall and, advanced, of restoration; the self-willed source becomes a passive feminine principle.

equivalences.quote: that which is above (the feminine principle, --- Wisdom, --- the heart life)

quotes.text: As the feminine spirit is the cause of the Fall

terms.meaning: The Hermetic art/science; antique, perhaps coeval with the universe; Egypt's 'Sacred Art', of which the Smaragdine Table is the sole surviving Egyptian record; its practical method is given in the Tractatus Aureus; stigmatized as a 'Black Art' possibly from the word Chemia.

terms.meaning: The tradition attributed to Hermes; early, eastern, 'romantic and mystical', recorded in dark and enigmatical monuments, emblems and writings.

terms.meaning: The subject of the inquiry, considered as to its means and principles.

quotes.text: has been likewise stigmatized as a Black Art

terms.meaning: Mentioned only as the topic of an allegory in Vaughan's Lumen de Lumine; not explained here.

terms.meaning: What the one Art is the medium of; not further defined here.

quotes.text: the one Art and medium of vital perfectibility

terms.meaning: The 'protochemistry of Hermes', on which Vaughan grounds his discourse on the nature of man; not explained.

quotes.text: grounded on the protochemistry of Hermes

terms.meaning: Subject of Vaughan's Anima Magia Abscondita, said to ascend and descend; not explained.

quotes.text: the universal spirit of nature, with its strange, abstruse, and miraculous ascent and descent

terms.meaning: The genuine masters of the Art, whose writing deliberately obscures.

quotes.text: the adepts appear to have a directly contrary aim

terms.meaning: Possession of the true key still gives only vestibule access when texts are scrambled.

quotes.text: even to those who had already become possessed of the true key

terms.meaning: Source of the artifices (inversion of order, dispersed repetition) used to hide the truth.

quotes.text: A variety of artifices according to the cabalistic method

terms.meaning: The Hermetic/alchemical art; described as cabalistic, full of mysteries, for the wise, plain in itself but veiled in metaphor.

equivalences.quote: the most commendable art of Alchemy

quotes.text: For is not our art cabalistic
The world is fully as ignorant of the genuine doctrine and Art of Wisdom as were the imposters whomit repudiated

terms.meaning: Said of the art: full of mysteries, not taught openly, not to be understood according to the letter.

quotes.text: For is not our art cabalistic

terms.meaning: What the art teaches; not taught openly.

quotes.text: you, fool, believe we teach the secret of secrets openly

terms.meaning: In Bacon's phrase, the understanding.

equivalences.quote: operate according to the blood; i.e., according to the understanding

terms.meaning: Something with which ignorant montebanks deceived the world; not explained in this chunk.

quotes.text: have with their Whites and Reds deceived almost the whole world

terms.meaning: What literal chemists hoped to 'sublime' with stills and furnaces; Atwood implies lifeless instruments cannot do so. Not otherwise defined here.

quotes.text: in hope by such lifeless instruments to sublime the Spirit of Nature

terms.meaning: What chemists sought to extract with salt, sulfur, mercury and antimony; not defined here.

quotes.text: to extract the Form of gold

terms.meaning: Substances which, with antimony, literal chemists used in failed attempts to extract the Form of gold; not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: by salt, sulfur and mercury, or the three combined with antimony

terms.meaning: Something required before practice, lacked by those who failed; not explained here.

quotes.text: without the true Light or heeding their injunctions

terms.meaning: The understanding that must be properly conceived before experiments are undertaken.

quotes.text: leave off experiments until the ground of wisdom is properly conceived

terms.meaning: The subject of the book; a genuine tradition distinct from the deceits of sophists, not disproved by public disbelief.

quotes.text: the genuine tradition of Hermetic science
are no proofs in philosophy, even if it were without so many witnesses, that the Hermetic mystery is groundless

terms.meaning: The physical change whose possibility rests on a theoretic ground and matter Atwood will investigate next.

quotes.text: the theoretic ground and matter on which the physical possibility of transmutation rests

terms.meaning: Genuine masters of the art, as opposed to pretenders, sophists, montebanks; used of Sendivogius.

quotes.text: the pretenders to the Art were in latter times far more numerous than the true adepts

terms.meaning: The common root substance of all natures, to which bodies can be reduced and from which they can take a new form; the true subject of transmutation.

equivalences.quote: their Universal Subject or first matter
nor does ordinary analysis at all discover this Universal Matter of the adepts

quotes.text: may be reduced into their common basis or mercurial first matter

terms.meaning: The foundation of the Hermetic experiment: both what is transmuted and, once freed in its proper essentiality, what transmutes.

equivalences.quote: their Universal Subject or first matter

quotes.text: this Universal Subject is the alleged foundation of the whole Hermetic experiment

terms.meaning: What underlies a species. Unlike species it is corruptible and can be freed and transferred to another form.

equivalences.quote: the subject-matter of these metals, the radical moisture of which they are uniformly composed

quotes.text: but the Subjects of species rather, since they are corruptible and may be changed

terms.meaning: The substance of which metals are uniformly composed; it can be withdrawn from inferior Forms.

equivalences.quote: the subject-matter of these metals, the radical moisture of which they are uniformly composed

terms.meaning: The homogeneous root substance of all things; its homogeneity is the ground of transmutation.

quotes.text: the homogeneity of the radical substance of things

terms.meaning: Used in a special sense: the specific kind of a thing (lead as lead). Species are indestructible, not liable to corruption and not transmutable.

quotes.text: It is not species that they profess to transmute

terms.meaning: The specifying form of a body. Subject-matter is withdrawn from inferior Forms, and one form is expelled so another can be introduced. Atwood calls it an error that the Form was extracted from metals.

quotes.text: one form being expelled, another may be introduced
the alchemists extracted from the Form out of these metals to transmute and increase with

terms.meaning: In the philosophers' sense, the first matter to which bodies are reduced. It is the root of gold and silver and alone suffices for the work. It is distinguished from 'mercury as mercury specificate', which cannot be changed into gold.

equivalences.quote: reduce the body into water, that is, into mercury
a reduction of the body into water, which is argent vive
when Sol is reduced to his first original, i.e., the mercury
gold and silver are not unlike in kind to this our Mercury; for it is their root

quotes.text: All is in Mercury which the wise men seek
nor do they ever teach in theory that lead as lead, or mercury as mercury specificate, can be changed into gold

terms.voice: QUOTED: Bacon, Rosarium, Geber, Aquinas (endorsed by ATWOOD)

terms.meaning: The first work and foundation of the art: reducing the body into water, i.e. mercury.

quotes.text: this is called Solution, which is the foundation of the whole art

terms.meaning: Said of fusible mineral and metallic bodies once reduced to their beginning; apparently 'turned into mercury' (not glossed).

quotes.text: Mineral and metalline may be mercurizate

terms.meaning: A superior power by whose force the subject-matter is freed. The Ether is described as 'fermenting'. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: being set free by the force of a superior ferment or attraction
the fermented Spirit assimilates the Light throughout

terms.meaning: The only thing that can truly be multiplied; it comes from the first fountain of multiplication and generation. Once perfected by art it exalts any body in its kind, acting on that body's passive principles.

quotes.text: It is the Light only that can be truly multiplied, for this ascends and descends from the first fountain of multiplication and generation

terms.meaning: A notion the adept rejects as one of the impostors' fables.

quotes.text: those imposters who tell you of a sulphur tingens, and I know not what fables

terms.meaning: A name the adept calls too narrow for a science 'ancient and infinite'.

quotes.text: who pin also the narrow name of Chemia on a science ancient and infinite

terms.meaning: The Sages' name for the one universal thing present everywhere. It contains all nature and all Life, is extracted from 'their earth', and is not vulgar salt.

quotes.text: The band of Sages only have known it, And they call it their salt.
Nor the vulgar salt in any manner, But rather the salt of the world

terms.meaning: One single thing; the whole mystery; identified with a spirit and a living water.

equivalences.quote: our Stone is no other than a foetant spirit and living water

quotes.text: The Stone is one

terms.meaning: The philosophers' name for the 'living water' that the Stone is.

equivalences.quote: living water, which we have named dry water

terms.meaning: Made from the salt of the world; one single thing in which the whole mystery consists; preserves from all maladies.

quotes.text: the medicine is one, in which the whole mystery consists
Of it is made that medicine which will preserve you from all maladies

terms.meaning: An all-pervading, perfective essence that regulates nature. It is a distinct, universally diffused substance, sensible only in its mixtures and effects; it is the source and bond of the elements, always ready to act on predisposed subjects, and it gives air its vitalizing power.

equivalences.quote: which he likewise calls ether, and a pure invisible fire

quotes.text: the occult virtues of the Ether; its all-pervading essence and perfective power

terms.voice: ATWOOD; QUOTED: Homberg, Boerhaave, Boyle, Berkeley

terms.meaning: The Ethnics' doctrine, which Atwood says differs from Hebrew doctrine only in words.

quotes.text: the assertions of the Ethnics, about the Anima Mundi, differ very little or nothing in substance from the Hebrew doctrine, but in words only

terms.meaning: The ancient theory of a single vitalizing principle in air and all things. Moderns deride it because it escapes their analyses.

quotes.text: the ancient theory of the One Element has been very much derided

terms.meaning: Nature's source-spirit, distinct from its manifestation and from sensible fire, which is only its excitation or effect.

quotes.text: the fontal Spirit of nature, apart from its manifestation

terms.meaning: Ordinary sensible fire. It is not true fire, only 'an excitation only or effect of the antecedent potency'.

quotes.text: distinct from that elementary ignition with which we are sensibly familiar

terms.meaning: The magi's universal essence, held to be an object of experimental science, obtainable as a compact, tangible, homogeneous essence rather than only mixed in air or water.

equivalences.with: Lumen Vestimenti, the Vehicle of Light
equivalences.quote: in which pure estate, the Kabalists, also describing, call it, Lumen Vestimenti, the Vehicle of Light
and the Greeks, the Free Ether, that is to say, freed from the prison of gross matter

quotes.text: that elder Quintessence of the magi which they introduce, not as a being of speculation merely, but of experimental science

terms.meaning: The essence freed from gross matter, working by its own included light; in Euripides' verse, the all-nourishing Ether embracing the earth.

equivalences.quote: The viewless Ether in his genial arms Clasping the earth; Him call thou Lord and Jove

quotes.text: freed from the prison of gross matter, and able to work of itself intimately by the virtue of its own included light

terms.meaning: A supposed 'New Imponderable' suggested by recent experiments and Mesmerism; few believe in it and Atwood does not assume it here.

equivalences.quote: the supposition of a New Imponderable, or Odic Force

terms.meaning: The sought spirit, which never subsists separately on earth but is hidden and defiled within the beings it sustains.

quotes.text: the ethereal spirit does not subsist of itself, separate or tangibly on earth

terms.meaning: The subject of the Art: a water of another nature (Lully); a stone and no stone, spirit, soul and body, volatile and clear, One Thing (Arnold); the thing in which the conversion of natures is carried out.

equivalences.with: aqua alterius naturae (water of another nature)
equivalences.quote: argentums vivum nostrum est aqua alterius naturae

quotes.text: the method of conversion in our Argent vive is the reduction of natures to their first root
it is a stone and no stone, in which the whole Art consists, spirit, soul and body

terms.meaning: The two states the work inverts: the fixed is to be made volatile and the volatile fixed.

quotes.text: that which is fixed becoming volatile and the volatile nature fixed

terms.meaning: Formula closing the verse on the fixed and volatile; the chunk ties it to the inversion of fixed and volatile.

quotes.text: Solve, Coagula, Fige.

terms.meaning: The externally generated form imposed on a body, to be constricted, versus its inner central form, to be developed into life and act.

quotes.text: the adventitious or externally generated image may be constricted utterly, and the central form contrariwise developed into life and act

terms.meaning: Reversal of nature's ordinary order of procedure, required for perfect manifestation; beyond ordinary art and nature.

quotes.text: by a real experimental inversion
the order of natural procedure ought to be introverted for a true and perfect manifestation

terms.meaning: Making light things heavy and spirits no spirits; a mutation of natures reducing them to their first root.

equivalences.quote: our operation is nothing else than a mutation of natures

quotes.text: let him understand the conversion of the elements, to make light things heavy, and to make spirits no spirits

terms.meaning: Figure for laying hold of and working matter to the utmost degree.

equivalences.with: working upon matter in the extremist degree
equivalences.quote: manacles and fetters; i.e., lays hold and works upon matter in the extremist degree

terms.meaning: In Paracelsus, the natural (not specially divine) secret that gives entrance into nature by unmatched quickness of separation.

quotes.text: if that magic then were natural, certainly it was most wonderful, very excellent for quickness of separation

terms.meaning: The greatest miracle in philosophy and the beginning of all generation; the first half of Ripley's procedure before recombination.

quotes.text: separation was the principle and beginning of all generation

terms.meaning: The matter of the metals, which brings everything into its due form.

equivalences.quote: The truphat, or matter of the metals

terms.meaning: Result of separating the elements of Mercury and recombining them in equal proportion.

quotes.text: again commixed by equal weight or proportion, make the elixir complete

terms.meaning: In Hermetic usage not the common elements or chemical simples, but the elements of the Mercury, properties of the universal spirit; the true element is an invisible spirit of life, the visible being only its receptacle.

equivalences.with: elements of the Mercury, properties of the universal spirit
equivalences.quote: the elements they speak of, as being introverted and transformed are the elements of the Mercury, properties of the universal spirit
the true element is a spirit of life, and grows in all things

quotes.text: We must not limit, says Paracelsus, an element to a bodily substance or quality.

variants: first matter of the elements of the elements
terms.meaning: The invisible, intangible spirit of life in all things; the life creatures have.

equivalences.with: that life which the creatures have
equivalences.quote: the first matter of the elements of the elements is nothing else but that life which the creatures have

quotes.text: This is the First Matter of the elements, which can neither be seen nor felt, and yet is in all things

terms.meaning: The occult being in nature on whose assumption all Hermetic theory and practice proceeds.

quotes.text: the whole of the Hermetic theory and practice proceeds upon the assumption of a certain Universal Being in nature, which is occult

terms.meaning: The perfective product of the Art, made in and by the universal spirit; the permanent water is the stone, though not a stone while still water.

equivalences.quote: this very permanent water is the stone, but whilst it is water it is no stone

quotes.text: the perfective miracle of their Stone

terms.meaning: The subject as found by the masters: a cold, moist watery element, permanent water, unctuous vapour, spirit of body.

equivalences.quote: the mercury of the wise to be a watery element, cold and moist, a permanent water, an unctuous vapor, and the spirit of body
Which Lully, not dissimilarly viewing, calls Hyle

terms.meaning: An unctuous subtle humidity forcibly incorporated with a subtle earthy part.

quotes.text: the first material of the metals is an unctuous subtle humidity, forcibly incorporated with a subtle terrestreity

terms.meaning: Lully's name for the subject: a clear compounded water like argent vive, flowing on earth, generated in every compound from the substance of the air, extremely heavy.

quotes.text: it is a clear compounded water, most like in substance to argent vive

terms.meaning: In the Orphic hymn, the strong subtle whole that is all fire, air, earth or water, beginning and end of all; Atwood then speaks of 'the most Ancient Nature' as 'he', to be taken as the Hermetic masters found it.

quotes.text: Fortis subtilis Pan, integer et generalis; Et totus ignis, aura, terra, sive aqua,
Yet not in his elementary immanifest diffusion let us invoke the most Ancient Nature

terms.meaning: Possessed, with the pure and clear Mercury, by whoever has the vapour of the subject; not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: Has the gilded splendor of the Red Lyon, The pure and clear Mercury.

terms.meaning: Contained in the subject; knowing it gives the whole foundation. Not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: And he who knows the red Sulfur which it contains, Has within his power the whole foundation

terms.meaning: The ancients' art, unknown to Bacon together with its subject.

quotes.text: he knew nothing of their Great Art, or of its subject even, and naturally mistook their hidden ground

terms.meaning: The one indescribable subject of the art: a middle/third substance generated from the Universal Spirit's active and passive relations; the simple substance of life and light flowing unmanifest through nature; not any sensible thing.

equivalences.with: union of masculine and feminine spirits
equivalences.quote: the First Matter is indeed the union of masculine and feminine spirits

quotes.text: the simple generated substance of life and light, immanifestly flowing throughout nature
Thus obscure, after all, is the true Matter of the Alchemists

terms.meaning: Source whose active and passive relations generate the First Matter; in its common estate said to be everywhere in nature.

quotes.text: its generation by active and passive relations of the Universal Spirit
as the Spirit is in nature, said to be everywhere

terms.meaning: The subject as celestial soul drawn out by the work; produces all effects within itself; also a name of the whitened oil stage.

equivalences.quote: the quintessence is no other than our viscous celestial and glorious soul drawn from its minera by our magistery
This Proteus, then, or Mercury, or quintessence of philosophers

quotes.text: which, whitening, is called milk, dew, quintessence

terms.meaning: The ever-changing omniform aspect of the one subject; contained in Pan.

equivalences.quote: This Proteus, then, or Mercury, or quintessence of philosophers

quotes.text: For Pan contains Proteus
Etherial, watery, earthy general soul, Immortal Fire! Even all the world is thine And pars of thee, O Proteus, power divine;

terms.meaning: The subject as one being whose offspring are multitudinous; contains Proteus and evolves all forms from his central will.

quotes.text: so is it said to be with the Alchemical Pan, who, being but one himself, is in his offspring multitudinous

terms.meaning: Name of the subject (Proteus/quintessence) and one of the three principles; 'multiplying the Mercury by its proper Light' is part of the preparation. Common mercury is excluded as the Matter.

equivalences.quote: This Proteus, then, or Mercury, or quintessence of philosophers

quotes.text: multiplying the Mercury by its proper Light

variants: three great magnetic principles of being
terms.meaning: Three principles nature exhibits from the Matter's unity after the annihilate condition, related as agent, patient and offspring; modes of being of one thing.

quotes.text: The three principles, the Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury, are merely different as modes of being of the same thing

terms.meaning: Process out of which the Matter first appears pure and white; not further explained here.

quotes.text: pure, as they say, and white, out of the philosophical contrition

terms.meaning: State into which the artist brings all, pressing out 'the waters of her extreme life', after which nature reacts.

quotes.text: when the wise artist has brought all into this annihilate condition

terms.meaning: The work by which the soul/quintessence is drawn from its minera.

quotes.text: drawn from its minera by our magistery

terms.meaning: That from which the quintessence is drawn; not glossed in this chunk.

quotes.text: drawn from its minera by our magistery

terms.meaning: The Matter as liquid.

equivalences.quote: this Latex is the sharp vinegar which makes gold a pure spirit, seeing she is even that blessed water which engenders al things

terms.meaning: Means by which 'our sea water' is extracted; otherwise unexplained.

equivalences.quote: our chalybs, or steel

terms.meaning: The precious thing, congealed in gold and silver; abiding 'in the sea of the world'.

equivalences.with: a ting more precious than the whole world
equivalences.quote: a ting more precious than the whole world; which I plainly tell thee is nothing else than our sea water

terms.meaning: One of the epithets of the Matter.

equivalences.with: dead head; foeces of our sea
equivalences.quote: O our caput mortuum, or dead head, or foeces of our sea!

terms.meaning: The listed epithets of the Matter (heaven, water, mercury, salt nitre, sulfur, caput mortuum etc.) are said to be its epithets; never at rest.

quotes.text: And these are the Epithetes of Hermes, his Bird, which is never at rest.

terms.meaning: Name for the Matter as latent in and about all; celebrated by 'the Enigma'. Not further explained.

quotes.text: the alone Laelia Aelia latent in and about all, which the Enigma celebrates as comprehending all

terms.meaning: The Matter as subject of the work, with virtue and perfective properties beyond ordinary light phenomena; universal, so every epithet fits it.

quotes.text: the alleged virtue and perfective properties of the Philosophic Subject
inasmuch as nothing can be said amiss of a Universal Subjet

terms.meaning: The subject when it is 'nothing', a formless potential state amid its mutations.

equivalences.quote: but a potential chaos and egg of philosophers

terms.meaning: The artificial process of the subject's progress to perfection; the 'fermental principle of the spirit' is denoted by liquid analogies.

quotes.text: In its artificial fermentation and progress towards perfection
the fermental principle of the spirit and her distilled quintessence

terms.meaning: Name, with serpent and dragon, of the matter when first sublimed, for its strength and crude vitality.

quotes.text: it is called a serpent, dragon, or green lion, on account of its strength and crude vitality

terms.meaning: Name of the putrefying stage, a stronger poison.

quotes.text: which putrefying, becomes a stronger poison, and their venomous toad

terms.meaning: Name of the matter calcined by its proper fire.

equivalences.quote: is called magnesia and lead of the wise

terms.meaning: Name of the dissolving stage.

equivalences.quote: becomes their vitriolic solvent and most sharp acetum

terms.meaning: The final perfection of the matter.

equivalences.quote: it is henceforth a phoenix, salamander, their royal essence and Red Stone

terms.meaning: One of the forms the subject takes in its changes; not further explained in this chunk.

quotes.text: a stone, a vapor, or an aqua sicca

terms.meaning: The philosophers' water: not common water but the ethereal body of life and light, altered by art and corporified; heavenly, not wetting the hands.

equivalences.with: ethereal body of life and light
equivalences.quote: it is the ethereal body of life and light which they profess to have discovered

quotes.text: a certain tortured water, having suffered alteration by art and becomes corporified

terms.meaning: The one being whose magnetic relation, action and passion the authors mean by sulfur, mercury, earth, twofold or third matter.

quotes.text: the magnetic relation, action, and passion of the Ethereal being in itself

terms.meaning: Name in the verse for the privy quintessence, with Azot, Basiliske, Adrop, Cockatrice, Eagle, Toade.

quotes.text: Our great Elixir most high of price, Our Azot, our Basiliske, and our Adrop, our Cockatrice.

terms.meaning: The product of the Art: the purified, concentrated Ether of nature, perfected by its own Light; in its fermented, crystalline perfection called the Stone; it transmutes by assimilating crude life into its own light.

equivalences.quote: their stone is nothing more or less than the pure Ethereality of nature
this fermented Spirit or Stone, (as in the crystalline perfectness of its essence it has been called,)

equivalences.with: Stone of Fire / seed of gold
equivalences.quote: the seed of gold, says the adept, is a fiery form of Light inspissate, and this is the Stone of Fire

quotes.text: Lapis noster, hic est ignis, ex igne creatus

terms.meaning: The forming, fermenting agent that perfects the Ether; the Form the matter lacks; source of central heat; self-multiplying.

equivalences.quote: This Form is Light, the source of central heat
Light is the true fermental principle which perfects the Ether in its proper kind

quotes.text: the universal magnet of its own infinite self-multiplicative Light

terms.meaning: The subtle material of nature which, separated and purified, is the matter of the Stone, and in which the Formal Light multiplies.

quotes.text: the Formal Light, by multiplication in its Ethe, is said to produce gold

terms.meaning: The inward agent that matter lacks and that, joined to matter, begets a seed; also the diverse specific shapes the one material assumes.

equivalences.quote: This Form is Light
her forms or sulfurs are perplexed

quotes.text: This agent is the form that matter wanted
though the material is one throughout, forms are diverse

terms.meaning: What Form (Light) clothed with matter begets; it impresses its character on matter. Metals arise from metalline seeds out of the Universal Spirit; vulgar gold lacks seed until art helps it.

equivalences.quote: the seed of gold, says the adept, is a fiery form of Light inspissate, and this is the Stone of Fire

quotes.text: Which clothed with mater doth a seed beget.

terms.meaning: A thing's own agent of change that converts it into a different nature without anything foreign added; in the Art, the Spirit's own prepared leaven, by which it is raised and gains virtue.

quotes.text: by its won prepared must or leaven
in proportion to the virtue which it has acquired in the fermentation

terms.meaning: The spirit that alchemy promotes from one form of being into another by its own leaven, passing through many stages to perfection.

quotes.text: Just so is the Vital Spirit said to be, by the art of Alchemy, promoted from one form of being into another

terms.meaning: The common source of metals and all things, from which metalline seeds come; the only means of growth, transmutation and increase.

equivalences.quote: from metalline seeds out of the Universal Spirit or Mercury

quotes.text: without this spirit growth is impossible, or transmutation or increase

terms.meaning: Not found of itself on earth; cannot be held or perfected without the Art.

equivalences.quote: the Universal Spirit or Mercury

quotes.text: the Mercury of the philosophers is not found of itself on earth

terms.meaning: The operation that obtains the right recipient, separates pure from impure and subtle from gross, and makes agent and patient one.

quotes.text: by the Hermetic dissolution the right recipient is said to be obtained

terms.meaning: The active and receptive principles, which after Hermetic dissolution are one identity.

quotes.text: the agent and the patient are one identity

terms.meaning: Nature's receptive spirit, in ordinary state enclosed and impure; made a right recipient by dissolution.

quotes.text: the passive spirit of nature is included and impure

terms.meaning: Attraction of crude life away from other forms into coalescence with the Stone's own light.

quotes.text: transmutes, i.e., attracts the same away from other forms into intimate coalescence with its own assimilative light

terms.meaning: Something in the Art whose will, unlike natural species, is free to form itself about its own self-multiplicative Light; context ties it to the fermented Vital Spirit, but the chunk does not define it.

quotes.text: the will of the philosophic Proteus is free to be drawn without hindrance

terms.meaning: The one uniform substance in nature that is the material basis of Hermetic philosophy and sole principle of transmutation, life, increase and perfection.

quotes.text: the existence of a Homogeneal Subject in nature

terms.meaning: The gross earthy part of metals that overcomes their spirit and must be purged away.

quotes.text: unless they be first purged from their terrestreity

terms.meaning: Something in metals that must be set free in the subtle Origin of all life before they can fructify; not further defined here.

quotes.text: their tincture set free in the subtle Origin of all life

terms.meaning: Product of the work, whose divine virtues wise men admire; things altered by the pure mineral spirit come to equal it. (¶46 separately names 'the elixir of the wise' as the result of superior skill and coction in vegetal life; the chunk does not assert the two are identical.)

quotes.text: the Philosophical Elixir, whose divine virtues wise men so much admire

terms.meaning: The metallic root, which appears first in the experimental process and is most easily apportioned.

quotes.text: the metalline radix first presents itself in the experimental process

terms.meaning: A cooking/maturing operation; with superior skill it yields the elixir in vegetal life. Not defined in this chunk.

quotes.text: through superior skill and coction in the vegetal life

terms.meaning: That to which bodies must be reduced, by introversion of the generated life, for true manifestation and permanence.

quotes.text: the reduction of bodies to their original matter, by introversion of the generated life

terms.meaning: In the Emerald Table, that from which all the rest proceed by adaptation; the unitary basis of production.

quotes.text: the miracles of the One Thing whence all the rest proceed by adaptation

terms.meaning: Its properties are hidden in all existence, understood only by its own inner analysis and 'introverted light'. The 'central experience' within it cannot be found without God.

quotes.text: the properties of the Universal Spirit are abstrusely included in all existence

terms.meaning: To be understood spiritually rather than bodily: the four parts or 'hypostatic relations' of the philosophic water.

equivalences.with: four parts or hypostatic relations of the philosophic water
equivalences.quote: The philosophic water then, being divided into four parts or hypostatic relations, they are called elements

quotes.text: not corporally but spiritually and wisely

terms.meaning: The one water from which everything grows and into which it dissolves again. It is divided into four relations and contains its own sulfur.

equivalences.quote: this water or mercury of the adepts has, within itself, its own good sulfur

quotes.text: which have their growth all from the same identical water, and are resolved into the same again

terms.meaning: The active principle inside the philosophic water. Tripling it is part of the operator's 'weights'.

equivalences.quote: its own good sulfur, or vital flame

quotes.text: to double mercury and triple sulfur

terms.meaning: The true philosophic proportions of the work. Hermes says they are the two-thirds part of the divided Water.

equivalences.quote: the true philosophic proportions called also by Hermes the Weights of the Wise

quotes.text: the two third waters are the Weights of the Wise

terms.meaning: The stages of colour the work must pass through. In Hermes' division of the Water, 'colour' is one third part, a coagulating moisture. The Scholiast says Hermes divides the colours into three red spirits and three white.

equivalences.quote: the one third part of which is colour, that is to say --- a coagulating moisture

quotes.text: into three red spirits and three white, which have their growth all from the same identical water
