terms.meaning: The object of the inward search, whose true method and conditions are sought from the ancients; a true, catholic psychical experience, not trance or vision.

equivalences.quote: For it is this, no common trance or day-dream, or any fanatical vision of celestials, that we propose to scrutinize, but the true psychical experience

quotes.text: the true method and conditions of Self- Knowledge

terms.meaning: What is discovered by inquiring into the substance and practical evolution of the psychical experience.

quotes.text: It is into the substantiality of this and for its practical evolution that we must inquire, if we would discover the true Light of Alchemy

terms.meaning: What the alchemical reduction of nature uncovers without destroying nature's vehicle; not defined in this chunk.

quotes.text: such a reducation of nature as shall discover this Latex without destroying her vehicle, but the modal life only

terms.meaning: The part of nature that the reduction destroys, as opposed to her vehicle; apparently her 'superfluous forms'.

quotes.text: where nature may be addressed in order to the rejection of her superfluous forms

terms.meaning: In ¶47, what in nature is preserved during the reduction; in ¶51, the vehicle of the soul, strengthened by material Rites.

quotes.text: there is no other means of strengthening the vehicle of the sold but by material Rites

terms.meaning: The force the alchemists claim man has developed into action by rational conditioning.

quotes.text: man, by rationally conditionating, has succeeded in developing into action the Recreative Force

terms.meaning: The direct operative cause of the work, concealed by the alchemists. ¶52 also speaks of a 'central efficient' produced into conscious being by arts and media; the text does not assert the two are identical.

quotes.text: what was their immediate efficient?
producing the central efficient into conscious being and effect

terms.meaning: A dissolution 'according to the course of nature' whose ignorance made men think gold-making impossible.

quotes.text: the artificial destruction according to the course of nature

terms.meaning: The truth of causes, as opposed to remote effects; drawn from a deep well.

quotes.text: who have never glanced even in imagination toward the Causal Truth

terms.meaning: The deep experience of things reached by ascending in thought and then descending.

quotes.text: hope to penetrate so far as to the superstantial experience of things

terms.meaning: Hidden, imprisoned light separated from understanding by the senses' outward attraction.

equivalences.quote: the true light shut up as in a prison, the fountain of Universal Nature

terms.meaning: The only means of strengthening the soul's vehicle; perfecting the soul by the power of materials on earth.

quotes.text: To initiate or perfect the human soul by the power of materials here on earth

terms.meaning: The magic of Zoroaster, whose use is to perfect the soul by the power of materials.

equivalences.quote: calls the magic of Zoroaster the service of the gods

terms.meaning: Assistance without which the Divine union is neither effected nor understood.

quotes.text: bears witness to the efficacy of Divine Works

terms.meaning: The goal effected only with the assistance of Divine Works.

quotes.text: without such assistance the Divine union is neither effected not rightly understood

terms.meaning: Means given (by Jupiter, per the Platonic Successor) for communication with the gods after spontaneous revelation ceased.

quotes.text: has given us observation through Sacred Arts, by which we have at hand sufficient assistance

terms.meaning: Those who knew the means of the Art and kept silent on them.

quotes.text: that the Initiated were so profoundly silent upon these means

terms.meaning: Recovery of what the soul forgot in embodied life; also the recovery of the ancient experiment; felt by souls allied to antecedent realities.

quotes.text: thrilling into reminiscence, as of some long past life forgotten
will recollect all those things, the remembrance of which she loses in the present life

terms.meaning: The Egyptian art of divine works, known to the Greeks as Theurgy and practised in the Mysteries.

equivalences.quote: Now the Egyptians, that is the Hermetic Art, or Art of Divine works, was by the Greeks called Theurgy
the Hermetic Art, or Art of Divine works

quotes.text: the Greeks were not ignorant of the Hermetic Art

terms.meaning: Greek name for the Hermetic Art; the practice of the Mysteries by which Theurgists partook of the Wisdom of true Being through divinely potent arts.

equivalences.quote: Now the Egyptians, that is the Hermetic Art, or Art of Divine works, was by the Greeks called Theurgy

quotes.text: through their Theurgic disciplines
The Neoplatonists wrote largely of the Theurgical art

terms.meaning: The ancients' art practised in the Mysteries, compared with Mesmerism.

quotes.text: if we connect it with the ancients’ Sacred Art

terms.meaning: The initiatory rites (Ethnic and Christian) whose object was Ontological Wisdom and which really procured it; they held a secret distinct from ordinary worship.

quotes.text: There was undoubtedly a secret, hanging about these celebrations, both Ethnic and Christian

terms.meaning: The higher grade of initiation, to which alone assimilation and final contact with the first principle were promised; their doctrine related to the whole universe.

quotes.text: to those who were initiated in the Greater Mysteries only
The doctrine of the Greater Mysteries, says Clemens Alexandrinus, related to the whole universe

terms.meaning: The first grade, in which, it appears, the revelations of the natural spirit's first sphere were passed.

quotes.text: passing these, as it appears, in the Lesser Mysteries

terms.meaning: Name for the Mysteries, as the beginning of a life of reason and virtue.

quotes.text: they were truly called Initia, for they were the beginning of a life of reason and virtue

terms.meaning: Philosophy in the true sense: the knowledge of Being that was the object of initiation.

equivalences.quote: philosophy, that is to say, Ontological Wisdom

quotes.text: the Wisdom of true Being

terms.meaning: Heraclitus' name for the theurgic media, as remedies of imperfect souls; they also healed the body.

quotes.text: Heraclitus calls these medicines, as being the help and remedy of imperfect souls

terms.meaning: Cleansing of the soul, the function of the Bacchic rites and a chief benefit of the Mysteries.

quotes.text: the sacred rites of Bacchus pertained to the purification of souls
moral enlightenment and purification of life

terms.meaning: Purificatory rites of the Mysteries by which the soul is liberated into a divine condition.

quotes.text: by the lustrations in the Mysteries, as they describe, the soul becomes liberated and passes into a divine condition of being

terms.meaning: In Clemens, the Lord himself, who seals and illuminates the adept; not otherwise defined here.

quotes.text: it is the Lord himself who is the hierophant

terms.meaning: The initiate whom the Lord illuminates and seals.

quotes.text: he sets his seal upon the adept whom he illuminates with his beams

terms.meaning: The final stage of the church's mysteries, kept most secret; not further explained here.

quotes.text: especially those that relate to the final apotheosis

terms.meaning: The rites or celebrations of the Mysteries.

quotes.text: These are the orgies of the Mysteries

terms.meaning: The modern discovery producing Trance and healing effects; names for an unknown agency.

equivalences.quote: Animal Magnetism, or Mesmerism, or Vital Magnetism, or by whatever other term the unknown agency is better expressed
Animal Magnetism, or Mesmerism, or Vital Magnetism

quotes.text: the unknown agency

terms.meaning: The mesmeric state, suggested by some writers as revealing the temple mysteries; Atwood treats it as a key not yet carried beyond therapy.

quotes.text: suggest their Trance and its phenomena as a revelation of the temple mysteries

terms.meaning: One of the ordinary mesmeric phenomena, with prevision and community of sense, will and thought.

quotes.text: The ordinary phenomena of lucidity, prevision, community of sense, will, and thought

terms.meaning: The medium at work in mesmerism, which can be improved, ascend or descend, and has a right determination; mesmerists take it as it naturally presents; the ancients dissolved it further.

quotes.text: as respects the Universal Medium, they even, who believe in such a thing, take it as it presents itself naturally
to dissolve the medium more entirely

terms.meaning: What mesmeric tests have identified as the same throughout; not further defined here.

quotes.text: prove nothing but to identify the same Imponderable through all

terms.meaning: The cause of mesmerism's own effects, which mesmerism has not investigated.

quotes.text: the subject-being, the cause of its own effects

terms.meaning: The spirit in its natural state, degraded and incapable of true intelligence; diseased, falsifying and dulled until clarified.

quotes.text: condemn the Spirit of the natural life as degraded and incapable of true intelligence
in what the disease of the Spirit consists

terms.meaning: The spirit to be separated from defilements and sense-impressions implanted by birth into sense.

quotes.text: to segregate the Vital Spirit away from those defilements and imaginative impressures

terms.meaning: Imaginative impressions implanted in the Vital Spirit by birth into sense, obscuring intelligence.

quotes.text: imaginative impressures which, by the birth into sense, had become implanted there

terms.meaning: Inner faculty of perception which, purified and strengthened, perceives the truth of all beings.

quotes.text: that divine eye which, as Plato says, is better worth than 10,000 corporeal eyes

terms.meaning: One of the goods promised to initiates of the higher Mysteries.

quotes.text: the Self-Knowledge and perfection of life and immortality promised

terms.meaning: Used in contrast to Christian ('both Ethnic and Christian'); not further defined here.

quotes.text: both Ethnic and Christian

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the intermediate nature between rational and brutal life, corporeal and incorporeal, joining divine natures with the lowest. It is phantastic before purification by art.

equivalences.quote: the phantastical condition also of the natural understanding essence, before it is purified by art and exalted. This Etherial Spirit

quotes.text: it is the medium which conjoins divine natures with the lowest of all

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the imaginative spirit in man and animals. Unpurified, it produces a 'phantastic life', confusion and possession of the mind, and it is likened to the Sphinx. It can be purified ('mundified').

equivalences.quote: Thus Iamblicus, speaking of this mundane spirit, says

quotes.text: such is said to be the nature of the Phantastic Spirit before it is mundified
But the phantastic Spirit may be purified, even in brutes

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the medium of the mind ('primary and proper vehicle of the mind'). It is clear-seeing when the mind is purified and terrene when the mind is sensual. Unpurified, it 'disports herself' in many forms.

quotes.text: the primary and proper vehicle of the mind, when it is in a wise and purified condition, is attenuated and clear seeing
our vehicle disports herself oftentimes in many mingling forms

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the higher spirit that can 'superinduce Divinity' once false imagination is destroyed, and that rises above nature's dominion at the end of the trials.

quotes.text: before the understanding spirit can superinduce Divinity
till the Understanding Spirit rises superior to the dominion of nature

terms.meaning: In this chunk, imagination considered as an impediment to intellectual conception and as contrary to enthusiasm.

quotes.text: The phantasy, says he, is an impediment to our intellectual conception

terms.meaning: In this chunk, what remains of sense impressions even in trance. It must be destroyed before the understanding spirit can receive Divinity.

quotes.text: a false imagination, which it is requisite to destroy

terms.meaning: In this chunk, residual impressions, from the senses or from 'this life's birth and sphere of accidents', that cloud the spirit.

quotes.text: their impressure yet remains
err amongst the turbulent and shadowy impressures of this of this life’s birth and sphere of accidents

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the state of being agitated by the inspiring influence of divinity. It is contrary to the phantasy.

quotes.text: when we are agitated by the inspiring influence of divinity, and the phantasy intervenes, the enthusiastic energy ceases

terms.meaning: In this chunk, universal concepts. Perceiving them proves the soul can act without phantasy, and they promise a higher reality and help introduce the Idea of Wisdom.

quotes.text: they reveal in us a necessity of Being beyond present experience

terms.meaning: In this chunk, a consummate state in which passive reason receives 'the substance of her Whole'. It is intuitive Intellect without imaginative error, not worldly, reached by a gradual transition through Art.

equivalences.with: Intellect diving intuitively without imaginative error
equivalences.quote: Plato appropriates the possession of Wisdom to old age, signifying by this Intellect diving intuitively without imaginative error

quotes.text: a Wisdom such as is not worldly, since it by no means belongs to the common life of man

terms.meaning: In this chunk, rites directed to the experience of truth, ordered by fixed intellectual canons.

quotes.text: Theurgic rites conspiring to this end were scientifically disposed and early defined by intellectual canons

terms.meaning: In this chunk, ignorance that does not know it is ignorant and so has no desire to emerge.

quotes.text: which being ignorant that it is ignorant has no desire to emerge

terms.meaning: In this chunk, purification of the soul. Will is its greatest part.

quotes.text: Will is the greatest part of purgation

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the soul's consent to its purification. Without it the soul has no 'purifying machine'.

quotes.text: the soul is deprived of every purifying machine because destitute of assent, which is the greatest pledge of reconciliation

terms.meaning: In this chunk, admission into the deeper mysteries. Restoration of the soul is obtained by a few 'as a gift of divinity and initiation', and the uninitiated are surrounded by 'dense thickets'.

quotes.text: those who have not been purely initiated

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the real being or substance of oneself, which cannot be discerned by self-contemplation with an unpurified spirit.

quotes.text: we shall not there discern the true hypostasis

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the field whose 'upper grades' are aspired to through labours and dangers.

quotes.text: those who aspire to the upper grades of Intellectual Science

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the depth into which the Spirit sinks when it grows heavy, through downward will or evil agencies.

quotes.text: the Spirit grows heavy and sinks into profound Hades

terms.meaning: In this chunk, named alongside 'our individual reason' as what the spirit 'becomes perfectly everything from which' these consist. Not further defined.

quotes.text: becomes perfectly everything from which dianoia and our individual reason consist

terms.meaning: In this chunk, glossed as 'comprehend'. Solution is also what the impure perceptive medium needs, and 'perfect solution' is the first rule of the work.

equivalences.quote: solve, that is comprehend, it on its own ground

quotes.text: it needs alternation and solution, as the oracles teach
The first rule of the work is a perfect solution

terms.meaning: In this chunk, purified (said of the Phantastic Spirit).

quotes.text: the Phantastic Spirit before it is mundified

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the alchemists' Matter as first known: full of heterogeneous qualities and notions, fallen from its sphere and defiled, needing preparations, solutions and calcinations.

quotes.text: full of heterogeneous qualities and notions, as a subject fallen from its sphere and defiled

terms.meaning: In this chunk, what the vulgar Matter becomes after preparation: pure, agile, intelligent, living, in her own sphere.

quotes.text: the Mercury of the Philosophers --- pure, agile, intelligent, living --- as they say, in her own sphere, as a queen upon her throne

terms.meaning: In this chunk, the 'occult Arcanum', identified with 'our brass', to be washed until pure.

equivalences.quote: the occult Arcanum, which is our brass

quotes.text: Take, says Albertus Mangus, the occult Arcanum, which is our brass, and wash it that it may be pure and clean

terms.meaning: In this chunk, one of the preparations the vulgar Matter undergoes before it becomes the Mercury of the Philosophers. Not further defined.

quotes.text: Hence all those preparations, solutions, calcinations, etc.

terms.meaning: The universal Spirit as it is first consciously revealed in the receptive life of humanity. It can receive and be converted to anything.

equivalences.quote: which Aristotle, in his Metaphysics, calls passive intellect

quotes.text: the universal Mundane Spirit, as it is at first consciously revealed in the recipient life of humanity

terms.meaning: Aristotle's term, as Atwood reports it: an intellect capable of receiving and being converted to all things.

quotes.text: calls passive intellect, because capable of receiving and being converted to all

terms.meaning: The agent at work in mesmerism and the Alchemists' subject-matter. It is indifferent, present everywhere and converted to every will.

equivalences.with: the agent of present-day mesmerizing / photogenic medium / New Imponderable
equivalences.quote: the identical agent which is spread abroad in the present day mesmerizing, the photogenic medium, our New Imponderable, for it is the Common Soul
also the subject-matter of the Alchemists aforesaid

quotes.text: a thing indifferent, abject, and exposed in all hands

terms.meaning: Atwood's name for the agent of mesmerism, which she identifies with the Common Soul.

equivalences.quote: our New Imponderable, for it is the Common Soul

quotes.text: the object was different and immeasurably superior to those proposed by modern Mesmerism

quotes.text: and hath the medium, will be richer than any other
the medium of that holy and sublime experience

quotes.text: the microcosmic life is not dissimilar from the vitality of the greater world

terms.meaning: Improvement. The natural life needs it, and the 'principles of melioration' are required in the operator.

quotes.text: how much such a life is in need of melioration
wanting the very principles of melioration in themselves

terms.meaning: The subject seen as one essence that contains everything yet is separated in each particular. It is the ground of the magians' elements.

equivalences.quote: This is the Monster and the Eternal Riddle explained to common sense as suits it, but misunderstood to this day; that Compound Simple
that Compound Simple and ground of the magians’ elements

quotes.text: an essence all comprehending, yet separated in each particular, by so great an interval from itself

terms.meaning: Something whose 'revealment' comes, in the order of the Mysteries, just before the Purificative Rites. The chunk does not define it explicitly (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: which were designed also to restore the monarchy of reason in the soul

quotes.text: the Hermetic purifications and Mysteries, celebrated in the Eastern temples and by the priests at Eleusis, were real and efficacious

terms.meaning: Named in an objection: why, if true Being is everywhere present, partaking things do not enjoy the light of this 'so-called' world. The chunk does not define it.

quotes.text: the light of the so-called superstantial world

terms.meaning: The life prior to and underlying outward experience. Experience might reveal it if the outward-looking faculty were turned inward and impediments removed.

quotes.text: experience might then reveal to us the antecedent life

terms.meaning: The imaginative region of notions and instincts. Its contents are often more false, fleeting and evil than sense images, and it is dangerous to dwell in passively.

quotes.text: the region of the phantasy, with its notions and instincts

terms.meaning: The human understanding, considered as an essence to be purified. It has an 'occult Causality' that can be developed to consciousness.

quotes.text: purifying the human Understanding Essence, and developing to consciousness its occult Causality

terms.meaning: What the ancients began by purifying, 'in its proper Light'.

quotes.text: purifying the Vital Spirit in its proper Light

terms.meaning: What the same principle becomes when it is solved, resolved and wisely manipulated.

quotes.text: solved and resolved, and wisely manipulated, becomes to be the concrete Stone of philosophers

terms.meaning: That into which the 'least' thing is to be drawn by artifice. The chunk does not define it.

quotes.text: draw it by artifice into the true ferment of philosophers

terms.meaning: A middle substance that is passive, undetermined and convertible to all extremes. That is why it can be perfected by art.

quotes.text: this Universal Spirit is described as a middle substance --- passive, undetermined, susceptible of conversion and all extremes

terms.meaning: The agent and patient aspects of the one self-purifying subject. Fully advanced, they are the Sun and Moon philosophical.

equivalences.quote: in turn agent and patient, which are the Hermetic luminaries
which are the Hermetic luminaries; in their full representative advancement, the Sun and Moon philosophical

terms.meaning: The true work, within which the luminaries pass through phases from imperfection to perfection.

quotes.text: passing through many phases from imperfection to perfection in the true magistery

terms.meaning: The subject of the hermetic art, referred to as 'her'. The art takes it where nature leaves it and disposes and manipulates it.

quotes.text: the right disposition and manipulation of this our Undetermined Subject

terms.meaning: The new, concentric form in which the subject is established through sublimation at the end of the operations.

quotes.text: establishing her in a new and concentric Form of Light

terms.meaning: Something 'rejected' that regains 'her Head place' only after the labors of the Heroic Intellect. The chunk does not decode it.

quotes.text: before the rejected Keystone regains her Head place

terms.meaning: The intellect whose long labors must be passed through before the work is complete.

quotes.text: all the labors of that Heroic Intellect to be passed through

terms.meaning: The hermetic art: the right disposition and manipulation of the Undetermined Subject through stated operations. Knowing it, with its expressions and the medium, brings the greatest riches.

quotes.text: he that knows the Art, and the expressions, and hath the medium

terms.meaning: The first, popular initiation open to all, revealing only the internal life; a field of natural contemplation without rule.

quotes.text: this was the only popular initiation open to all

terms.meaning: Rites after which the inclination is freed from the dominion of sense; prerequisite for the deeper mysteries.

quotes.text: the inclination being already freed from the dominion and all the superficial progeny of sense

terms.meaning: The spirit released in trance, which can range its sphere, reveal hidden things and philosophize, but whose freedom does not guarantee truth.

quotes.text: the intrinsic intelligence and power of the Free Spirit which can expatiate into the whole circumference of its sphere and reveal hidden things

terms.meaning: The art whose object is to concentrate vitality, turn the spiritual eye, purify and analyze the total essence, and draw forth and know the true Efficient.

quotes.text: this was their object and the Art of Theurgy

terms.meaning: The true active cause within the total essence, to be drawn forth and known in co-identity.

quotes.text: draw forth the true Efficient and to know it in co-identity

terms.meaning: The medium of sense-consciousness that trance dissolves; consciousness is later translated beneath it.

quotes.text: dissolve the sensible medium and convert it to the experience of another life

terms.meaning: Term adopted from the old doctrine for the change in the vital relationship in trance; the Alchemists say the sensible medium ought to be dissolved; perfect solution is the beginning of the work.

quotes.text: We adopt the term dissolve here in accordance with the old doctrine

terms.meaning: The goal towards which consciousness is translated beneath the sensible medium by obscuration.

quotes.text: to translate the consciousness underneath this medium by obscuration, towards the Central Source

terms.meaning: Not the corporeal nature or fleshly existence, but a state of vital submersion in the Mysteries, consciousness drawn about the penetralia of its first life.

equivalences.quote: by Hades, or that profound Lethe

quotes.text: a state of vital submersion in the Mysteries, when the consciousness is artificially drawn about the penetralia of its first life

terms.meaning: Required propitiation for the descent; literally part of the sacred equipage; read ontologically as a ray of living light, the intellect.

equivalences.quote: a ray of living light, golden and flexible, the true Brancha Spiritualis of Raymond Lully

quotes.text: connected with the Mercurial caduceus

terms.meaning: The intellect's congenial life: our lapsed soul hidden in her dark hypostasis.

equivalences.quote: its own congenial life, which is Proserpine, and that lapsed soul of ours, seated in her dark hypostasis unknown

terms.meaning: A murky enveloping medium through whose circumference the intellect penetrates to the lapsed soul; not further explained.

quotes.text: the murky circumference of the chloric ether

terms.meaning: Linked to the middle region out of which consciousness passes, clear and rational, into the Fire World; not defined here.

quotes.text: clear and rational from out the Aquaster, enters the Fire World

terms.meaning: The region consciousness enters after the middle region, at the dark descent; not defined here.

quotes.text: enters the Fire World

terms.meaning: Name of the cave-place of descent; read as the heavy, inelastic nether air verging on the chaos of matter.

quotes.text: destitute of elasticity, Aornus, heavy like that of an enclosed cave, and vast

terms.meaning: The adepts' name for the dark nether region and the apparent corruption preceding mystical death and regeneration.

equivalences.quote: as describing the same ens, they call it lapis niger, vilis, foetens
Sendivogius calls it Urinus Saturni

quotes.text: It is the Black Saturn of the adepts, and that appearing corruption that precedes the mystical death and regeneration into new life

terms.meaning: Called by the Alchemists their mineral tree, with allusion to the dark matter of the descent.

equivalences.quote: the Alchemists also call the Ether their mineral tree

terms.meaning: The original life whose penetralia consciousness is drawn about in Hades, and from whose perpetual motion the nether darkness flows.

quotes.text: flowing out from the perpetual motion of the first life

terms.meaning: Whose dark dominion is dissolved by the magnetic friction of its proper light.

quotes.text: the dark dominion of the selfhood

terms.meaning: The light reached after passing through the dark region; the object of inquiry.

quotes.text: before inquiry can hope to meet its object in the Elysian light

terms.meaning: That which Intellect seeks in the allegory of the descent.

quotes.text: an inquiry of Intellect after its Paternal Source

terms.meaning: The first of two kinds of apparition in the Chaldaic rites: a mere apparition, for example of light in some form, seen by the celebrant. It is not to be heeded.

quotes.text: the first called superinspection, when he who celebrates the divine rites sees a mere apparition

terms.meaning: The faculty that makes the apparitions, as in dreams but more intensely.

quotes.text: For it is the imaginative spirit which is the maker of these images

terms.meaning: The soul's subtle vehicle. When humid and condensed it presents apparitions to the inner sense, and the soul looking outward sees its shadow and images.

quotes.text: our pneumatic vehicle, becoming humid and condensed beneath her heaven
beholds the shadow and images of her vaporous vehicle

terms.meaning: A connection by which the person in this state meets the whole image-world of his sphere. The change to a spiritual body happens 'by rapport divine'.

quotes.text: each by rapport in this state becomes conversant with the whole phantasmagoric universe of his sphere
is changed from an earthly to a spiritual body, by rapport divine

terms.meaning: Apparitional beings arising from the enclosed vapor of imagination. They are called progeny of matter and are said to have sense, arts and an operative life, which they use to deceive. They are vivified by desire and are at war with the truth-seeking soul. The Chaldaic oracle also speaks of 'pure demons'.

quotes.text: all the race of demons, so much celebrated by antiquity, appear to have their origin in a life of this kind, viz., from an included vapor of the imagination
as the progeny of matter, and as having an energetic virtue, but at natural war with the truth-seeking soul

terms.meaning: The term is used once, in connection with the material images seen during the evaporative purification. Its referent is unclear (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: And that such actually appeared to be the Musai, during the evaporative process of purification

terms.meaning: Contemplation in which, according to Proclus, the same order holds as in the Mysteries: phantasms first, illumination later.

quotes.text: the same method takes place in the speculation of Wholes

terms.meaning: The dark, image-loving lower world, and the aerial moisture of life in its unpurified state. In it, consciousness wrapped by the Mysteries is anxious and perplexed.

equivalences.quote: is that Hades we are treating of, the Purgatory of the wise

equivalences.with: aerial moisture in its native (unpurified) state
equivalences.quote: which moisture in its native state, before it is purified by the inflowing light of reason, is that Hades we are treating of

quotes.text: Hades dark all over, squalid, delighting in images, unintelligible, precipitous

terms.meaning: The state of a soul that has left nature and its moisture. It turns to itself and radiates its own light. Heraclitus calls it the wisest.

quotes.text: then she becomes a dry splendor from exhalation
a dry soul is the wisest

terms.meaning: In the sage's saying, the earth means our chaotic sense-life, not soil.

equivalences.with: our dark divulsed chaotic life from sense
equivalences.quote: not the feculent dead soil, but our dark divulsed chaotic life from sense

quotes.text: Visit the interior of the earth rectifying

terms.meaning: Hidden in the interior of the 'earth'. It is generated with light and brings forth clouds and darkness.

equivalences.quote: thou shalt find the hidden Stone, the true medicine

quotes.text: Our Stone comes with light and with light it is generated

terms.meaning: The incombustible moisture in which the thick fire of life is imprisoned. Unpurified, it is Hades.

quotes.text: a thick fire imprisoned in a certain incombustible aerial moisture

terms.meaning: What the consciousness in Hades is taught to aspire to but cannot find by itself through the darkness.

quotes.text: that Hypostatic Reality towards which it is instructed evermore to aspire

terms.meaning: The inner 'secret chamber' that horrors and phantoms guard.

quotes.text: guarding the secret chamber of their mineral soul

terms.meaning: Never seen twice in the same shape. It is driven like clouds by the fire of nature.

equivalences.quote: speaking of the mineral nature or First Matter
