terms.meaning: Not defined in this chunk; said to come neither through intelligence nor judgment but through silence imparted by faith, and caused by faith.

quotes.text: muesis, in short, is neither through intelligence nor judgment, but through the uncial silence imparted by faith

terms.meaning: An energy of the soul that faith surpasses; set beside 'intelligence' and 'judgment'. Not defined further.

quotes.text: which is then better than every Gnostic energy

terms.meaning: Acts like a discreet mother who educates the soul and sets it to exercise. God inspires it into philosophers, and the elevated intellect is filled with it.

quotes.text: philosophers into whom the incomprehensible Deity has inspired his own Wisdom
where he is filled with the Demiurgic Wisdom and an empyreal life

terms.meaning: In the Oracle, the source from which intellectual notions crop the Flower of Life. Not further explained.

quotes.text: Intellectual notions from the Paternal Fountain cropping the Flower of Life

terms.meaning: Meeting, union with and direct sight of the Father or Maker. It is not opinion or science but Intellectual Vision.

equivalences.quote: This, then, is the Paternal Port and the discovery of the Father

quotes.text: For discovery is this, --- to meet with him, to be united to Him, and to see Him Himself

terms.meaning: Undefiled union with the Father, with the soul established in him as in a harbour.

equivalences.quote: This, then, is the Paternal Port and the discovery of the Father, according to Proclus, viz., an undefiled union with him

quotes.text: locating the soul in the Father, as in a port

terms.meaning: Pertaining to opinion. It is dubious and close to irrational life, and it is not the true discovery.

quotes.text: not that which is doxastic, or pertaining to opinion

terms.meaning: Direct intellectual sight, meaning contact with the Intelligible and union with the Demiurgic Intellect. It is opposed to syllogistic science.

quotes.text: But it is that which subsists according to Intellectual Vision itself: a contact with the Intelligible, and a union with the Demiurgic Intellect.

terms.meaning: What the soul becomes when assimilated as far as possible to the whole intelligible universe.

quotes.text: the soul thus becoming an Intellectual World

terms.meaning: The object of intellectual contact. The Oracle says it is understood with the Flower of the mind, never wholly comprehended, and exists beyond the mind. The Platonic Successor speaks of transcending even the Intelligible toward the Ineffable.

quotes.text: That thou mayest learn the Intelligible, for it exists beyond the mind.
having transcended the Intelligible

terms.meaning: The faculty with which the Intelligible is to be understood. It is associated with an 'empty mind' and a 'pure turning eye'. The chunk does not define it further.

quotes.text: There is something Intelligible which it behooves thee to understand with the Flower of thy mind.

terms.meaning: The impulse toward the First, which the passions impede. The text gives no further gloss.

quotes.text: the passions alone, which impede our anagogic impulse to the First

terms.meaning: The highest principle. It is celebrated first as unfolding the Intelligible Universe, and only last as producing earth, heavens and souls. It is beyond and more ineffable than all.

quotes.text: as the God of all gods, the Unity of all unities, and beyond the First Adyta
as more ineffable than all silence, and more Unknown than all recondite essence

terms.meaning: The highest reality, called unknown because it is concealed in this life. It becomes known in Identity when the soul concentrates herself.

quotes.text: seek to prove Reality in the Great Unknown --- unknown, because concealed in this life

terms.meaning: Knowing without separation of subject and object. The soul becomes consubstantial with what she knows.

quotes.text: but absolutely, in Identity

terms.meaning: The condition, proved by ancient experience, of passing beyond this life's consciousness toward deification.

quotes.text: Such is the condition and metaphysical alienation which ancient experience sublimely proved, as passing to deification

terms.meaning: Something without which, together with Theurgic assistance, one cannot transcend the consciousness of this life. This chunk does not explain it.

quotes.text: Without the Pontic Medium, without Theurgic assistance we are unable to transcend the consciousness of this life

terms.meaning: Concerning rites and assistance by which an ascent was made through appropriate media and gradual assimilation to the First Cause. Such an ascent cannot be made without them.

quotes.text: by Theurgic rites, an ascent was made through appropriate media and a gradual assimilation, which without these could not be effected, to the knowledge of the First Cause

terms.meaning: The movement of being. In the ultimate circulation all is transparent and self-evident; in the sensible world the circulation is broken at the circumference. The Vital Spirit ascends and descends in 'successive circulations'.

quotes.text: And all things in that ultimate circulation are diaphanous
But in the sensible world the circulation of things is altogether different

terms.meaning: The universal centre, from which the sensible world is an outbirth, versus the circumference, where the equilibrium of being is broken for manifestation. The illuminated light spreads from the freed centre to the circumference of sense.

quotes.text: the equilibrium of being is broken everywhere at the circumference for manifestation
diffusing itself from the freed center outwardly center outwardly until it moved the dark circumference of sense itself

terms.meaning: That which may lawfully descend and ascend in successive circulations until it ends in the Principle of things.

quotes.text: it is said to be lawful for the Vital Spirit to descend and ascend in successive circulations until she terminated her flight in the Principle of things

terms.meaning: That in which Prometheus is fabled to have concealed the fire he stole from heaven. 'Thrysus bearers' are those who have and perceive the fire but cannot draw it forth to manifestation; the chunk sets them against 'Bacchic souls'.

quotes.text: For, in the thrysus, Prometheus is fabled to have concealed the fire he stole from heaven
many had the fire indeed, and were able even to perceive it, who were without the power to discover and draw it forth to manifestation

terms.meaning: The light exhibited in the true Eleusinian initiations. It could be kindled and fortified.

equivalences.with: The light exhibited in the Eleusinian msteries
equivalences.quote: The light exhibited in the Eleusinian msteries, i.e., in the true initiations as is plainly to be gathered from the sense of the ancients, was the Light of Life

quotes.text: was the Light of Life which these could kindle and fortify

terms.meaning: Atwood's name for the process sketched through the Mysteries in connection with the Sacred Art and Alchemy. Its progress discloses powers and secrets of nature.

quotes.text: In the progress of this Vital Experiment, it may not be difficult to imagine that powers would be disclosed and particular secrets of nature in the substance of her Whole.

terms.meaning: Intermediate fruits of the Vital Experiment, called 'vital products'. Exhibited without discovery of their source, they gave rise to 'much astonishment of common chemistry'.

quotes.text: Both of which are vital products

terms.meaning: Named alongside Alchemy as the art whose connection with the Mysteries this chapter was meant to show.

quotes.text: to indicate the connection of the Sacred Art and Alchemy

terms.meaning: Those to whom, according to the expounders, narcotic liquors were given before the shows.

quotes.text: which were administered to the Mystae before the shows commence

terms.meaning: The alchemists' foundational substance; they claim for it extreme attributes and a miraculous origin, as the Greeks do for the ethereal hypostasis.

quotes.text: claiming like extreme attributes and miraculous origin for their first matter

terms.meaning: The principle on which the whole Hermetic philosophy and every tradition of occult science depend. Atwood will examine it and 'how possibly it became known in its first arcane descent and emanation'. Its antecedent is ambiguous (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: it will be requisite to consider this, their Initial Principle, more particularly

terms.meaning: The Greek counterpart of the alchemists' first matter, discussed earlier in the book.

quotes.text: that ethereal hypostasis we were before discussing

terms.meaning: Is in the universe what the natural intelligent Spirit is in man: the commonly diffused vestibule or vehicle of the universal soul of the world, an outward shadow guarding the Light within.

equivalences.quote: so is that Ether then the Sphinx of the Universe

quotes.text: for what the natural intelligent Spirit is in man, that Ether is in the universe
the commonly diffused Ether is as a vestibule or vehicle in respect of the universal soul of the world

terms.meaning: Placed by the Egyptians in the vestibule of Isis; Door-keeper of the Egyptian Mysteries. Stands for the Ether. Passively all that the inner light is impassively; animal form with human face shows a twofold life; her 'winds' image imagination's elevating power. The ancients mastered her.

equivalences.quote: so is that Ether then the Sphinx of the Universe
Such was the Door-keeper of the Egyptian Mysteries

quotes.text: And she is all things passively which the internal light is impassively.

terms.meaning: The natural vehicle of our life, situated in the 'vestibule'; the intelligence that is 'phantasic ... and drawn without', the vestibule of Reason.

equivalences.quote: the Phantastic Spirit, which is the natural vehicle of our life
for what the natural intelligent Spirit is in man, that Ether is in the universe; and this intelligence, phantasic as it is and drawn without, may be called the vestibule of Reason

quotes.text: the Phantastic Spirit, which is the natural vehicle of our life

terms.meaning: In man, the counterpart of Ether in the universe; called 'phantasic' and the vestibule of Reason. Earlier chapters showed the natural Spirit's imperfection and the occultation of its Light.

quotes.text: for what the natural intelligent Spirit is in man, that Ether is in the universe
showing the imperfection of the natural Spirit in his world, the occultation of its Light

terms.meaning: What stands before a 'temple' in ¶5. In man, the phantasic intelligence before Reason; in the universe, the Ether before the world-soul. Mesmerism opens into it.

quotes.text: may be called the vestibule of Reason
opening into the vestibule

terms.meaning: The 'temple' of Intellectual Illumination, entered through the phantasic vestibule.

quotes.text: Reason, which is, as it were, the temple of that Intellectual Ilumination

terms.meaning: Illumination that proceeds from the Divinity within when the conditions are duly offered; Reason is its temple.

quotes.text: Intellectual Ilumination which proceeds, when the conditions are duly offered, from the Divinity within

terms.meaning: Occultly suspended in Nature and called her temple; the Ether is its vestibule or vehicle.

equivalences.quote: the universal soul of the world, which is occultly suspended in Nature, and may be called her temple

quotes.text: the universal soul of the world, which is occultly suspended in Nature, and may be called her temple

terms.meaning: The goddess in whose vestibule the Sphinx stood; the same with Minerva and with the Wisdom under investigation.

equivalences.quote: the vestibule of Isis, who is the same with Minerva and that Wisdom we are investigating
the vestibule of Isis, who is the same with Minerva and that Wisdom we are investigating

terms.meaning: The object of the inquiry. By its Light occult nature's universal efficient is revealed. In the Job passage its place is hidden from all living and God understands its way; for man, the fear of the Lord is Wisdom.

equivalences.quote: the vestibule of Isis, who is the same with Minerva and that Wisdom we are investigating
Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is Wisdom; and to depart from evil is understanding

quotes.text: with her universal efficient by the Light of Wisdom thenceforth revealed

terms.meaning: Possesses an elevating power, imaged by the Sphinx's 'winds', through which the phantastic spirit becomes capable of divine assimilation.

quotes.text: the elevating power which the imagination possesses

terms.meaning: The ancient experimental work on life (the vital alteration of the Mysteries); this chapter examines its Method and Principles before the practice.

quotes.text: Let us examine yet further into the Method of this Vital Experiment

terms.meaning: The genuine art, to be told apart from 'clouds of sophistry'; its Light and virtue assisted the ancients.

quotes.text: that Light and virtue of true Chemistry, by which the ancients were assisted

terms.meaning: The ancient rites, which operated a vital alteration on those desirous of wisdom and immortality; their conduct was 'uniform and entirely scientific'.

quotes.text: the conduct of the Mysteries was uniform and entirely scientific

terms.meaning: What the alchemists establish on the same substantial foundation as Greek philosophy; the chunk does not explain the term further.

quotes.text: In just such a foundation do the Alchemists establish their Free masonry

terms.meaning: The work; its material is an invisible, insensible substance.

quotes.text: Material of our Magistry a substance insensible.

terms.meaning: Modern practice of 'mesmerizing one another', done without knowing how to amend 'the Thing'; a first key that opens only into the vestibule and shows the labyrinth of life.

quotes.text: This Mesmerism, in respect of our Mystery then, may be regarded as a first key

terms.meaning: A young discovery, not yet grown into a science, pursued by patiently gathering outward facts.

quotes.text: the discovery of Vital Magnetism is young, and has had no time to grow up into a science

terms.meaning: Capitalized; what mesmerists reach but do not know how to alter and amend. Not further defined.

quotes.text: without the important knowledge how to alter and amend the Thing

terms.meaning: The ancients' philosophical method, contrasted with modern inductive science; long uncultivated, and Atwood wants philosophy to return to it.

quotes.text: return with her instruments to work as formerly on the a priori ground

terms.meaning: The spirit that ferments spontaneously and so changes the Passive Subject; by grafting and transplanting it could be grown and sublimed by degrees.

quotes.text: the spontaneous fermentation which the Vital Spirit undergoes

terms.meaning: A spontaneous process the Vital Spirit undergoes, changing the Passive Subject; not exploited or 'pushed to the uttermost' in modern practice. Named in the chapter title.

quotes.text: the spontaneous fermentation which the Vital Spirit undergoes, and the change that is thereby effected in the Passive Subject

terms.meaning: What the Vital Spirit's fermentation changes. Not further defined (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: the change that is thereby effected in the Passive Subject

terms.meaning: The ancients' exact art for growing and subliming the Spirit to a third, fourth and fifth degree of concentrated essentiality, in as many representative vessels or forms.

quotes.text: that exact art of grafting and transplanting which the ancients practiced

terms.meaning: The growth and raising of the Spirit through degrees of 'concentrated essentiality', effected by grafting and transplanting.

quotes.text: a growth and sublimation of the Spirit was effected, even to a third, fourth, and fifth degree of concentrated essentiality

terms.meaning: Bound in man like milk in a hard nut; must be freed from its impure envelopes to become pure crystalline matter.

quotes.text: The true medicine, according to the Paracelsians, is bound in man

terms.meaning: The life-fire in man; does nothing excellent while immured, as fuel does nothing unlit; after purgation the pure life flows forth as panacea.

equivalences.quote: our fire of life (called Antimony by adepts

quotes.text: our fire of life (called Antimony by adepts, can effect nothing comparatively excellent whilst it is immured

terms.meaning: The adepts' name for the fire of life.

equivalences.quote: our fire of life (called Antimony by adepts

terms.meaning: The separation of the pure life from impurity, as metal from ore.

quotes.text: by a due purgation, the pure life is separated, as metal from the dark and sordid ore

terms.meaning: What the purged pure life flows forth as.

quotes.text: a pure panacea from the god of Light

terms.meaning: Its knowledge is to be tried by fire; according to Crollius inseparable from pyrotechny; practised by the 'physician'.

quotes.text: the trial of the knowledge of physic is to be made by fire

terms.meaning: According to Crollius inseparable from physic, in the context of trial by fire.

quotes.text: physic and pyrotechny, says Crollius, cannot be separated

terms.meaning: The agent that teaches to segregate every mystery into its own receptacle and to free the medicine from impure external elements. Not defined further (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: the natural inbred chemist teaches to segregate every mystery into its own reservacle

terms.meaning: The separated, purified medicine, to be administered to our bodies.

quotes.text: that the pure crystalline matter may be administered to our bodies

terms.meaning: A master of the art; used for the author of the shell-licking and reason-to-experience sayings (n3, n6: Vaughan), and for those who call the fire of life Antimony.

quotes.text: Verily, says the adept

terms.meaning: An art of purifying and informing the Mind, more lasting than bodily medicine. Through purification and subjugation of the passions it converts the whole hypostasis into inner light. Its practitioners consulted the divine intellect only on purification, liberation and salvation of life.

quotes.text: the Theurgic Art professed a power of purifying and informing the Mind much more beneficial and lasting

terms.meaning: What is converted, as a whole, into substant light within. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: the whole hypostasis was converted finally through faith into the identity of substant light within

terms.meaning: The hidden light, held captive, that is to be found and freed. It is the adepts' aim and the inner treasury that natural reason unlocks. The superior Reason is said to be Light (see Reason).

quotes.text: To find this Light, and to free it from captivity
the Central Light and Wisdom was all their aim

terms.meaning: The superior, supernatural reason. When ascendant it gathers all, as a ferment, into its own Light, separating false forms and assimilating the inferior life. Natural reason is its image.

equivalences.with: Wisdom, Intellect, Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture
equivalences.quote: it is of this the ancients speak, calling it Wisdom, Intellect, Gold, Sol, Sulfur, Tincture
For it is Light indeed, and an occult splendor of existence transcendentally pure
so are we taught to conceive of the Intellectual sun

quotes.text: this Reason gaining the ascendancy, would gather all up, as a ferment, into the superior essence and traction of her own Light

terms.meaning: Ordinary reason. It is necessary but is only an aid at the threshold, dull and inoperative in the work itself. It cannot purify the phantastic Spirit. It is the image of the supernatural reason.

equivalences.quote: as it were an iron key, intended to unlock the golden treasury of light within

quotes.text: these things which the natural reason as an image enacts theoretically, this supernatural reason is said to do as an archetype essentially
But the natural Intellect cannot do this

terms.meaning: The intellect that natural reason helps introduce into self-knowledge. It then turns on the outer life and analyzes and transforms it 'chemically'. The following 'this vital perscrutinator' (the operating agent of the change) appears to refer to it.

quotes.text: this latter, returning with power upon the life without, proceeds to analyze and revolutionize

terms.meaning: The searching, investigating intellect that operates the whole change. Hermes speaks of it, and the sequestration that gives form and essence belongs to it.

equivalences.with: internal fire of the sulfur of thy water
equivalences.quote: It is this vital perscrutinator, the internal fire of the sulfur of thy water, as Eirenaeus calls it

quotes.text: that same perscrutinating Intellect which Hermes speaks of

terms.meaning: The superior separating power. It purifies and attenuates the phantastic Spirit and extends it to Divinity (Synesius). It is unmingled, purest and all-knowing, rules soul, and separates contraries (Anaxagoras). Its special part is the sequestatrix (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: Intellect above all things separates whatever is contrary to the true purity of phantastic Spirit
Intellect is infinite and possesses absolute power, and is not mingled with any thing; but is alone by itself.

terms.meaning: The true Separator: both the efficient cause and the regimen of the work. Nothing foreign enters it.

quotes.text: we observe Mind to be the true Separator, the efficient as well as the regimen of the work

terms.meaning: The Art's primary object and 'the greatest miracle in philosophy': separating pure from impure and subtle from gross. Mind does it, not mechanical dissolution. Atwood identifies it with the Mysteries' ordeal of the death of the natural life.

equivalences.with: the ordeals of the Mysteries (decomposition and death of the natural life)
equivalences.quote: appears to be identical with that which is described as taking place in the Mysteries, when the great ordeals are passed through during the decomposition and death of the natural life

quotes.text: This Separation is indeed the primary object of the Art

terms.meaning: That which gives each thing its form and essence. Atwood calls it, or the Separation, the special part of Intellect (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: that is the sequestatrix, which gives to every thing its form and essence

terms.meaning: What the Alchemists distill. At the end of Separation the pure Ether is resurrected into Light.

quotes.text: our Oedipus distillers of this Ether, the instructive Alchemists
the final resurrection of the pure Ether into Light

terms.meaning: The God-given standard for discerning right from wrong. The superior Reason is 'the Reason of our Rule'.

quotes.text: Take hold of that Rule which God hath given thee for direction
the superior virtue of that which is the Reason of our Rule

terms.meaning: Something that comes only by ingenuity and industry, when nature is helped beyond her common course. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: the Mercury of the Wise comes not but by help of ingenuity and industry

terms.meaning: What nature holds concealed, to be sought with one's own eyes and hand. It is the basis for philosophizing with judgment.

quotes.text: Learn and look for the first foundation, says the monk, which nature holds concealed

terms.meaning: Its attainment is laborious and is the fruit of intellectual research.

quotes.text: the attainment of the Tree of Life is laborious, and the fruit of intellectual research

terms.meaning: The 'Magistery of life', reached only by those who hold 'this passport'.

quotes.text: they only who have obtained this passport can attain to the Magistery of life

terms.meaning: The inner fire. It is imprisoned in the hard, dry body and freed by our water, appears in the Third Menstrual, and is to be tended more than the furnace fire. In ¶13 Atwood names Eirenaeus' 'internal fire of the sulfur of thy water' as the vital perscrutinator.

equivalences.quote: Our fire is the true sulfur of Gold, says Eirenaeus
this is the seed of gold, involved in many links, and held prisoner, as it were, in a deep dungeon

quotes.text: be not so careful of the fire of the Athanor as of your internal Fire

terms.meaning: The hard, dry body that imprisons the fire and is rotted by our water. A gloss in the passage makes it the ethereal body.

equivalences.quote: by rotting the moles of the body (i.e., of the ethereal body)

quotes.text: which in the hard and dry body is imprisoned

terms.meaning: 'Our water' frees the fire by rotting the body. The 'first water' is prepared, joined to the body in just pondus, opens its pores and extracts part of the tincture of Sol. The text does not say whether the two are the same (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: by the mediation of our water it is set loose
the first water will work on the body till it hath opened the pores and extracted partly the tincture of Sol

terms.meaning: There are three. The freed fire appears visibly in the third, which only one who knows the first two can see.

quotes.text: it appears visibly in our Third Menstrual
he that knows not our two first menstruals is altogether shut out

terms.meaning: The just weight or proportion in which the first water is joined to the body.

quotes.text: to join it to the body in a just pondus

terms.meaning: The source of the external fire, which matters less than the internal Fire.

quotes.text: be not so careful of the fire of the Athanor as of your internal Fire

terms.meaning: What the first water partly extracts from the body, as a sign. (Separately, 'Tincture' is a name for Reason, and 'foreign tincture' is what Reason grinds out of the inferior life.)

quotes.text: extracted partly the tincture of Sol

terms.meaning: Named as the signal. This chunk does not explain them.

quotes.text: your signal the Doves of Diana

terms.meaning: What the Sybil sends Aeneas to find. Atwood offers it as a parallel to the hidden object of the work.

quotes.text: he may discover and bring to her the Golden Bough

terms.meaning: The place to be entered with a prudent motive. From it the mineral radix of the Art is carried away.

equivalences.with: Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life
equivalences.quote: the Cave of Mercury, which, according to the Hermetic interpretation, is Taenerus, the most hidden vapor of life

terms.meaning: What is carried in both hands from the Cave of Mercury: the root and true matter of the Art.

equivalences.with: true mater of the Hermetic Art
equivalences.quote: the mineral radix and true mater of the Hermetic Art

terms.meaning: The 'bottomless' Mercury into which the gold body is thrown. In Eirenaeus it is to be 'the internal'. Not decoded here.

quotes.text: such a Mercury as is bottomless, or whose center it can never find, but by discovering its own
let Mercury be the internal

terms.meaning: Reason acts 'as a ferment', gathering all into its Light. A 'brazen ferment' is contrasted with the true gold body.

quotes.text: would gather all up, as a ferment
that body which is gold (not a brazen ferment)

terms.meaning: The spirit that, when subjugated, abandons its phantasy and yields the clear light of understanding to the trained investigator.

equivalences.quote: ends in her subjugation; in other words, the Ethereal Spirit abandons her phantasy

terms.meaning: The spirit whose impurity Intellect separates; Intellect attenuates it and extends it to Divinity. The text does not assert that it is the same as the Ethereal Spirit.

quotes.text: Intellect above all things separates whatever is contrary to the true purity of phantastic Spirit

terms.meaning: A mode of the One Thing, alongside folly and passion. If it prevails it converts the inner life to folly. The Ethereal Spirit abandons it when subdued.

quotes.text: the phantasy, if suffered to prevail, will convert all to her own folly in the internal life

terms.meaning: Something that man can both find and effect.

quotes.text: man should be able not only to find the Causal Nature but to effect it

terms.meaning: A complete process that must be passed through before the work is perfected. Not defined here.

quotes.text: it is not perfected unless the whole introversion is passed through

terms.meaning: The whole matter of the work. Folly, phantasy, passion and Reason are its modes of being.

quotes.text: the whole matter I know to be One only Thing

terms.meaning: What Lully, Arnold, Bacon and Geber celebrate, in connection with Reason acting as a ferment.

quotes.text: abundantly celebrating the virtues of their Head Stone

terms.meaning: The Spirit, made passive, into which the supernatural reason infuses itself throughout.

quotes.text: by pure infusion of Itself to the passified Spirit throughout

terms.meaning: The only universal faculty that can be consciously distinguished by itself. In individual consciousness it is the foundation of all law, and its luminous revelation in a purified intelligence is the beginning of Wisdom. Cut off from its source it is weak and unaware of that source.

quotes.text: this root of reason which is truly catholic
in our mere individual consciousness it is the foundation of all law

terms.meaning: The purified divine intelligence. It is to be sought in spirit, is supremely beautiful, and gives the soul a sudden Light that is Intellect itself. It is isolated and in anguish when its light is taken away.

equivalences.quote: this Light is from Intellect, and is also It

quotes.text: That Intellect must be assumed which is most perfectly purified
the wanderings and anguish of Intellect so artificially isolated on the plain of Truth

terms.meaning: The individual and the universal. The microcosmic experiment yields knowledge of the macrocosmic Cause, and the microcosm's fire takes over where the macrocosm's operative fire ends.

quotes.text: by the microcosmic experiment into It, the knowledge if the macrocosmic Cause also was derived
the corporeal fire of the microcosm

terms.meaning: The agent that dissolves the vital medium and draws the Voluntary Efficient upward.

equivalences.quote: the purified spirit or intelligence, that is Isis

terms.meaning: What the purified intelligence dissolves to open the occult source. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: by dissolving the vital medium, opens the occult source

terms.meaning: Something drawn upward into intellectual reminiscence once the vital medium is dissolved; Wisdom 'recovering her lost Efficient'. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: draws the Voluntary Efficient upward into intellectual reminescence
to Wisdom recovering her lost Efficient in the Light of life

terms.meaning: A small, purified, fire-tested portion that re-enters its native life and transmutes it all into its own Aurific Light.

quotes.text: a small grain of the metaphysical ferment leavens the whole lump
the metaphysical graft, already purified and passed the fire, re-enters to redeem its congenital life

terms.meaning: The gold-making light of the ferment, into whose substance everything is transmuted.

quotes.text: transmutes all into the substance of its own Aurific Light

terms.meaning: The sharp, discriminating spirit of the working leaven, which enters the philosopher's Mercury and makes it putrefy.

quotes.text: this acute discriminative sulfuric Spirit occasions a putrefaction of the philosopher’s Mercury

terms.meaning: The impure vapour of life, which the sulfuric Spirit causes to putrefy.

equivalences.quote: the philosopher’s Mercury, i.e., of the impure vapor of life

terms.meaning: The decay of the vital vapour under the ferment, and more generally the death and corruption each life goes through before it rises better, like a grain in the earth.

quotes.text: Does not the grain putrefy in the moist earth before it springs?

terms.meaning: The intermediate life that comes before the heroic work. It must be cut off in its prime, shut up and buried. Until it dissolves, the Vital Spirit cannot be radically improved.

quotes.text: the celestial medial life which, in the order of divine rites, precedes the heroic work
this dissolution of the first medial life

terms.meaning: What the work aims to improve. It needs a motive, which comes from being deprived of its Understanding Light.

quotes.text: Nothing is done radically to meliorate the Vital Spirit

terms.meaning: The light the Divine Law takes from the spirit while it is in full vigour, so as to give it a motive.

quotes.text: depriving it when in full vigor of its Understanding Light

terms.meaning: The self-sacrificing will (Achilles' 'vindicative will') that enters after the loss and stirs the bitter waters to recover the lost kingdom.

quotes.text: the Heroic Will enters in, self-sacrificing, and stirs the bitter waters

terms.meaning: Generation in which the parent is bettered in the offspring, up to a fourth or fifth generation.

quotes.text: the Law especial of spiritual generation that the parent is bettered in the offspring

terms.meaning: The true separating agent. Finding it is the greatest difficulty, which Atwood likens to Virgil's hidden tree.

quotes.text: To find the true Separator is described, in fact, as the greatest difficulty

terms.meaning: Something hidden under the oblivion of natural birth and revealed only by celestial instinct. Its bough, not the whole tree, is to be taken.

quotes.text: The tree of life covered over, indeed, with the dark oblivion of this natural outbirth, is latent and difficult to find

terms.meaning: The celestial instinct that conceived the tree of life. It alone reveals the tree and leads into the Paternal light of life.

equivalences.quote: the celestial instinct only to reveal; that subtle Maternal; intelligence which originally conceived it

terms.meaning: The light that is more central and comes before the Maternal intelligence, which leads into it.

quotes.text: the yet more central, antecedent Paternal, light of life

terms.meaning: The heroic, separable, thrice-refined purpose personified by many heroes and by Hermes' 'our Son'. It passes through darkness, death and the Stygian waters.

equivalences.quote: This is that prolific Mustard-seed, and Light of divine Faith
our Son, as Hermes calls him, born a king

equivalences.with: Caduceus of Hermes; Golden Bough; ferrying Cup of Hercules
equivalences.quote: Such was the Caduceus of Hermes --- the Golden Bough, the ferrying Cup of Hercules

quotes.text: that heroic, separable, triply refined intellectual purpose

terms.meaning: What the Light of Faith discovers when it searches the interior.

equivalences.quote: the occult Stone --- the hidden Medicine

terms.meaning: One of the 'golden passports' into the hidden realms. It is the bough rather than the tree, the small portion to start from.

equivalences.with: Caduceus of Hermes; ferrying Cup of Hercules
equivalences.quote: Such was the Caduceus of Hermes --- the Golden Bough, the ferrying Cup of Hercules

quotes.text: Ramus, non arbor --- The bough, not the whole tree, is to be taken

terms.meaning: The true principle of the Art, about which the alchemists are very wary. It is a divine ray issuing from the will of the divinized.

equivalences.quote: it is no common light that enters into Divinity, but a congenial ray; a Power

quotes.text: This vertical separated Light then we take henceforth to be the true alternative principle in the Divine Art

terms.meaning: The secret Fire that Pontanus calls the unrevealed key of all the philosophers, to be found by profound meditation.

equivalences.quote: seek to know this Fire with all thy soul, that so thou mayest attain to thy desire; for it is the key of all the philosophers

terms.meaning: The decisive secret of the Art. It opens the first and the last gate, and missing it ruins the whole course.

quotes.text: this key is the principal part of the whole Art; this opens the first gate, this will also unlock the last

terms.meaning: In Basil Valentine's words, the stone of Fire. Preparing it is the key of Alchemy, and it is matured with the microcosm's corporeal fire.

equivalences.quote: our stone of Fire (which is Antimony)

quotes.text: in the preparation of Antimony consists the Key of Alchemy

terms.meaning: The name given to the method of using the key.

quotes.text: the method, which is called Manual Operation, by which to use it

terms.meaning: The boiling and maturing of the stone of Fire with the microcosm's corporeal fire.

quotes.text: let no man wonder at this coction

terms.meaning: The method of the Art, which Atwood says Palingenius 'divulges' in verse.

quotes.text: divulges the artificial method in the few following lines

terms.meaning: Simple and harmoniously framed; it baffles and condemns the operator who introduces his own blind purpose.

quotes.text: The Law of Nature, being simple and harmoniously framed, will baffle him

terms.meaning: The trained seeker or operator of the Art, who must learn what, where and how to obey, inquire, will and hope.

quotes.text: all the care that is taken to train the true Inquisitor

terms.meaning: Revelation without which the operator's purpose is blind; its 'corroborative virtue', drawn by the new life, turns the Quintessence into living gold. ¶40 also speaks of the 'guardian of the Light'.

quotes.text: he who presumes without the revelation of the Divine Light to introduce his own blind purpose
needs only the corroborative virtue of the Divine light which it draws

terms.meaning: A divine 'artist of great subtlety' within the lovers of Art; it must not be given into the bestial hand.

quotes.text: whose Separator is an artist of great subtlety in them

terms.meaning: The receptive intelligence (spoken of as 'her') which, freed by art and set in conjunction, answers the Will of her seeking Reason, finds the way, removes obstacles and passes with him through the abyss.

equivalences.quote: the Moon is singularly honored, for it is the Passive Intelligence

quotes.text: responds to the Will of her seeking Reason

terms.meaning: Understanding gotten in transcendental contemplation of herself; it directs the mode of analysis and provides most of its means. The chunk does not explicitly identify it with the Passive Intelligence.

quotes.text: the Passive Understanding gotten in transcendental contemplation of herself

terms.meaning: In Alchemy, the Passive Intelligence; with the Sun, one of the pair that 'sound the depths together'; per Plutarch, reflects the works of reason and proceeds from Wisdom. Boehme finds Sol and Luna together at the cross.

equivalences.quote: the Moon is singularly honored, for it is the Passive Intelligence

quotes.text: the influence of the Moon, says Plutarch, seems to reflect the works of reason, and to proceed from Wisdom

terms.meaning: Partner of the Moon in the work; per Plutarch its operations work by strength and force. In Boehme's passage Sol is given to the reduced body as its soul.

equivalences.quote: give it Sol, viz., the soul

quotes.text: the operations of the Sun are seen to resemble those strokes which by mere dint of strength and force bear down all before them

terms.meaning: The active principle (spoken of as 'him') whose Will the Passive Intelligence answers and accompanies through the abyss.

quotes.text: responds to the Will of her seeking Reason

terms.meaning: The working cause. The 'true efficient' springs from within together with knowledge, one with it in principle but distinguished in practice for the sake of offspring. The 'Rational Efficient', armed with intelligence, discovers the evil of its first conception and dissolves the Vital Bond. The chunk does not explicitly say the two phrases name the same thing.

equivalences.quote: which are indeed one in principle

quotes.text: It is from within that the knowledge springs together with the true efficient
the Rational Efficient, armed with a bright intelligence

terms.meaning: The two principles of the work, active and receptive, equal Spirits that must both be prepared and allied; each dies in the other, the old life is crucified, and their reunion under another law yields the new life.

quotes.text: Both therefore have to be prepared --- the spiritual agent and the spiritual patient
by death and contrition of the agent in the patient, and vice versa

terms.meaning: That whose miracles are performed according to the Smagardine Table, whence all the rest proceed by adaptation.

quotes.text: for performing the miracles of the One Thing whence all the rest proceed by adaptation

terms.meaning: Something the precepts demand, given as why the two Spirits need each other. Separately, the 'sensible medium' is what is dominant in this present birth and is made occult in regeneration.

quotes.text: for the precepts demand a medium
the sensible medium, which in this present birth is dominant, being made occult

terms.meaning: The inner fire which, purified, alone perfects the work; contrasted with the external coal fire and the fire of the natural life, which only alter.

quotes.text: the internal alone is able, being purified, to perfect the work begun

terms.meaning: The fire used to besiege the bound serpents. Not defined here; the chunk does not say whether it is the 'fire of the natural life' of ¶43.

quotes.text: Thou must incamp against them with the fire of nature

terms.meaning: Two are to be mortified together, each venerating and venerated: of Auripigment and the Oriental of magnesia. Not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: the Argent vive of Auripigment and the Oriental Argent vive of magnesia

terms.meaning: What the Rational Efficient proceeds to dissolve; not further defined here.

quotes.text: it proceeds even to a dissolution of the Vital Bond

terms.meaning: The life-spirit in which, after the first preliminaries, the work aims to produce an alteration by Rational Analysis.

quotes.text: the object was to produce an alteration in the Vital Spirit

terms.meaning: The operation, repeatedly passed through, that alters the Vital Spirit and dissolves the whole natural born hypostasis. ¶40 says 'the mode of analysis' is directed by the Passive Understanding; the chunk does not explicitly link the two phrases.

quotes.text: a true Rational Analysis, which, repeatedly passed through, leads on to a dissolution of the whole natural born hypostasis

terms.meaning: The 'natural born' constitution whose dissolution is the condition for new life and growth into consciousness.

quotes.text: a dissolution of the whole natural born hypostasis

terms.meaning: The new life elicited from the crucifixion of the old by reunion of the principles under another law; with the Divine light it becomes living gold.

equivalences.quote: which life is a very real and pure Quintessence, the Mercury so much sought after, even the Elixir of Life
which life is a very real and pure Quintessence, the Mercury so much sought after, even the Elixir of Life

quotes.text: the new life is elicited

terms.meaning: What the Quintessence becomes with the Divine light's virtue: transmuting and multiplicative, the concrete form of what is valued in dead metal.

quotes.text: the living gold of the philosophers, transmuting and multiplicative --- the concrete form of that which in the dead metal we esteem

terms.meaning: Something to be found and then made profitable only by joining it with a consanguineous spirit and circulating the two until one conceives by the other.

quotes.text: this is the true way and means by which the metaphysical body of gold will be made profitable

terms.meaning: What the philosophers searched for; what they found in it is the miraculous principle of regeneration. The Master says it comes and is generated with Light, then brings forth darkness.

equivalences.quote: That which they sought after, and profess accordingly to have discovered, therefore, is this miraculous principle of regeneration

quotes.text: Our stone comes with Light, and with Light it is generated

terms.meaning: The miraculous principle by which the relationships of the vital elements are exchanged: the sensible medium becomes occult and the occult, catholic reason of life becomes manifest.

quotes.text: by which the relationships of the vital elements are exchanged

terms.meaning: What the stone brings forth after Light; called the mother of all things.

equivalences.quote: it brings forth the clouds, or darkness, which is the mother of all things

terms.meaning: That in which Nature contains and separates all things.

quotes.text: which containest and separatest all things in a middle principle

terms.meaning: In Boehme, what one must enter, 'in the Fourth Form', where Sol and Luna are together, to seek gold. Atwood's gloss speaks of the old life being 'crucified'.

quotes.text: enter in even to the Cross, then seek gold and you will not be deceived
out of that crucifixion, by reunion of the principles under another law, the new life is elicited

terms.meaning: Where the cross is entered and Sol and Luna are found together; not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: enter I even to the cross in the Fourth Form, there you have Sol and Luna together

terms.meaning: Where the two serpents, tied in a love knot, are shut up; not explained here.

quotes.text: tie them in a love knot and shut them up in the Arabian Caraha

terms.meaning: Two, found everywhere on earth: a living male and a living female, to be understood spiritually, without corporeal allusion.

quotes.text: they are a living male and a living female (understand in relation to the spirit always without all corporeal allusion)

terms.meaning: The deep red bird that appears after the fire is fortified; fed with the fire of his father (meat) and the ether of his mother (drink).

quotes.text: It is a red bird of a most deep color with a shining fiery hue.

terms.meaning: Required for the insoluble, transmuting, uniting union that is sought; creating and transmuting without violence belong to the first power, wisdom and love.

quotes.text: such a tie cannot be without the first unity

terms.meaning: Its end and perfection is the inward, essential union (marriage) of the elements through the first love. Boehme also speaks of a 'composed magical body' that, bruised, becomes 'magical and hungry after nature'.

quotes.text: they will never inward and essentially unite; which is the end and perfection of magic
bruise that composed magical body

terms.meaning: One of the three principles into which the ethereal hypostasis separates; it is the soul and golden ferment. In the dissolution the oppressive will dislocates it, and it floats on the ethereal waters. In Sendivogius's fable Sal mortally wounds Sulfur.

equivalences.quote: The sulfur, which is the soul and golden ferment
The sulfur, which is the soul and golden ferment

quotes.text: the soul, the spirit, and the body principle; the paternal, maternal, and proceeding substance of life; sulfur, mercury, salt
the blackness from the sulfur

terms.meaning: One of the three principles, listed second in the series of III.1 ¶53, in the same position as spirit and the maternal substance; whether these correspond is not stated (see ambiguities). Maria says the resolved poison coagulates 'our Mercury' into pure silver.

quotes.text: it coagulates our Mercury into most pure silver o all tests

terms.meaning: One of the three principles, listed third in the series of III.1 ¶53, in the same position as the body principle and the proceeding substance (see ambiguities). The Adept says no one attains the Science without it. In Sendivogius's fable Sal mortally wounds Sulfur.

quotes.text: yet without Salt no man can attain to this Sacred Science
Sal gave Sulfur a mortal wound

terms.meaning: The one life-substance that, in the dissolution, is divided against itself into three principles.

quotes.text: the ethereal hypostasis is divided against itself and brought to a separation even as these three

terms.meaning: The waters the displaced sulfur floats on. They tear, decoct and soften the sensual dominant.

quotes.text: to float upon the ethereal waters, whilst these continue to tear, decoct, and soften the sensual dominant

terms.meaning: The dominant sense-life. The ethereal waters soften it so that it is fit for returning reason and understanding to work on.

quotes.text: make it more fit for the returning reason and understanding to work upon

terms.meaning: Sulfur is called the 'golden ferment'. The rising light carries a 'fermental odor of the body' so that the soul does not depart altogether.

quotes.text: a fermental odor of the body

terms.meaning: The inner self-will that arrests the entering light. It must be humbled by voluntary sacrifice, and the connate spirit finally subdues it to self-mortification.

quotes.text: penetrating to meet the self-willed Identity within, is arrested
humiliation of the Selfhood under the exemplary cross of Christ

terms.meaning: The breaking-up of the body of the light and of the natural-born life, in which the three principles separate. Its cause appears to be vital heat artificially stirred in the blood.

quotes.text: an eclipsation of the light takes place, and a dissolution of its body

terms.meaning: The period of the principles' separation, during which a coction goes on amid flood, eclipse and confusion.

quotes.text: during this period of the severation, a wonderful coction is described as going on

terms.meaning: The cooking or digesting that goes on during the severation. The waters 'decoct' the sensual dominant, and the dragons are 'decocted' in their own venom.

quotes.text: a wonderful coction is described as going on

terms.meaning: That which undergoes the abyssal regeneration and contest in the intermediate stages, before it is born into sense perception.

quotes.text: the abyssal regeneration and contest of the metaphysical Embryo before it is born into the perception by the eye of sense

terms.meaning: The operative procedure, which Atwood says she is not yet setting out but only seeking to understand.

quotes.text: But we are not yet proposing to exhibit the Practice, but only to understand it

terms.meaning: The adepts describe what is entered for the dissolution as 'the greatest poison', and the root of the Science is called 'a deadly poison'. The text does not say whether these are the same thing. Resolved into a subtle water, the poison coagulates our Mercury into silver.

equivalences.quote: because the root of this Science is a deadly poison

quotes.text: adepts describe it indeed as the greatest poison

terms.meaning: In the fable, Osiris's uterine brother, who killed and scattered him. Applied to the work, Typhon is the wrathful fire or Efficient of the dissolution, and also a name of the unclean Instrument that moves the gold to putrefy. He is called Seth and Bebo, names that import violent restraint, contrariety and subversion. Isis gradually enthrals him.

equivalences.quote: Adepts call him the Green Lion, Typhon, Firedrake
or during the mortification, he is their venomous Black Toad

equivalences.with: the Instrument moving the gold to putrefy; Satan, Aquafoetida, Ignis Gehanna, Mortis Immundities
equivalences.quote: it is called by them Typhon, Satan, Aquafoetida, Ignis Gehanna, Mortis Immundities, etc.
they gave to Typhon, in this predicament, the name of Seth, Bebo

quotes.text: importing a certain violent, forcible restraint, contrariety, and subversion

terms.meaning: The newly roused, wrathful active agent of the dissolution. It reduces the body of Light (Osiris) to vapor.

quotes.text: the newly roused Efficient is exceeding wrathful

terms.meaning: The putting to death of the fiery self-willed agent once it has grown to the full and the time is ripe. The connate spirit finally brings the agent to it as self-mortification.

quotes.text: until the time for his mortification is ripe and ready at hand

terms.meaning: In the fable, the brother whom Typhon kills and scatters. Applied to the work, Osiris is the Divine Light, the 'foreign body of Light'. The Efficient reduces it to vapor, and it suffers restraint in passing through the voluntary axle.

equivalences.quote: the foreign body of Light, which is Osiris
Osiris, i.e., the Divine Light

terms.meaning: The philosophers' name, given 'on account of its origin', for the vapor into which the body of Light is reduced. It condenses at the top of the vessel and runs down continually. In the fable, Typhon scatters Osiris's members 'to the four winds'.

quotes.text: a mere vapor, called by the philosophers, on account of its origin, the Four Winds

terms.meaning: The common name for this stage of dissolution: a dark entrance with Cimmerian windings and continual terror of the Spirit.

quotes.text: This is commonly called the Gate of Putrefaction

terms.meaning: The realm whose powers are shaken and defiled during the putrefaction.

quotes.text: the powers of the Philosophic Heaven are so wonderfully shaken and defiled

terms.meaning: In Hermes, a principle that dwells in all the threefold nature, with their darkness and blackness as its houses. In the French adept, two dragons that bite each other until they become a Fifth Essence.

quotes.text: The Dragon dwells in all the threefold nature, and his houses are the darkness and blackness that is in them

terms.meaning: What the two warring dragons become once they are decocted totally in their own venom.

quotes.text: being decocted totally in their own venom, are turned into a Fifth Essence

terms.meaning: The swifter contrary current in the circulation, which surmounts and eclipses the Divine Light.

quotes.text: the swifter current of the Infernal motive wheel surmounts and eclipses the Divine Light in the circulation

terms.meaning: The one unclean thing that enters the Stone, moving the gold to putrefy; it is 'the very grave of the rational light'. It is evil at first but necessary, and once returned through the natural Alembic it constitutes the work's force and perfection.

equivalences.with: Typhon, Satan, Aquafoetida, Ignis Gehanna, Mortis Immundities
equivalences.quote: it is called by them Typhon, Satan, Aquafoetida, Ignis Gehanna, Mortis Immundities, etc.

quotes.text: except One thing, which is the Instrument moving the gold to putrefy
it is the very grave of the rational light

terms.meaning: That through which the impure Instrument is brought and returned. Because a phrase is repeated, the printed text may also say that the Instrument constitutes it (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: when finally brought through the natural Alembic, and returned, it constitutes the natural Alembic

terms.meaning: The completed work, whose force and integral perfection the returned Instrument constitutes.

quotes.text: the force and integral perfection of the Divine Superstructure

terms.meaning: The object of the work. Only one unclean thing enters its composition. After its darkness in purgatory it is purged and becomes a white Elixir.

quotes.text: nothing of an unclean nature that enters into the composition of the Stone, except One thing

terms.meaning: What the purged stone becomes in whiteness.

quotes.text: in whytenes Elixir of great might

terms.meaning: The inborn spirit whose attractive grace subdues the self-willed agent and brings it to self-mortification. 'This Spirit' (very probably the connate spirit) has self-motion and intelligence.

quotes.text: it is by the attractive grace of the connate spirit

terms.meaning: The agent that takes the principal part when Sol is eclipsed. It acts as Isis does in the Mysteries.

equivalences.quote: the Lunar Vulcan acts a principal part, as Isis in the Mysteries

quotes.text: Sol being eclipsed, the Lunar Vulcan acts a principal part

terms.meaning: In the fable, she gathers Osiris's members and hides them in a chest. In the work, the Lunar Vulcan plays her part: she tempers Typhon and reconciles the opposed principles, which then circulate with her in equilibrium. She is also called Athena, to express this Spirit's self-motion and intelligence.

equivalences.quote: as Isis in the Mysteries, where she is also called Athena

quotes.text: but Isis, recollecting, hides them in a chest
to express that self-motion and intelligence with which this Spirit is endowed

terms.meaning: What Osiris (the Divine Light) passes through in the regeneration, suffering Typhon's restraint, contrariety and subversion.

quotes.text: suffers in passing through the voluntary axle in the regeneration

terms.meaning: The poem's central agent: called green because unripe, not coloured; not common quicksilver; swift; devours and eclipses the Sun, turning red to white, yet perfects him; as Priest weds Sun and Moon, who were born in its Bed; supplies the Lion's Blood; beguiles most who hunt it.

quotes.text: But our Lyon wanting maturity, Is called greene for unripenes trust me,
For they weene that our Lyon ys Common Quicksilver, but truly they miss:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The 'secret' drawn off after Lion, Sol and Luna unite and form a skin; the King's only food, given after he rises from the dead; worked with Luna or Sol to prepare the ferments. Possibly called the King's Father and Mother (see ambiguities).

equivalences.quote: A right good secret withouten any nay: Wych must serve to doe thee good’ For yt ys the Lyons Blood:

quotes.text: And tis as strange that thys Kings food, Can be nothing but thys Lyons Blood;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The liquid given to the pure matter at each imbibition; not further defined in this chunk (relation to Lion's Blood: see ambiguities).

quotes.text: A portion of your Lyons sweate Must be given it for to eate:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The bright one devoured and eclipsed by the Lion and brought to more perfection; brother and bridegroom of the Moon; with her, parent of the King; feeds a red King. 'Sol' occupies parallel positions (fed to the Lion with Luna; 'Of Sol for Redd'), but the chunk does not assert the identity.

quotes.text: This Lyon maketh the Sun sith [fith] soone To be joined to hys Sister the Moone:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Sister and bride of the Sun, born with him in the Lion's Bed; with him, parent of the King. 'Luna' occupies parallel positions (fed to the Lion with Sol; worked alone with the Lion's blood for the white ferment; feeds a white King), but the chunk does not assert the identity.

quotes.text: Worke Luna by her selfe alone, With the blood of the Greene Lyon:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Offspring of Sun and Moon wedded by the Lion; fed on the Lion's Blood; dies (paired with blackness) and rises; fed with Luna if white, the Sun if red. The matter is also called 'this young Chylde' / 'Child' in the same sequence; the identity of King and Child is not explicitly asserted.

quotes.text: And yet thys King was begott by none other, But by Sun and Moone hys owne Sister and Brother.

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The fair white part left in the midst when the matter separates from its black, light 'vile Erth'; must show full white; the ferment is put into it as one fourth part.

quotes.text: Your magnet in the midst wilbe, Of Collour faire and white trust me;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Something whose creation the old philosophers described at large, while concealing how to order it afterwards (imbibition).

quotes.text: To create Magnesia they made no care, In their Bookes largely to declare;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Giving the dried matter 'drink' (Lion's sweat), grinding, sealing and drying, repeated on a fixed schedule; the secret the old philosophers never told, in which 'the whole subtill warke' consists.

quotes.text: The secret of Imbibition never out tould;
Because in it consisteth the whole subtill warke;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: In the poem: a preparation of the same nature as the work's beginning (Luna for white, Sol for red, each worked alone with the Lion's blood; 'Ferment of peure Gold' for red), added warm to the Magnet as one fourth part; continual fermentation multiplies the Medicine; fermentation is how all things are brought forth fitted to their generation. Atwood's 'Rational Ferment' (¶66) is a separate term.

quotes.text: Which Ferment must be of such a thing, As was the workes begyning;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Increasing the Medicine without restarting the work, best done by continual fermentation.

quotes.text: It’s so well Multeplied as with continuall Firmentation:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The final use or test of the product; those ignorant of imbibition found nothing in it; continually fermented medicine 'in Projeccion ren full fast'.

quotes.text: And sure far it will be exalted at the last, And in Projeccion ren full fast:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: The product, augmented by keeping ferment always in the fire.

quotes.text: That thy Medicine augment mayst aye;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: Residue removed once the matter has grown very dry, before lodging the young Child in a bright bed.

quotes.text: The excrements be tane away;

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: In the poem, the learned who will find truth in the work, as against the 'lay', who should keep counsel and leave off; the narrator says he is 'noe Clerke' in science yet has laboured in the work.

quotes.text: For surely if thow be a Clerke, Thow wilt finde trewth in thys werke:

terms.voice: QUOTED: The Hunting of the Greene Lyon

terms.meaning: A principle with 'stolen forces' that provokes a bloody conflict in life; the Divine Art requires an identical representative of him so those forces can be drawn forth and spent; depicted in Egyptian relics in human semblance between foes.

quotes.text: innumerable similitudes belonging both to this rebellious Principle and to that identical representative of him which the Divine Art requires

terms.meaning: The Art under discussion; it requires a representative of the rebellious Principle. ¶66 speaks of 'the Hermetic Art'; the chunk does not assert the two names identical.

quotes.text: that identical representative of him which the Divine Art requires

terms.meaning: That which must be stripped of its (lion's) skin by the Hand, not by arrows or clubs; per the Latin it then enters the great salt sea and comes out again with beauty. Not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: For the Orient Animal must be stripped of his skin, not with arrows or clubs, but with the Hand, as Adepts say

terms.meaning: Something that must be dissected and shorn, in parallel with stripping the Orient Animal's skin.

quotes.text: the whole garment of Light must be dissected, shorn, and the signal of victory be heroically transferred

terms.meaning: The imperishable, perpetually victorious quintessential virtue of the New Life; the first Material foundation of the Hermetic Art; known only to the Wise who have it in themselves.

equivalences.with: first Material foundation of the Hermetic Art
equivalences.quote: is the Corner Stone or first Material foundation of the Hermetic Art

equivalences.with: quintessential virtue of the New Life
equivalences.quote: the New Life thence arises whose quintessential virtue, imperishable and perpetually victorious, is the Corner Stone

quotes.text: known, as the Adept says, only to the Wise, because they alone can know it who have it in themselves

terms.meaning: What arises when the evil of Original Sin is overcome by subtle stratagems; its quintessential virtue is the Corner Stone.

quotes.text: The evil of the Original Sin being overcome by so many subtle stratagems, the New Life thence arises

terms.meaning: An evil overcome by 'so many subtle stratagems', whereupon the New Life arises.

quotes.text: The evil of the Original Sin being overcome by so many subtle stratagems

terms.meaning: What Cadmus, Jason, Orpheus, Aeneas and the rest represent; the other faculties of the mind are originally attendant on it.

quotes.text: identified him with Jason, Orpheus, Aeneas, and the rest, who represent the Rational Ferment;

terms.meaning: A principle that, once freed, rapidly draws the mind's other faculties into its vortex, revels with them, becomes satiated and thus more easily ensnared. The chunk does not assert its identity with the 'rebellious Principle' of ¶64.

quotes.text: drawn away afterwards into the vortex of the Opposive Principle, rapidly attracting them when it is freed

terms.meaning: The Will, signified by the drunken Saturn of the verse, which revels unrestrained through the subordinate faculties until sated and asleep.

equivalences.quote: For the Saturnian Will, being allowed to revel without limitation or rational restraint

quotes.text: his desires are more than satisfied, and, as the image runs, from the effect he sleeps

terms.meaning: The watchful faculty that cuts off the sleeping Will.

quotes.text: the watchful eye of Intellect, well advised and able
