equivalences.with: God (according to Xenophanes, as reported by Aristotle)
equivalences.quote: looking to the whole heaven, he says, the One is God

quotes.text: if any one should undertake to demonstrate the philosopher’s Unit, he would unfold Being

terms.meaning: The totality contained proportionally in every portion of existence; simple; known by contact and intuition in self-knowledge.

quotes.text: every portion of existence to be continent and comprehended proportionally of the Great Whole
it is simple, and not so much therefore an object of reason as of contact and intuition

terms.meaning: Where the Greeks arrived at an experimental conception of the Whole's reality.

quotes.text: an experimental conception of its reality in the self-knowledge

terms.meaning: Universal matter subsisting about Intelligibles, origin of all vital and corporeal existence; occult but manifestable to sense; mediates between causes and gross effects; made manifest by the Theurgic Art; connascent with the gods and a receptacle of Divinity.

quotes.text: a certain pure matter subsisting about Intelligibles which is universal
a certain pure and divine Matter mediately subsisting between primary and secondary causes and their gross effect

terms.meaning: What persists through all change of bodies, distinct from them; receives and reflects forms; matter subsists according to it.

equivalences.quote: matter according to the subject which is indefinite, because it is note form

quotes.text: that which receives the forms and reflects them --- always remains the same

terms.voice: QUOTED: Plotinus (summary gathered from Plotinus and Porphyry); endorsed by Atwood

terms.meaning: Dissolution, which belongs only to composites; especially artificial corruption manifests the underlying subject.

quotes.text: This therefore Corruption manifests (especially the artificial), for corruption is of that which is composite

terms.voice: QUOTED: Plotinus (summary gathered from Plotinus and Porphyry); endorsed by Atwood

terms.meaning: The only analysis by which a pot is resolved into gold and gold into an indissoluble water; conformable to hermetic doctrine in internal and external senses; its ultimate stage yields Light.

quotes.text: For by no other analysis either is a pot resolved into gold, or gold into a water which is indissoluble.

terms.meaning: Glossed as illuminated, by contrariation of its Form.

equivalences.quote: aurified --- that is, illuminated by contrariation of its Form

terms.meaning: Of a metal: what, under a fermentive test, passes from its own Form into a more perfect one.

quotes.text: The radical moisture of the metal likewise, obeying the fermentive virtue of such a test when applied

terms.meaning: The formal essence of all things, most abundant in gold, found in the ultimate alchemical analysis.

equivalences.quote: Light, which is the formal essence of all things, and most abundant in gold

terms.meaning: In the analysis, the incorruptible, indissoluble end-product into which gold and metals are reduced; the first pure matter of metals.

equivalences.quote: all metals, likewise, may be reduced into water, that is, into their first pure matter

quotes.text: the water, being incorruptible, will require no analogous process

terms.meaning: Matter as the formless subject, opposed to form; not to be despised when it applies itself to things prior, i.e. the divine exemplaries and the most excellent life.

quotes.text: This Indefinite is not therefore everywhere to be despised

terms.voice: QUOTED: Plotinus (summary gathered from Plotinus and Porphyry); endorsed by Atwood

terms.meaning: The art by which the pure divine Matter is made manifest and imparted through arcane and blessed visions.

quotes.text: by means of the Theurgic Art it is made manifest and imparted through arcane and blessed visions

terms.voice: QUOTED: Plotinus (summary gathered from Plotinus and Porphyry); endorsed by Atwood

terms.meaning: That which is referred to all things and through which they sympathize; not conceivable by ordinary rational contemplation; the soul becomes into it after the descent to nonentity; one is present with it by being present with oneself.

quotes.text: it becomes necessary simply to refer Being to all things, and all things sympathize thereby internally with each other
then he is present with true Being, which is everywhere

terms.meaning: The principle discoverable only by becoming assimilated to it; the most united in nature, through which it is Deity, uniting the universe in sympathetic consent.

quotes.text: if any one wish to discover the One Principle he must become first assimilated to it

terms.meaning: The higher of the twofold nature (intelligible and sensible); better for the soul to abide in; one is assimilated to it by being established in one's own essence.

quotes.text: And since there is a twofold nature, one intelligible and the other sensible, it is better indeed for the soul to abide in the intelligible world

terms.meaning: Ordinary reasoning, into which the soul falls back from Intellect after the divine state.

quotes.text: falling off from Intellect into the discursive energy of reason

terms.meaning: The principle the Divine experience imparts; one and all, everywhere and nowhere; uncompounded; described only by negations, an Infinity; apprehended by ablative reasoning and negation; the last and lowest effect, inverse of the First Cause; yet held to be real.

quotes.text: the Material Principle which, according to these philosophers, the Divine experience imparts
I mean, he says, by Matter, that which of itself is neither essence nor quantity, nor any one of those things, by which Being is defined
they assert this subject-matter to be somewhat; and real, notwithstanding all its inverse and irrational characteristics

terms.meaning: An error the mind is to avoid: taking the Identity of Being as heaped up or compounded rather than uncompounded.

quotes.text: that the Identity of every Being is something uncompounded, and that the mind should not fall into the error of coacervation

terms.meaning: Reflective contemplation; excluded, with multitude, when Matter is called 'one so far as one'.

equivalences.quote: depriving the idea of multitude and dual, i.e., reflective, contemplation

terms.meaning: Used in ¶53 for the subject described by negations (neither form, quality, body, reason nor bound, but a certain Infinity), in continuing the discussion of Matter; identity with Matter is not stated (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: But since the ethereal element is described by so many ablative characteristics

terms.meaning: The character of the Matter; by the principle that like knows like, apprehended only by the Indefinite, reason passing out into an undefined void of thought.

quotes.text: the Indefinite also will be apprehended by the Indefinite

terms.meaning: What the Matter is ('a certain Infinity'); eluded by thought as a circumscribing boundary.

quotes.text: but a certain Infinity
for the thought, as circumscribing boundary, eludes the Infinite

terms.meaning: Defective reasoning by negation, the means by which Matter is apprehended; describing it only by what it is not.

quotes.text: Matter is indeed to be apprehended, and that by a sort of defective or ablative reasoning

terms.meaning: In the Aristotle passage: separate subsistence as a particular thing, implying composition of subject and object; Matter is not essence. In Porphyry: one's own Essence, in which one is to be established.

quotes.text: a separate subsistence as this or that particular thing especially belongs to what we call essence, (that is to say, composition of subject and object is necessarily implied in the idea of true intelligence)
being established in yourself and in your own Essence

terms.meaning: The state reached by passing through reason beyond every bound.

equivalences.quote: that kind of ultimate ignorance, which is the Infinity of Life

terms.meaning: What the objectless mental eye becomes when all thought is submerged, as the eye becomes one with darkness; a crass, obscure vacuity; related to true Being as night to day.

equivalences.quote: that obscure oblivion which is the Original of Life

quotes.text: a crass, obscure vacuity

terms.meaning: The initial nothingness of all, shown by Parmenides and the rest; the soul does not endure to stop at it and becomes into true Being.

quotes.text: Parmenides and the rest cited to prove the same initial nonentity of all
not enduring any longer to stop at nonentity, becomes into true Being

terms.meaning: The continuum extended from infinite pure light above all intelligence down to the darkness of Matter at the opposite extreme.

equivalences.with: ladder of Celsus and of Zoroaster
equivalences.quote: this is that ladder of Celsus and of Zoroaster which reaches from Tartarus to the highest Heaven

quotes.text: the opposite extreme of the magnetic chain, which is extended a non gradu ad non gradum

terms.meaning: The top of the ascending series of causes (the 'Final Cause of all'); the lowest effect reverses its attributes; selfhood is raised into it.

quotes.text: the last and lowest effect, in which all the attributes of the First Cause are not only deficient but reversed

terms.meaning: The condition of the mind beholding Matter: suffering the reception of the formless, perceiving obscurely, vastly, infinitely; feeling without understanding.

quotes.text: When therefore the mind is in the Night of Matter

terms.meaning: Matter as perceived in the Night of Matter; obscure, vast and infinite. Also called, in the same passage, the Abyssal Subject into which the intellect sinks (no identity asserted outright).

quotes.text: her perception of the Formless Subject is obscure, and vast, and infinite
sinking into the Abyssal Subject

terms.meaning: Into whose 'bosom' Intellect descends when it perceives the Formless Subject.

quotes.text: descending into the bosom of the Mysteries

terms.meaning: The soul's last remaining unity, about which it rallies when it retracts from nonentity.

quotes.text: rallying about her last deserted Unit

terms.meaning: Possible only when every other knowledge is removed.

quotes.text: Self-knowledge is impossible unless every other knowledge is deprived

terms.meaning: The self that is obliterated in the attraction into the First Cause; in ¶59 'non-being' is glossed as the subjective selfhood, whose additions bring poverty.

equivalences.quote: anything is added from non-n\being (i.e., from the subjective selfhood)

quotes.text: as this selfhood likewise is obliterated in the overwhelming attraction, which raises it into the First Cuase

terms.meaning: The moment when extremes are present and Light springs forth out of the abyssal Darkness.

quotes.text: extremes are said to be present at the new birth, when Light springs forth to manifestation out of the abyssal Darkness

terms.meaning: The abyssal Darkness brought forth by God to give contrasting substance to His revelation; the one substance God created in the beginning; without affirmation, not known in energy, fleeing one who intently beholds it; unknown or known as nothing; present but unperceived by self-active striving.

equivalences.quote: the abyssal Darkness, which is then alone before its Creator; and is brought forth by Him for a First Matter

equivalences.with: unam substantiam (one substance created by God)
equivalences.quote: Creavit unam substantiam, Hanc primam materiam nominamus.

equivalences.with: very natural true sperm of the greater world
equivalences.quote: it was the First Matter and very natural true sperm of the greater world

equivalences.with: water of our sea; water of life
equivalences.quote: This same, Sendivogius in his New Light, calls the water of our sea, the water of life, not wetting the hands

quotes.text: the First Matter, which cannot either receive the appellation of Being, since it is not known in energy, but flies from him, indeed, who wishes intently to behold

terms.meaning: Used of the First Matter (in the beginning without all affirmation) and of the Eternal Essence perceived intellectually.

quotes.text: such an hypostasis is in the beginning without all affirmation
begin to perceive intellectually an hypostasis unwearied, untamed, and never failing

terms.meaning: An essence infinite in power, self-established, self-sufficient, seeking nothing but itself; nothing can be added to it, and adding place or relation diminishes it.

quotes.text: When you have assumed to yourself an Eternal Essence, says Prophyry, infinite in itself according to power
it is much more sufficient than any perpetually flowing fountain can be conceived to be

terms.meaning: That which is present with a man himself; presence with it, and absence from the external, is presence with true Being.

equivalences.with: that which is present with himself
equivalences.quote: to be present with that which is present with himself, that is to say, with his rational part

terms.meaning: That in which contraries (small and great, deficient and exceeding) always consubsist.

quotes.text: contraries are always consubsistent in the Divine Original

terms.meaning: Something passive to intellect as a mirror is to images, subsisting without any imagination; felt, not known. The Passive Nature is said to be 'a thing of this kind'.

quotes.text: so is this ethereal glass to intellect, subsisting according to processure and in defect of all imagination

terms.meaning: The pure, indeterminate receptive nature that should reflect the Divine Light without refraction or mixed images; identified as the Alchemists' Matter.

equivalences.with: the Matter so often celebrated by the Alchemists
equivalences.quote: Such was the Matter so often celebrated by the Alchemists

quotes.text: And the Passive Nature ought indeed to be a thing of this kind, pure and indeterminate

terms.meaning: The pure passive subject celebrated by the Alchemists. Not found in the natural world; discovered only by Life and the Fire of Intellect.

equivalences.quote: the Matter so often celebrated by the Alchemists, the Quintessence of Plato
the Water of Thales
the Non-Being of Parmenides
that Abyss of the Kabalists, styled also by them Unknown, Void, Nothing, Infinite

quotes.text: For in the natural world there is no such Matter to be found
discovers the True matter of the adepts

terms.meaning: The Kabalists' name for the Matter, which they also call Unknown, Void, Nothing and Infinite.

equivalences.quote: that Abyss of the Kabalists, styled also by them Unknown, Void, Nothing, Infinite

terms.meaning: What remains to one who passes beyond all things: what is prior to all things.

equivalences.with: That which is prior to all things
equivalences.quote: is That which is prior to all things, and the First Matter

terms.meaning: That by which the Matter returns 'in the Freed Will' to consciousness and manifests the Supreme Cause. Not further explained in this chunk.

quotes.text: returning by its Rational Boundary in the Freed Will to consciousness

terms.meaning: That which true generation would simply represent. Nothing in nature is generated so as to represent it alone.

quotes.text: simply so as to represent the Formal Agent alone

terms.meaning: The originals from which things beheld in nature are derived; natural phenomena do not truly resemble them. In III.2 ¶66, what one established in Intellect beholds through it 'as an image'.

quotes.text: If indeed things beheld in nature were such as the Archetypes, whence they are derived
able through it, as an image, to behold the Archetype

terms.meaning: The magical bond that shuts up Nature's Inner Light and principle of perfection. Nature cannot loosen it herself.

quotes.text: the bond of coagulation by which her Inner Light and principle of perfection is everywhere shut up

terms.meaning: Nature's principle of perfection, shut up by the bond of coagulation.

equivalences.quote: her Inner Light and principle of perfection

terms.meaning: The dissolution which, with human aid, enables the Spirit to leave its extraneous forms.

quotes.text: Without the magical solution and human aid to fortify

terms.meaning: The agent that discovers the True matter: the Fire of Intellect, sublimed and fortified in its efficient source.

equivalences.quote: no other Fire but that of Intellect

terms.meaning: The life-spirit whose dissolution, and the alienation of its natural bind, discovers the True matter.

quotes.text: a dissolution of the Vital Spirit and alienation of its natural bind

terms.meaning: Where 'the strength of sin' lies. Not explained further in this chunk.

quotes.text: the strength of sin is in the Law of dual generation

terms.meaning: The art whose whole performance is comprehended in solution, sublimation and fixation.

quotes.text: All that is performed in the Proto-chemic artifice may be comprehended in three terms

terms.meaning: The operation that dissolves and liquefies the included Spirit.

quotes.text: Solution dissolves and liquifies the included Spirit

terms.meaning: The operation that volatilizes and washes the Spirit.

quotes.text: sublimation volatilizes and washes it

terms.meaning: The third operation: after calcinations, a reunion into a more permanent form of Being.

quotes.text: after calcinations there is a reunion into a more permanent form of Being

terms.meaning: A step preceding the reunion into permanent form. Not defined further in this chunk.

quotes.text: after calcinations there is a reunion

terms.meaning: What Hermes suffered and toiled to obtain. Not otherwise explained.

quotes.text: to obtain the blessed Lunary of Diana, he had suffered much, and toiled incessantly

terms.meaning: The subject of the work, in which the ass's qualities must be found if it is to carry out the Divine behests.

quotes.text: very applicable and necessary to be found in the Philosophic Subject

terms.meaning: That on which the ass's influence occultly depends, glossed as Hochma.

equivalences.quote: Sephiroth, i.e., Hochma

terms.meaning: The interior of the temple, which the Aspirant enters after leaving all the statues behind; an image of the mind entertaining the simple Unity of Light within.

quotes.text: the Aspirant entering into the interior to behold the Adytum, leaves behind him all the statues in the temple

terms.meaning: Association not with an image but with the reality images represent; afterwards the mind's prior content recurs exalted and multiplied.

quotes.text: subsequent to the Divine Union, there recurs That also which was in the mind prior to the union, exalted and multiplied

terms.meaning: A state in which, while it lasts, subject and object are not two in consciousness; the life understanding and the light understood are one.

quotes.text: as in the Divine conjunction, whilst it lasts, there are not two things as of subject and object in the consciousness

terms.meaning: That with which one becomes One by mingling, keeping a remnant of it.

quotes.text: whoever thus becomes One by mingling with the Efficient, will have a remnant of it with himself

terms.meaning: Light shining primarily in itself, illuminating and illuminated at once; the foundation of every intellect, which primarily knows itself.

equivalences.quote: this First Light, which is the foundation of every intellect and primarily knows itself

quotes.text: at one and the same time illuminates and is illuminated

terms.meaning: A power that was alienated and is reunited to mind by the primary motion of the ebbing life.

quotes.text: the Generative Virtue, which was alienated, becomes re- united to mind

terms.meaning: Reason turning back on itself: logic is bounded about it, the experiment effects it; strictly followed, both reach the First Source.

quotes.text: reason becomes bounded about its own inversion

terms.meaning: Named in the chapter heading as what is manifested and 'informed' by Light; not otherwise defined in this chunk.

quotes.text: Of the Manifestation of the First Matter, and its Information by Light.

terms.meaning: That which, purified through sacrifice of foreign attractions, revolves about its center with active and passive power united, about to generate its fullness.

quotes.text: the Vital Spirit theurgically purified and freed through sacrifice of all foreign attractions

terms.meaning: Principles that subsist even in their extreme separation by Art.

quotes.text: His marvelous subsistence of the Vital Principles in their extreme separation by Art

terms.meaning: 'Hypostatic union' of active and passive power in the Vital Spirit; 'hypostatic principles' of attraction, repulsion and circulation; a 'new hypostasis' is created out of darkness at the Soul's return.

quotes.text: the hypostatic principles of attraction and repulsion and circulation
a new hypostasis is created out of the darkness to abide

terms.meaning: The blessed Water nature sheds, contemplated in the vestibule of the first Adytum.

equivalences.quote: the Tears of Isis, even that blessed Water which nature sheds divinely for the world

terms.meaning: Sanctuary approached; the first one has a vestibule where the Tears of Isis are contemplated.

quotes.text: to the gate of the first Adytum

terms.meaning: Bringing attraction, repulsion and circulation into equilibrium in the ethereal bond.

quotes.text: great care and diligence is needed at this juncture to apply the threefold secret of the Art

terms.meaning: The 'new Chaos' of universal nature that appears unfolded and separated when the process is rightly done.

quotes.text: the new Chaos of the Universal Nature

terms.meaning: Something to be touched and seen which, with internal and external fire, suffices for the Stone.

equivalences.quote: thou shalt see Azoth! The Universal!

terms.meaning: A fire with which the internal and external fire must be in sympathy; not defined.

quotes.text: in harmonious sympathy with the Olympic Fire

terms.meaning: Spoken of as 'herself'; by returning faith and desire it draws the Soul back into itself at the extreme of tribulation.

quotes.text: the returning faith and desire of the Passive Spirit attracts the Soul again into herself

terms.meaning: Atwood's 'chain of the magnetic series' moves when the Soul is drawn back into the Passive Spirit.

quotes.text: the first link in the chain of the magnetic series moves

terms.meaning: Name the cited French source gives to the work of repeated cooking until the rainbow colours and heavy drops appear ('magnetic', our translation). The chunk does not link it to Atwood's 'magnetic series' (III.3 ¶10).

quotes.text: Cet ouvrage s’appelle Aimantique

terms.meaning: Divine command that blesses the union of Soul and Passive Spirit; the sensual dominant is occultated and subdued in it.

quotes.text: the Divine Fiat comes mercifully to bless the union
when the sensual dominant is occultated in the Divine Fiat and subdued

terms.meaning: The 'ethereal bond' in which the three principles are balanced (¶9); the 'liquid crystal of the understanding ether' in which the fiery soul is held and its light shines (¶10); the 'simple Understanding of its ether', identified with non-being, to which Thought unites (¶15). ¶13 also uses 'apparent ether' of the sky.

equivalences.quote: unites itself to the non-being, or simple Understanding of its ether

quotes.text: the liquid crystal of the understanding ether
in the ethereal bond

terms.meaning: Drawn by subtle operations from the vitriol left after the conjunction of Mars and Venus.

equivalences.quote: un souphre solaire ou or philosophique vivant

terms.meaning: The union (of Mars and Venus, ¶11) during which a spirituous vapour rises; in ¶13 its 'various hours' bring Darkness, Saturn, the Head of the Crow.

quotes.text: in the various hours of conjunction

terms.meaning: Listed with Darkness, Night, Saturn, the Antimony of the Wise and Obscurity as present in the hours of conjunction; not defined.

quotes.text: Obscurity and the Head of the Crow in the various hours of conjunction

terms.meaning: Listed among the dark presences of conjunction; not defined.

quotes.text: Night, Saturn and the Antimony of the Wise will be present

terms.meaning: With Iris, the appearance of all colours after darkness; a token of reconciliation.

quotes.text: all the colours of the world will be apparent; also Iris, God’s messenger, and the tail of the peacock

terms.meaning: Where the rainbow-token of reconciliation appears, by analogy with the sky after storm.

quotes.text: the same beautiful token of reconciliation is made apparent in the Microcosmic Heaven

terms.meaning: Under which all is sown and fire and water fall together and germinate; under it true Wisdom comes (¶14, our translation); linked to the 'crucifixion of the cerebral life'.

quotes.text: All is sown under the cross and completed in its number
out of the crucifixion of the cerebral life

terms.meaning: Union of Mind and Universe: solitary Thought uniting with the simple Understanding of its ether; prefigured by ancient mythic marriages.

equivalences.with: union of Mind and Universe (Mentis et Universi)
equivalences.quote: This is the union supersentient, the nuptials sublime, Mentis et Universi

quotes.text: the bridegroom crowneth the bride in the North

terms.meaning: The dominance of the senses, subdued in the Divine Fiat and overcome by Spirit in regeneration; identified with the corporeal.

equivalences.quote: overcomes the corporeal, which is the sensual dominant, in the regeneration

quotes.text: when the sensual dominant is occultated in the Divine Fiat and subdued

terms.meaning: Water with which sublimed arsenic and calcined mercury are ground; carries the entry of life and light into them.

quotes.text: the Water of Myght, Which beareth ingression of Lyfe and Light

terms.meaning: The adept's water, taken from higher places, not wells, as ripe Mercury rises.

quotes.text: Our golden water, says the adept, is not found in wells, nor in profundities, but in higher places

terms.meaning: Feminine ('her'); when ripe rises to her superior habitation; in ¶16 calcined with arsenic; in ¶21 congealed by the dissolved body (our translation).

quotes.text: for Mercury, being ripe, arises to her superior habitation

terms.meaning: Drawn dry without moisture from the Fountain by the Crowned King; not defined.

quotes.text: drawing from thence the Auripigment, dry without moisture

terms.meaning: The consummation; speaks of itself as earth-bodied and fire-empowered (¶8, our translation); appears after ashy, white and yellow as a glorified King, a shining carbuncle.

equivalences.quote: thou shalt behold the Stone oft eh Philosophers; our King and Lord of hosts go forth

quotes.text: as a shining carbuncle, most temperate in splendour

terms.meaning: The dissolved body, said to be a perennial water congealing Mercury (our translation only).

equivalences.quote: Corpus solutum est aqua perennis congelans Mercurium perpetua congelatione.

terms.meaning: What must be destroyed as seed to be multiplied; saving it means resting in the first fruits of reason.

equivalences.quote: he that saves his gold, that is to say, remains satisfied in the first fruits of his reason

terms.meaning: The assimilating ferment by which bodies are transformed, spiritualized and preserved; the old leaven is to be purged.

equivalences.quote: preserved by the assimilating must or leaven

quotes.text: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump

terms.meaning: Once discovered and set in motion, actuates the Spirit, which then overcomes the corporeal.

quotes.text: The Rational Light, once discovered and set in motion, actuates the Spirit

terms.meaning: The vessel containing fire, air and water in the work.

equivalences.quote: in their earthly vessel, i.e., in their gross body or composition

terms.meaning: The Monk's fire, which excites the elemental fire as the matter desires a fitting Form; contrasted with coals and common fire.

quotes.text: For I have my heavenly fire, which excites and stirs up the elemental one

terms.meaning: Monk: the incombustible sulphur heats or thickens the cold, crude quicksilver until they are one body. Boehme: the virtue in the red fire-form.

equivalences.quote: which is red, and therein the virtue, viz., sulphur is

terms.voice: QUOTED: the Benedictine Monk; Jacob Boehme

the original in the blood, viz., fire, which is its warmth, is life

terms.meaning: Proceeds in the virtue of the warmth (fire) in the blood.

quotes.text: in the virtue of the warmth, the Thin Water of Life proceedeth

terms.meaning: That with which the resigned Spirit is clothed; it qualifies and sanctifies the true Adept.

equivalences.quote: It is this material of the Corner-Stone which links reason to Divinity

quotes.text: And this Essentiality it is which qualifies the true Adept

terms.meaning: The self as likeness of its divine source, to be reflected into for self-knowledge; the soul passes from herself as image to the Archetype.

quotes.text: that great and miraculous mystery of our Image
passes from himself as an image to the Archetype

terms.meaning: The original of which the self is image; end of the soul's progression; the creative mind whose Law of Light orders all things causally and which 'shadows the intellectual spheres'.

quotes.text: where the Archetype shadows the intellectual spheres
that which is in the Archetypal mind creatively efficient

terms.meaning: That with which the soul associates and of which she gains a similitude; her cause.

quotes.text: the soul, being in such a condition, associates with her Efficient

by a transmutation of the hypostatic relations

terms.meaning: The material efflux of the soul; differs from the aerial spirit in constitution only, not in nature.

equivalences.quote: the aura or material efflux of the soul

terms.meaning: The goal, unattainable without sanctified mind, purified soul and union with God.

quotes.text: it is impossible for you to attain this immortal essentiality

quotes.text: a conversion of the elements in this respect is just to make active passive and passive active
