terms.meaning: That from which the articulate voice proceeding from Spirit comes.

quotes.text: a voice which rolls forth in distinct utterance articulate, for It comes from the Mind

terms.meaning: That of which all Nature is the Efflux; Thought emanates it; the recreation is a birth into it; reason is to become a bright Light.

quotes.text: that Light, of which all Nature is the Efflux
Thought emanating Light
a stupendous metaphysical birth out of the Infinite into Light
reason BECOMING A BRIGHT Light

terms.meaning: The one with whom Atwood asks whether anyone can 'move One' and be His Will; at once the Antecedent and Final Cause of all.

equivalences.with: Antecedent and Final Cause of all
equivalences.quote: the First Mover, and Be His Will, who is at once the Antecedent and Final Cause of all

quotes.text: to move One with the First Mover, and Be His Will, who is at once the Antecedent and Final Cause of all

terms.meaning: What cannot be attained, entertained or thought self-actively by those living profanely without self-knowledge.

quotes.text: attain to the Divine Idea; either to entertain or think It self-actively is impossible

terms.meaning: That which contains all things; most capacious, swift and powerful.

quotes.text: Consider that which contains all things
it is most capacious, most swift, and most strong

terms.meaning: What everything is; hence the divine way proper to the Good meets one everywhere.

quotes.text: For there is nothing which is not the Image of God

terms.meaning: Hidden and 'slain from the foundation' in the fiat of our Identity; its occultation is in two diametrically reverse poles or principles. Not otherwise defined.

quotes.text: the exemplary Logos is hidden, --- slain from the foundation in the exterminating fiat of our Identity

terms.meaning: Used specially for our individual selfhood, whose 'exterminating fiat' hides the exemplary Logos.

quotes.text: the exterminating fiat of our Identity

terms.meaning: The origin to which life is led back from created individuality; its arrival is described as a return to its First Source.

quotes.text: from the manifest created individuality, back into the Initial germ
returns to refund its treasury again its First Source

terms.meaning: Hailed as a 'most mighty and surpassing magic' right after the account of life's return to its source; not defined.

quotes.text: Most mighty and surpassing magic of Reflection.

terms.meaning: Addressed as the august Mother of all things; at the Substant Unity 'Experience is present with Power'.

equivalences.quote: And thou august Mother of all things, Divine Experience.

quotes.text: where Experience is present with Power, and Effect in substance to bear them witness

terms.meaning: The affirmation in which Life feels itself to Be; by it the Kabalah signifies the Substant Unity of all that is.

equivalences.quote: in the Divine I Am, is by the Kabalah signified the Substant Unity of all that is

quotes.text: Life springs forth with motion, feeling itself to Be.

terms.meaning: The unity of all that is; fountain of Universal nature and her Exemplary Law; source of miracles, magical accordances, and every natural and supernatural increase.

equivalences.with: fountain of Universal nature and her Exemplary Law
equivalences.quote: the Substant Unity of all that is; the fountain of Universal nature and her Exemplary Law

quotes.text: the source of so many miracles and magical accordances, as of every natural and supernatural increase

terms.meaning: Universal nature's law, of which the Substant Unity is the fountain.

quotes.text: the fountain of Universal nature and her Exemplary Law

terms.meaning: A metaphysical birth out of the Infinite into Light, in which the visible springs from the invisible.

quotes.text: the recreation was seen to be a stupendous metaphysical birth out of the Infinite into Light

terms.meaning: Used specially for what the work brings to completion: it becomes a bright Light at the periphery of her fiery essence, immortal, Mistress of Life; at the end it has nothing left to doubt.

quotes.text: reason BECOMING A BRIGHT Light in the periphery of her fiery essence remains immortal, and is the Mistress of Life
leaving reason nothing more to doubt of

terms.meaning: 'Our most noble Mercury', said of what precedes (¶80); ranked against the rational soul in the same line; relation unclear (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: Hic est Mercurius noster nobillissimus

terms.meaning: The rational soul; per our translation, the line ranks it against 'our Mercury' as God's noblest creation under heaven (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: Deus nunquam creavit rem nobiliorem sub coelo praeter animam rationalem

terms.meaning: Outer and inner reality, seen at completion to blend in confluent harmony and confirm each other.

quotes.text: the External and Internal Worlds were seen to blend together in confluent harmony

terms.meaning: The law under which fulfilment is reached once outer and inner worlds agree.

quotes.text: a fulfillment under the Universal Law

terms.meaning: The art under discussion; distinct from every other branch of philosophy and requiring a naturally fitted disposition.

quotes.text: for that it is peculiar and distinct from every other branch of philosophy

terms.meaning: The art in which the nature of things is altered and reversed and Final Causes are manifest; Norton calls it holy because found only by grace.

quotes.text: But in Alchemy, where the nature of things is altogether altered and ultimately reversed
Wherefore old Fathers, conveniently, Called this science Holy Alkimy

terms.meaning: What the work is done on; all men have it and live by it, but few can handle it. Not identified further here.

quotes.text: because all men have the material and live by it

terms.meaning: The experiment of nature the Inquiry seeks to recover 'into her Causal Light'; not defined further.

quotes.text: recover the Ancient Experiment of nature into her Causal Light

terms.meaning: That into which the Ancient Experiment of nature is to be recovered; not defined in this chunk.

quotes.text: the Ancient Experiment of nature into her Causal Light

terms.meaning: The practical routine of the work, to be entered on after the impediments and endowments are set out.

quotes.text: before we enter on the routine of Practice

terms.meaning: Geber's term for natural incapacity for the work, arising from bodily defects or defects of soul.

quotes.text: Natural Impotency, he asserts, is manifold

terms.meaning: Geber's list of mental defects excluding a person: lack of sagacity, dullness, fantasy, changeability, beast-like blindness, disbelief, love of money.

quotes.text: respecting the Impediments of Mind, the Arabian continues

terms.meaning: The true root of the science, found only by a subtly searching mind.

quotes.text: cannot find the true Radix of this most precious science

terms.meaning: What fills a fanciful soul so that it cannot receive the true intention of natural things.

quotes.text: because there is replete with fumosities, it cannot receive the true intention of natural things

terms.meaning: Thorough searching investigation; its absence marks the stiff-necked.

quotes.text: void of ingenuity and every sort of perscrutination

terms.meaning: What the avaricious fear to 'interposit'. In Geber's wording the failure is covetousness of money; Atwood glosses the charges as abandoning the life of selfhood and returning the product to a benevolent and truthful end.

quotes.text: but are afraid to interposit the necessary charges
i.e., to abandon the life of selfhood, and return the product to a benevolent and truthful end

terms.meaning: 'The first and last defect'; leads either to fruitless searching in inert matter or, in Mammon's followers, to abuse of the attained power.

quotes.text: this first and last defect of Avarice

terms.meaning: The downward-looking spirit that led the depraved abusers of the work.

quotes.text: Mammon led them on; mammon that least erected sprit that fell

terms.meaning: Self-centred life, which must be abandoned as the 'necessary charges'.

quotes.text: to abandon the life of selfhood

terms.meaning: The 'forbidden regions' into which depraved minds climbed by the clue of life.

quotes.text: climbed by it into forbidden regions of self-sufficiency

terms.meaning: Something the depraved 'entangled' and climbed by into self-sufficiency; not explained here.

quotes.text: basely entangling the clue of life

terms.meaning: What the abusers succeeded in inducing before denying the Light its fulfilment; not defined further.

quotes.text: having succeeded in inducing an exalted energy

terms.meaning: Something with a 'true fulfillment' that the selfish deny and defile.

quotes.text: have willfully denied the Light its true fulfillment

terms.meaning: The soul that suffers when pressed by evil; it must be filled by a superior or an inferior power. Sense of 'subject' is open (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: And what will not the subject soul suffer when pressed by so execrable an evil?

terms.meaning: That which acts 'without intervention or concealment' throughout the work (III.4 ¶9); the 'highly effective agent' springing from ourselves, which follows directly, probably refers to it (inferred). Whether 'the Spirit' compelled to private ends (III.4 ¶6) is the same is not stated.

quotes.text: without intervention or concealment in the ministering Spirit throughout
compelling the Spirit to their private ends

terms.meaning: Ends or purposes; hidden in ordinary life, manifest in Alchemy in act as in effect; the superior power filling the soul is proximate to the Final Cause.

quotes.text: Final Causes are of all things most manifestly revealed
proximate to the Final Cause

terms.meaning: Personified ('she'); admits no impure leaven and forsakes the polluted tabernacle if anything is done against the right of nature; withheld from evil men.

quotes.text: No impure leaven (need we repeat it?) can enter into Wisdom

terms.meaning: The moral, physical and organic laws, apparently independent at the circumference of nature but one at the root.

quotes.text: the moral, the physical, and the organic are well reasoned, as in their constitutional consequences, apart from each other

terms.meaning: Nature's outer level, where things appear varied and nothing homogeneous is seen, as opposed to the root.

quotes.text: For nature at the circumference subsists in this way

terms.meaning: The pattern a work images; in ordinary arts the product shows the Idea, not the motive; in Alchemy the agent images the conceived Idea as the will directs.

quotes.text: remain to image, not the motive instigatory, but the Idea
to image the conceived Idea

terms.meaning: Degrees ('a second to a third') through which the agent is promoted and fortified; not explained further.

quotes.text: when promoted through a second to a third of concentration

terms.meaning: That in which the agent further multiplies (Atwood); Norton separately speaks of 'God's conjunctions' which man may not undo without grace.

quotes.text: further multiplying in the Conjunction
For God’s conjunctions man my not undoe

terms.meaning: The law exacting exact retribution ('eye for an eye') in the spheres of the work.

quotes.text: so does the Law of Justice exact retribution in those spheres

terms.meaning: What secrecy ensured could be discovered only through long labour of an experienced, upright mind.

quotes.text: that the Power might only be discovered through the long labour of an experienced and upright mind

terms.meaning: That upon which deviating profane persons may break or be broken; not explained.

quotes.text: become broken necessitiously upon the Wheel of Life

terms.meaning: The philosophers' withholding of truth from fools and the vicious, not from the just.

quotes.text: For this reason are the philosophers said to be envious

terms.meaning: Capitalized for that with which one may be 'really conversant' in the work; not defined here.

quotes.text: really conversant with the Subject

terms.meaning: 'The tincture of holi Alkimy', called marvellous; not defined further.

quotes.text: Is the tincture of holi Alkimy;

terms.meaning: Divine gift by which alone the science is found; the student must be proved able to receive it; needed to undo God's conjunctions.

quotes.text: A singular grace and gift of the Almightye;
But only by grace, she is holy in her kind.

terms.meaning: Reason as the guide of the pursuit: under it every step is progressive, it alone can enter the true Form of Gold, and its province is to prove all things.

quotes.text: every step is progressive where the Rule of Reason is pursued
Reason alone can enter into it
It is the province of reason to inquire and endeavor, by perscrutination, to prove all things

terms.meaning: The real object of Alchemy's 'golden promise', which avarice, ambition or curiosity cannot reach; only Reason enters it. Contrasted with 'the dead metal'. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: neither will be found to be the true Form of Gold

terms.meaning: A living gold-producing seed that must be 'quickened in life'; contrasted with dead metal. The covetous spirit cannot quicken it. Not further explained here.

quotes.text: it cannot quicken the aurific seed in life

terms.meaning: Personified as feminine. Her 'fiery ordeal' and 'pure Light' repel the covetous; one is 'introduced into this hidden Wisdom' by moral qualification.

quotes.text: he is the first to fly from Wisdom’s fiery ordeal
who would be introduced into this hidden Wisdom

terms.meaning: Fashionable faithlessness that without rational foundation denounces everything new or unfamiliar and believes nothing worthy of belief or veneration; perhaps the most absurd obstacle to human advancement.

quotes.text: by infidelity, we mean that fashionable kind of faithlessness, which, without rational foundation, denounces everything that is new

terms.meaning: Those Geber condemns next above the Covetous; they remain ignorant by choice and hinder others. Modern skeptics 'ape' sound reason. Their skepticism is the 'mock ally' of rational skepticism.

quotes.text: next above the Covetous, Skeptics are condemned by Geber

terms.meaning: Reason's inquiry that proves all things, rejecting the false and holding the true; required of the Hermetic Student.

equivalences.quote: Such skepticism, more properly perhaps called discrimination

quotes.text: Rational skepticism has quite another object and never exhibits itself in the refractory form of its mock ally.

terms.meaning: The searching examination by which reason proves all things.

quotes.text: It is the province of reason to inquire and endeavor, by perscrutination, to prove all things

terms.meaning: The door Nature opens to the multitude, relieving suffering and offering 'a new guide to knowledge and felicity'; the Door-keeper that first introduced Atwood to the vestibule of antique science.

equivalences.quote: We allude to Mesmerism: not ashamed, but grateful to acknowledge the neglected Door-keeper

quotes.text: the neglected Door-keeper that gave us first introduction to the vestibule of antique science

terms.meaning: The only one to whom Nature surrenders her casket: disciplined in her schools, tried and proven able to bear the sacred trust.

quotes.text: she will surrender to none but a philosopher, one too that has been disciplined in her schools

terms.meaning: The science and Art in question. God grants it to few; its records hold the inner sense aloof from the literal; it will probably stay concealed for ages.

quotes.text: Yet is this science of Alkimy full trew;
the Art will probably continue concealed though many ages still

terms.meaning: The theory acquired by reading, which calls for the same faculties as the later experimental proof.

quotes.text: in acquiring the Hermetic doctrine, by perusal, as is afterwards needed for the experimental proof

terms.meaning: The practical stage of the art, following study of the doctrine.

quotes.text: as is afterwards needed for the experimental proof

terms.meaning: The single path toward which all Hermetic treatises direct, 'when this is found'. Not otherwise defined here.

quotes.text: all directing on the same Royal Road when this is found

terms.meaning: The hidden meaning of the alchemical records, kept apart from their literal sense.

quotes.text: In almost all the records of Alchemy, the inner sense is held aloof from the literal

terms.meaning: The goal one passes into 'by a living experience'; also the 'abstruse light of Alchemy', not perceptible to the gross intelligence of the many. In Eirenaeus' allegory, the narrator's light, contrasted with the false light of the darkness.

quotes.text: progressively passing by a living experience into the Light
the abstruse light of Alchemy is not fir for the understanding of all

terms.meaning: Desire directed to its object, especially to God for wisdom; it collects the mind and, joined with labour ('cooperation'), brings revelation. Esoterically it has 'a far deeper sense' and works within the operations; Iamblicus distinguishes three classes leading to union and Divine Fire.

equivalences.quote: for if you burn with a great desire of knowing them, that is prayer
It likewise is the Divine Key which opens to men the penetralia of Wisdom

quotes.text: every desire of the mind is in its kind a prayer and preparative for the acquirement of its object
But the esoteric ground brings us acquainted with prayer in a far deeper sense
prayer especially, which is its principle exercise, is profitable for great undertakings

terms.meaning: The longing of the mind for its object; the research is 'wrapped in and about' it and made manifest through it; every desire is a kind of prayer; prayer enlarges it.

quotes.text: a research which is so much wrapped in and about the Desire as to be ultimately made manifest through its means
(by enlarging the desire)

terms.meaning: The One Leader able to deliver the veiled spirit and intention; strengthened in practice, then raised to the 'allegoric siege of life' and kindled to overcome the stronghold of evil there.

equivalences.quote: there is but One Leader, who should undertake the deliverance; one only, we repeat; he that is allied --- the same Rational Light

terms.meaning: Called 'allegoric'; that to which the Rational Light is raised and where it overcomes 'the stronghold of evil'. Not further explained here.

quotes.text: afterwards is raised to the allegoric siege of life

terms.meaning: What is perfected and corrupted; full knowledge of this is the goal of study.

quotes.text: a plenary knowledge of the verity of perfecting and corrupting Matter and Form

terms.meaning: Something overthrown by the enigmas, in a sentence about study wiping off ignorance. Not defined.

quotes.text: by these enigmas the Dagon is overthrown

terms.meaning: The practical work, to which the Hand is extended only after reading the philosophers and praying.

quotes.text: before thou extendest thy Hand to the Philosophic Work

terms.meaning: Means that must be employed besides prayer.

quotes.text: Mediums nevertheless are to be employed

terms.meaning: The means through which God grants the art: instruction and the labour of the hands.

quotes.text: but always by mediate dispositions, to wit, by instructions and the labour of the hands

terms.voice: QUOTED: the author of the Lucerna Salis

terms.meaning: The source of Wisdom, referred to as 'His', to be applied to by prayer as one applies to a master of an art.

quotes.text: the Causal Fountain for Wisdom, which is His alone and voluntarily to bestow

terms.meaning: The only way to be made partaker of the Divinity one aspires to.

quotes.text: no otherwise can we be made partakers, it is taught, but by a voluntary assimilation

terms.meaning: What man can do: prepare conditions by patient disciplined labour, without being able to compel the Divine blessing.

quotes.text: Man may conditionate: --- ought, by patient labour disciplining, to prepare the way of the Greater in the Lesser Good

terms.meaning: Man prepares the way of the Greater in the Lesser Good; the Lesser is blessed by the Greater.

quotes.text: to prepare the way of the Greater in the Lesser Good
the Lesser is blessed by the Greater

terms.meaning: Something man cannot cement or increase by himself.

quotes.text: neither cement the spiritual union or give it increase

terms.meaning: A period in which the Spirit transcends earthly control and recreates under the Divine Hand alone.

quotes.text: There is a period too, when in conjunction, the Spirit transcends all earthly control

terms.meaning: A seed taken out of a body; contains Sol, Lune, Life, Light, Water, Earth, Fire and 'Fryght'; set against common gold and silver.

quotes.text: But a sperme owte of a body I take,
In the which is alle, Sol, Lune, Life and Light, Water and Erth, Fyre and Fryght:

terms.meaning: What 'maketh the marriage'. Not explained here.

quotes.text: But the Water of the Wood, maketh the marriage.

terms.meaning: Named among the contents of the seed; not explained.

quotes.text: In the which is alle, Sol, Lune, Life and Light

terms.meaning: Named among the contents of the seed; not explained.

quotes.text: In the which is alle, Sol, Lune, Life and Light

terms.meaning: Works in which, esoterically, adepts credit prayer's efficacy 'when the mind is lifted up'. Not further defined.

quotes.text: adepts are eloquent in their imputations of its efficacy in Spagyric Works, when the mind is lifted up

terms.meaning: Operations 'full of labour and toil', in the midst of which adepts prayed. Not further defined.

quotes.text: even in the midst of the operations of Vital Chemistry, full of labour and toil, they prayed

terms.meaning: The mental labour of turning the mind variously to the problem alongside prayer, so that prayer is not 'a tempting of God'.

equivalences.with: variously discussing and meditating many things
equivalences.quote: when you incline your mind to this or that, variously discussing and meditating many things, this is cooperation

terms.meaning: The sudden arrival of a solution after persistent desire and labour, received only by one who prays with great desire and labour.

equivalences.quote: at length, in a moment, the solution will fall in; this is a revelation

terms.meaning: The veiled teaching and its hidden meaning, whose solution comes by desire and labour; the first class of prayer seeks entry into its 'intelligible profundity'; unfolding it opens 'the mystery of all things'.

quotes.text: seeking a clue whereby it may enter the intelligible profundity of the Enigma
which were not the solution of the Enigma, the solution itself arose

terms.meaning: Ancient rites in which different kinds of invocation were used; Atwood draws on them to defend prayer.

quotes.text: the different kinds of invocation which were employed by the ancients in their celebration of Theurgic rites

terms.meaning: The first class of prayer, of the early initiations; gathers the mental powers into accord with their leader; pertains to Illumination.

quotes.text: was called Collective, having for its object to gather the mental powers into accord with their leader

terms.meaning: What the first class of prayer pertains to.

quotes.text: The first, recapitulates our author, pertains to Illumination

terms.meaning: What the second class of prayer pertains to; that class effects the bonds of concordant spirits before intellectual alliance.

quotes.text: the second, to a Communion of Operation

terms.meaning: Received in perfect plenitude through the energy of the third class of prayer, the final seal of union.

quotes.text: through the energy of the third, we receive a perfect plenitude of Divine Fire

terms.meaning: What prayer expels: 'whatever is prone to generation' is set alongside 'the dregs of mortality'.

quotes.text: expels whatever is prone to generation, and retains nothing of the dregs of mortality

terms.meaning: Connected with sacrifice and bound up with the advantages of prayer. Its 'three terms' contain all the Divine measures, reconcile the warring elements of life and give three supernal benefits. Its end is where rational inquiry rests and true love is found.

quotes.text: these three terms of adoration, in which, according to the authorities, all the Divine measures are contained
And thus the end of all adoration is attained

terms.meaning: Sacrifice whose end is conjunction with the Demiurgic Intellect. It is connected with adoration and prayer.

quotes.text: the end of Theurgic sacrifice is a conjunction with the Demiurgic Intellect

terms.meaning: That with which Theurgic sacrifice seeks conjunction. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: a conjunction with the Demiurgic Intellect

terms.meaning: An image for the three offspring or supernal benefits that Life brings forth and sacrifices at each passage from one form of perfection to another.

quotes.text: as it were three Hesperian Apples of Gold

terms.meaning: The inner place within which effectual desire is addressed from the Divine Light within. Not further defined here.

quotes.text: addressed within the Living Temple from the Divine Light within

terms.meaning: Wakes to consciousness in the congress of allied mind. Its diversified parts are made one in the renascent harmony. It cannot increase without a medium and a bond. It finally constructs and vitrifies its own vessel and proves which instruments are fit.

quotes.text: the Spirit wakes to consciousness
these diversified parts of the Spirit are in the renascent harmony made one
The Spirit finally constructs its own vessel and vitrifies it
as by the Spirit they are proved fit

terms.meaning: That toward which even Matter extends.

equivalences.quote: extended to the desirable, i.e., to the Good

terms.meaning: The fullness that Matter and other things reach through desire of the Good. In it they become tranquil and are freed from parturitions and natural desire.

quotes.text: when things have run up so far as to this Sufficience they become tranquil in it

terms.meaning: The stage in which every faculty of the mind must be duly exercised and no part of the concord omitted.

quotes.text: deny any faculty of the mind its due exercise in the Preparation

terms.meaning: Has a corroborative efficacy when it acts in concert with its Final Cause to fulfil it.

quotes.text: the corroborative efficacy of the Human Will, acting in concert with its Final Cause to fulfill it

terms.meaning: What the student must find in order to begin operations: something to work with that reciprocates the design. Without it the work stays abortive. It is discussed as 'suitable assistance'.

quotes.text: without a Subject to work with and reciprocate the design it remains abortive

terms.meaning: Required for any increase of the Spirit.

quotes.text: neither is there any increase of the Spirit, as we have already shown, without a medium and a bond

terms.meaning: The vessel of the work. Writers describe its apparatus as 'of nerves, veins, and alembics'. It is best when it accords with the 'vessel of nature', is finally constructed and vitrified by the Spirit, and is called 'oracular'.

quotes.text: the Philosophic Vessel and its multiform distillatory apparatus, of nerves, veins, and alembics
She that concordeth with vessel of nature

terms.meaning: The vessel material that keeps spiritual matters from escaping. Norton's Master names it as the vessel God gave. The better kind is 'morning stuffe' and the harder kind is 'Freton'. Vaughan says 'the glass is one'.

equivalences.quote: Si Deus non dedisset nobis vas Nihil dedisset, and that is glasse

quotes.text: But other vessels be made of glasse, That spiritual matters should not outpasse
the glass is one, and no more

terms.meaning: Clay that has undergone great roasting. Mixed as powder with good raw clay, it withstands fire.

quotes.text: Dead clay is called such a thing, As hath suffered great roasting

terms.meaning: The harder kind of glass, made from clippings of other glasses.

quotes.text: The harder stuffe is called Freton, Of clipping of other glasses it come

terms.meaning: The preliminary stage. Few of the many called at first are chosen to proceed beyond it. Norton describes the ministers employed about it.

quotes.text: few, it will be understood, are chosen to proceed beyond the exigencies of the preliminary Gross Work
the needful qualification and numbers of individuals employed about the Gross Work

terms.meaning: A practice Atwood will discuss later, where the value of assistance will be clearer. Norton describes it.

quotes.text: when we come to speak of the Preparatory Practice which Norton, naively, and without much envy, describes

terms.meaning: Agreement or fit between the art and its requisites. Norton numbers them: the Second Concord concerns apt ministers, the Fourth convenient places, and he also speaks of concord of art with instrument. Atwood herself uses 'concord' for the joining of prayer, self-sacrifice and the mind's faculties (III.4 ¶28).

quotes.text: The Second Concord with this Arte is,
Without full concord of arte with hys instrument
The Fourth Concord is full notable Between this arte and places convenable

terms.meaning: The assistants who carry on the work, with listed moral and practical qualifications, numbers and conduct.

quotes.text: When ye can finde apt Ministers
Noe Minister is apt to this intent But he is sober, wise, and diligent

terms.meaning: An instrument of the work. The old writers devised one for every part, many of them wrongly. The true one is a little simple shell carried in one hand.

equivalences.quote: Geber calls this furnace Athanor

quotes.text: The true furnace has been described as a little simple shell

terms.meaning: Its 'excitation' is a trivial, almost ridiculous thing, yet it contains all the secrets of corruption and generation. Not otherwise explained here.

quotes.text: the excitation of the Fire is a very trivial, slight, almost a ridiculous thing

terms.meaning: Indeterminate instruments serve at the beginning. Determinate ones 'declare themselves' when the Spirit proves them fit. This is Atwood's account of what Norton shows.

quotes.text: indeterminate instruments must be employed in the beginning, until the determinate shall declare themselves as by the Spirit they are proved fit

terms.meaning: The one with whose constitution and instinct the conditions of the work vary; not further defined here.

quotes.text: which vary with the constitution and instinct of the spiritual guide

terms.meaning: The person in trance, susceptible to imaginative impressions that linger in the place.

quotes.text: the entranced Subject is more or less susceptible of all imaginative impressures

terms.meaning: The connection the work requires: disturbed by air currents; communion 'with superiors' needs a heavenly way of life.

quotes.text: Strong currents of air are well known to disturb communion
otherwise thou canst have no communion with superiors

terms.meaning: Impressions of the imagination which persist in a place after their act and pollute its ether.

quotes.text: even after their act has passed away, hang and pollute the ether of their pertinacious abode

terms.meaning: Something belonging to a place, which lingering imaginative impressions can pollute.

quotes.text: pollute the ether of their pertinacious abode

terms.meaning: The 'ultimate' work to which 'the practice' refers.

equivalences.quote: the practice (that is of the ultimate Philosophic Work)

terms.meaning: What the operator applies ('thy heat'), which must not exceed 'the natural proportion'; its literal nature is not stated (see ambiguities).

quotes.text: if thy heat exceeds the natural proportion

terms.meaning: Natures that, provoked by excess heat, rise against the central fire.

quotes.text: thou hast stirred up the wrath of the moist natures, and they will stand up against the central fire

terms.meaning: The fire which the moist natures oppose, and which opposes them, when heat is excessive.

quotes.text: they will stand up against the central fire, and the central fire against them

terms.meaning: That in which division occurs when moist natures and central fire are set against each other.

quotes.text: there will be a terrible division in the Chaos

terms.meaning: The eternal spirit of Peace in the elements, which departs from them under violent handling.

equivalences.quote: the sweet spirit of Peace, the true eternal Quintessence

quotes.text: will depart from the elements, leaving both of them and thee to confusion

terms.meaning: The 'principal' matter whose knowledge amounts to discovering the Sanctuary of Nature.

quotes.text: if thou knowest the principal First Matter, know also for certain thou hast discovered the Sanctuary of Nature

terms.meaning: Where Nature's treasures lie, behind a Door that must be opened; discovered by knowing the First Matter.

quotes.text: There is nothing between thee and her treasures but the Door: that indeed must be opened.

terms.meaning: The nurse of Faith: charitable works yield hope of heaven, and hope leads to belief.

quotes.text: as God is the Father, so Charity is the nurse of Faith

terms.meaning: Higher and lower orders: superiors dissolve, inferiors coagulate; communion with superiors needs a heavenly life.

quotes.text: so superiors dissolve and inferiors coagulate
no communion with superiors

terms.meaning: Agents to be used provisionally until a single determinate agent is found; not further defined.

quotes.text: Make use of indeterminate agents till thou canst find a determinate one

terms.meaning: What is to be sought where extremes meet; not further defined.

quotes.text: where extremes meet, there look for complexions

terms.meaning: Atwood's word for the work, for which perseverance is insisted on.

quotes.text: than perseverance for this experiment

terms.meaning: Figure for that to which Atwood's preceding exposition has been an introduction; not explained.

quotes.text: we conclude our introduction, as it may be called, to the Sphinx’s lair

terms.meaning: That whose application moves the first link in the chain of vital causes; not explained here.

quotes.text: The first link in the chain of vital causes moves, as we apply the Master Key.

terms.meaning: The first stage of the Hermetic Practice: purifying the medium of its wild affections and innate defects by dissolution, done by one way only, the Manual or Linear way.

equivalences.quote: Of the Vital Purification, Commonly Called the Gross Work

quotes.text: for the Purification we read but of one way, called by the Adepts Manual, and their Linear way
they proceeded at once scientifically to purify

terms.meaning: The subject on which the work is done; prepared by hand; burdened with heterogeneous superfluities.

quotes.text: Preparation of the Philosophic Subject
such a mass of heterogeneous superfluities adhering to our subject

terms.meaning: Literal handwork by the operator, chiefly required in the first work; the name of the one way of Purification.

equivalences.quote: called by the Adepts Manual, and their Linear way

quotes.text: Manual operation is chiefly required

terms.meaning: The single uniform course of the dissolution throughout, in one matter and one vessel; not further explained.

equivalences.quote: called by the Adepts Manual, and their Linear way

quotes.text: one linear decoction throughout and dissolution by line
one linear way throughout

terms.meaning: The senses' own light, in which they are entranced at the start of the practice.

quotes.text: entrancing the senses in their own medial light

terms.meaning: What is released or included by entrancing; in its natural state volatile, immanifest, phantastic, irrational; must be purified. Also used in ¶7 for the means by which the Royal Diadem is extracted.

quotes.text: the medium in its natural state is volatile, immanifest, phantastic, irrational, and important
many ways of including the sensible medium

terms.meaning: Used in two senses: the anaesthetic (with chloroform), and that which the Alchemists purified of its 'wild affections and impressures'.

quotes.text: the virtues of ether and chloroform too are familiar
depriving the ether of its wild affections and impressures

terms.meaning: A barrier surrounding 'our Heaven' that must be scaled and passed through before the equilibriate felicity of Being within is discerned.

quotes.text: this is that Brazen Wall celebrated by Antiquity, which surrounds our Heaven and must be scaled

terms.meaning: Albertus' name for the occult Nature, to be washed pure and clean and then dissolved, distilled, sublimed, calcined and fixed.

equivalences.quote: Take the occult Nature, which is our Brass

terms.meaning: The core operation of the first work: dissolving the subject (in its own blood / own mercury) to remove superfluities; begins the whole work and must be total.

quotes.text: The beginning of the whole work is a perfect solution
nothing short of dissolution can give it rest

terms.meaning: Fixing or setting, alternated with dissolution; the cleansed Argent vive is coagulated by its own internal sulfur.

quotes.text: a successive dissolution and coagulation to make the fixed volatile, and volatile fixed

terms.meaning: Grinding, used figuratively ('as it were') for the hand's continual working that dissolves the subject's innate defects.

quotes.text: by a continual mechanic trituration, as it were, to dissolve and ultimately obliterate its innate defects

terms.meaning: The Mercury of the philosophers comes only by ingenuity and manual operation (Lully); the Stone is dissolved in its own mercury (Arnold).

quotes.text: The Mercury of the philosophers, says Lully, comes not but by help of ingenuity, and the Manual operations of man
to dissolve the Stone in its own mercury

terms.meaning: What is dissolved in its own mercury to be reduced to first Matter.

quotes.text: The work of philosophers, says Arnold, is to dissolve the Stone in its own mercury

terms.meaning: The state to which the Stone is reduced by dissolution in its own mercury.

quotes.text: that it may be reduced into its first Matter

terms.meaning: The Adepts' secret, whose Theory shows the medium by which the Royal Diadem is extracted; dissolution is impossible without it.

quotes.text: it will be entirely impossible to accomplish without the Theory of their Arcanum

terms.meaning: What is extracted from the Sordid Subject by the medium the Arcanum shows; not further explained.

quotes.text: the medium by which the Royal Diadem may be extracted from our Sordid Subject

terms.meaning: A power whose dominion returns if the dissolution is left incomplete before 'the total solution of her enigma'.

quotes.text: the Sphinx should retrieve her dominion unawares and frustrate the work begun

terms.meaning: Image of the incessant, repeated purifying labor that clears the wasted field of human life.

quotes.text: to clear the wasted field of human life, and harrow it for a more congenial growth

terms.meaning: The cooking process, carried on linearly until complete.

quotes.text: donec decoctio compleatur

terms.meaning: The spirit that dissolves and cleanses the body of Light and extracts from it a Second, tinging Spirit.

quotes.text: The Preparing Spirit dissolves the body of Light, and cleanses it from the corrupting causes

terms.meaning: The body dissolved and cleansed by the Preparing Spirit, from which a tinging spirit is extracted.

quotes.text: dissolves the body of Light

terms.meaning: A spirit 'subsisting and tinging in the body', extracted by the Preparing Spirit.

quotes.text: extracts a Second Spirit subsisting and tinging in the body
extracting from it the tinging spirit

terms.meaning: At first gross, unclean, fugitive, mixed with extraneous Sulfurs; cleansed by Art and coagulated by its own internal sulfur, red and white; then subtle, penetrative, resolving mineral bodies; decocted linearly and generated pontically.

quotes.text: this Argent vive was at first gross, unclean, fugitive, being mingled with extraneous Sulfurs
this Argent vive, which is decocted linearly, is generated pontically

terms.meaning: Extraneous Sulfurs defile the Argent vive; its own internal sulfur, red and white, coagulates it.

quotes.text: being mingled with extraneous Sulfurs
coagulated by its own internal sulfur, red and white

terms.meaning: Manner in which the Argent vive is generated, 'as it were by a reciprocal alternation, distributing its advanced virtue by hand to hand'; not otherwise explained.

quotes.text: is generated pontically, as it were by a reciprocal alternation

terms.meaning: The laborious manual first stage, the most tedious work, concerned with disposing the matter as first found; contrasted with the Second, where Nature works alone.

quotes.text: there is no work more tedious than our First Operation
nothing can be achieved in the First Operation without sweating and much labor

terms.meaning: Accomplished by assiduity and industry, with the Divine blessing and a good principle to begin with.

quotes.text: it is by assiduity and industry that we accomplish the First Work

terms.meaning: A later work whose commencement Eirenaeus says he is not speaking of when describing the literal labor on things as first found.

quotes.text: I am not speaking here indeed of the commencement of the Supernatural Work, but of things as we first find them

terms.meaning: Stage in which Nature alone operates, without hands, by well-regulated external fire.

quotes.text: In the Second, however, Nature alone operates, and without any imposition of hands

terms.meaning: The well-regulated heat that alone assists Nature in the Second operation.

quotes.text: by the sole assistance of a well-regulated external fire

terms.meaning: Their exact preparation is the first degree of perfection in the Art; not explained here.

quotes.text: the exact preparation of the philosophic Eagles may be considered the first degree of perfection in this Art

terms.meaning: Means the Alchemists delivered for entering the sanctuary of philosophy; they do not unfold the first approach.

quotes.text: delivered many Keys, whereby, as they say, we may enter into the sanctuary of philosophy

terms.meaning: A long phase of the practice (three years would be a blessed chance): foul, perilous, costly, a handicraft full of possible faults; once completed it need not be begun again.

quotes.text: For the Gross Worke is foule in her kinde,
But handie crafte, called Art mechanical,

terms.meaning: Handicraft; what the Gross Work consists of.

equivalences.quote: But handie crafte, called Art mechanical,

terms.meaning: The operation to which, according to Atwood, the Ordinal's period of years chiefly refers; linked to the discovery of the philosophic Salt. Its relation to the Gross Work is not stated.

quotes.text: This is meant chiefly in reference to the Second Operation

terms.meaning: Something discovered in the work; the stated periods of the work are often metaphorical for the time it takes to discover it.

quotes.text: the periods are often to be understood metaphorically with respect to the discovery of the philosophic Salt

terms.meaning: A phase of the work on which some have spent years.

quotes.text: Years have been employed by some in the Preparation

terms.meaning: That on which trituration is performed; must be worked slowly, gently, continuously.

quotes.text: the trituration of the Philosophic Subject, which ought to be slow, gentle, and continuous

terms.meaning: The working of the Philosophic Subject, which should be slow, gentle and continuous.

quotes.text: especially to the trituration of the Philosophic Subject

terms.meaning: What is worked on: to be fed leisurely, cleansed, given wings but restrained.

quotes.text: Cause, therefore, wings to be prepared for the Matter
The length of clensing matters infected

terms.meaning: The subject in its first prepared state; what is meant by the Lunar Vulcan.

equivalences.quote: the Lunar Vulcan, as we long ago suggested, is meant the first prepared Subject
the first prepared Subject, which is also called Diana

equivalences.with: secret natural interior Fire of Adepts
equivalences.quote: which is also called Diana, and the secret natural interior Fire of Adepts

terms.meaning: The assistance with which those who trace nature prepare the Stone; means the first prepared Subject, Diana, the Adepts' secret interior Fire; as 'Lunar Caustic' brought into act by exterior excitation.

equivalences.quote: the Lunar Vulcan, as we long ago suggested, is meant the first prepared Subject
this same Lunar Caustic is brought into act by an exterior excitation

quotes.text: prepared by those who trace nature with the assistance of the Lunar Vulcan

terms.meaning: The goal of the work; a pure petrification of the Spirit, prepared with the Lunar Vulcan; its 'simperings' must be known.

equivalences.quote: the Stone of Philosophers, which is a pure petrification of the Spirit

quotes.text: To know the simperings of our Stone

terms.meaning: Something of the Stone that must be known, until it can 'no more simper'; the verse sets simmering against boiling (sense inferred).

quotes.text: To know the simperings of our Stone, Till it may no more simper do, nor cease,

terms.meaning: An inner agent which, awakened by too great excitation, can cause disseveration in the Chaos.

quotes.text: lest by too great excitation the internal agent awakening should cause a disseveration in the Chaos

terms.meaning: That in which disseveration may occur if the internal agent wakes too soon; it holds the two Principles.

quotes.text: a disseveration in the Chaos, and the two Principles stand up one against the other

terms.meaning: Two principles that stand against each other if the Chaos is prematurely dissevered; not named in this chunk.

quotes.text: the two Principles stand up one against the other, before the intended mastery is secure

terms.meaning: Paired terms: the centers must not be stirred before the circumferences are ready to conceive them; not further explained.

quotes.text: lest the centers should be stirred up before the circumferences are ready to conceive them

terms.meaning: Their 'indisposition' and 'ignorance' respectively protract the work; not defined further.

quotes.text: by the indisposition of patients, as by the ignorance of agents

terms.meaning: Practitioners of the Art, who aim at the 'harbor' reached when the Matter's bonds are loosed after its due time.

quotes.text: loose its bonds towards which all sons of Art aim to arrive as to their long-desired and sought for harbor

terms.meaning: What the seeker seeks; requires avoiding things wild and vicious.

quotes.text: He that would seek tincture most specious

terms.meaning: The whole secret of the work, revealed to Eirenaeus in two and a half years.

quotes.text: the whole Arcanum was revealed to him

terms.meaning: The handling of the work, which has 'particular turnings' in which Eirenaeus often erred.

quotes.text: in some particular turnings of the Encheiresis I erred often

terms.meaning: A master of the Art; Adepts caution against excitation and are abstruse and envious in their disguises.

quotes.text: whilst adepts are so very abstruse and envious in their disguises
of a vulgar ignoramus I became a true Adept

terms.meaning: What is met sooner or later in the work; the practice develops by rational inquisition of the Light within; one 'makes choice of Light'.

quotes.text: Some have met the Light sooner, some later
by rational inquisition of the Light within
to make choice of Light

terms.meaning: Nature's Causal Light, reached by rational permeation through the Understanding of Nature.

quotes.text: by the Understanding of Nature, into her Causal Light

terms.meaning: The way, by reflexive analysis of the analyzer, of penetrating through the Understanding of Nature into her Causal Light.

quotes.text: this is the way of rational permeation, by the Understanding of Nature, into her Causal Light

terms.meaning: The 'separable Selfhood', which reiterated reflexive analysis resolves.

quotes.text: it may resolve the separable Selfhood

terms.meaning: The inseparable unity at which the reiterated analysis arrives.

quotes.text: until it arrives at the inseparable Unit of Truth

terms.meaning: That by which the Art is obtained, rather than by reading, sitting still, fancy or will; to be sought.

quotes.text: But, as I said, by grace it is obtained:

terms.meaning: Its dominion is the court of Alcinous and is signified by the Phoeacian ships.

equivalences.quote: that court of King Alcinous, to which Ulysses became admitted, is the dominion of Intellect

terms.meaning: A region approached after the first barriers, where one must choose Light; not explained.

quotes.text: approaching to the Nether confines, to make choice of Light

terms.meaning: Mixing in of something; to be avoided.

quotes.text: Beware of Commixtion that nothing miscape.

terms.meaning: Container of the work; one kind in material and shape must be used.

quotes.text: Use one manner of vessel in matter and in shape

terms.meaning: Moisture that nourishes and educates the Solar Light; set beside Luna as 'Domina Humiditatis'.

quotes.text: The ethereal humidity nourishes the Solar Light and educates it

terms.meaning: Light nourished and educated by the ethereal humidity; set beside Sol as source of all heat.

quotes.text: nourishes the Solar Light and educates it

terms.meaning: Said to be born of 'her foam'; identified with what the preceding sentence describes (exact referent unclear; see ambiguities).

quotes.text: and this is that Nemean Lion said to be born of her foam

terms.meaning: The means by which a proposed end is obtained; deliberation weighs media and traces them back to the first Cause.

quotes.text: they consider how and by what Medium it may be obtained

terms.meaning: In deliberation, the cause reached last by working back from the proposed end through its media.

quotes.text: until they arrive at the first Cause which is discovered in the last place

terms.meaning: A means toward an end. Inquiry traces media back to the first one immediately in the operator's power, where inquiry ends and the work begins.

quotes.text: That Medium, therefore, which is last in the analysis is first in generation

terms.meaning: The actual work, to which few of those who consult on the means are chosen to proceed.

quotes.text: few are chosen to proceed with the Philosophic Work

terms.meaning: The greatest power of purgation. The Divine Will must be conciliated, and must be with anyone who communicates the secret.

quotes.text: Will is the greatest power of purgation
no mortal can communicate it to another unless the Divine Will be with him

terms.meaning: The double capacity Cheiron figures; it educates the Heroic Fire and rectifies the Armed Magnet.

quotes.text: in his double capacity of Power and Motive in alliance

terms.meaning: Something of 'illimitable virtue' that Power and Motive corrects, educates, tames and directs. Not further explained.

quotes.text: corrects and educates the Heroic Fire, tames and directs its illimitable virtue

terms.meaning: Rectified by Power and Motive 'by an infallible rule'. Not explained.

quotes.text: rectifies the Armed Magnet by an infallible rule

terms.meaning: That in which the Intellect is secure as it rides through the abyss of sensual monarchy.

quotes.text: that Intellect rides through the abyss of sensual monarchy, secure in its Ether

terms.meaning: Not born without the instrumentality of Motion (Vulcan); figured by Pallas brought forth from Jove with Vulcan's help.

quotes.text: without the instrumentality of Motion, which the lame god personates, the Fabricate Intellect is not born

terms.meaning: Personates Motion (Atwood, ¶34). In the monk's words (¶40), Fire's master, sole separator of good from evil and pure from impure; a Vulcan acts in the Greater Orb and 'a certain other Vulcan' in the Lesser World.

equivalences.quote: Motion, which the lame god personates

quotes.text: Fire only can effect that, and Vulcan is the sole and only master of all these

terms.meaning: Called 'hyper-physical' here. It has a First Preparation and a Second part, the Second being one of the Art's greatest subtleties.

quotes.text: this said hyper-physical Gross Work

terms.meaning: The first part of the Gross Work, which Agrippa knew and made clear. Not described here.

quotes.text: knew the First Preparation, and has clearly discovered it

variants: Second part of the Gross Work
terms.meaning: One of the Art's greatest subtleties; it is the Solution of the Philosophic Salt.

equivalences.quote: By the Second Work we are to understand, therefore, the Solution of the Philosophic Salt

terms.meaning: Glossed as the voluntary bond. Its solution is the Second Work; knowing it and its solution is the secret of the Ancient Sages.

equivalences.quote: the Solution of the Philosophic Salt (i.e., the voluntary bond)

quotes.text: He who knows the Salt and its solution, knows the secret of the Ancient Sages.

terms.meaning: The dissolving of the Philosophic Salt; Lully performed it in nine days.

quotes.text: he performed the Solution in nine days

terms.meaning: What Ripley tried to putrefy by alternate heat and cold; he called it his Gold.

equivalences.quote: this Red Salt which he enviously calls his Gold

terms.meaning: The central difficulty of the Hermetic Mystery: knowing the Salt and its solution.

quotes.text: Here then liest the Gordian Knot of the Hermetic Mystery

terms.meaning: The starting matter of the first act, whose bonds of coagulation are relaxed; 'our heart of Saturn'.

equivalences.quote: Adrop (which in its proper tongue is called Saturn, i.e., the lead of the Wise)
called Saturn, i.e., the lead of the Wise

quotes.text: our heart of Saturn

terms.meaning: Appears with the Vitriol of Venus when the bonds of coagulation are relaxed; together they are the true matters of the Blessed Stone.

equivalences.with: true matters of the Blessed Stone (with the Vitriol of Venus)
equivalences.quote: the Green Duenech and the Vitriol of Venus, which are the true matters of the Blessed Stone

terms.meaning: With the Green Duenech, the true matters of the Blessed Stone.

equivalences.with: true matters of the Blessed Stone (with the Green Duenech)
equivalences.quote: the Green Duenech and the Vitriol of Venus, which are the true matters of the Blessed Stone

terms.meaning: Hidden in the Cavern of his Saturnine Hill; drawn out by allurements suited to his nature, pierced with a lance, his blood collected. Not otherwise explained.

quotes.text: The Green Lion, lurking and concealed, is drawn forth from the Cavern of his Saturnine Hill

terms.meaning: Made manifest in the first act as a wet, impure 'mud earth' partaking of Adam; First Matter of the Greater World 'of our very selves' and of the Stone.

equivalences.quote: the mud earth, wet, humid, stagnant, impure, partaking of Adam, the First Matter

quotes.text: the First Matter of the creation of the Greater World of our very selves and of our potent Stone

terms.meaning: A thick, dense substance, 'blacker than black', appearing in the first act; called Red for its tincture, the color of its virtue.

equivalences.quote: the Wine which the Wise have called the Blood of the Earth
which likewise is the Red of Lully

quotes.text: thick, dense, and black, blacker than black

terms.meaning: What the impure body becomes when consumed and blackened; of great worth, holding 'our pigmy'.

equivalences.quote: they are the diadem of thy body

quotes.text: in them lies our pigmy, conquering and subduing giants

terms.meaning: Khunrath's second stage after the first act: in one vessel, one furnace, one fire, body, spirit and soul dissolve and reunite by nature alone, without manual cooperation.

quotes.text: rot of themselves and without manual cooperation, by the sole labors of nature

terms.meaning: The one theosophic, cabalistically sealed furnace of the Second Operation.

quotes.text: one theosophic cabalistically sealed furnace of Athanor

terms.meaning: In the dissolution the fixed is made volatile, and in the Second Operation 'wholly'. Fixed Antimony reaches fixed disease; the fixed must be separated from the unfixed.

quotes.text: the fixed is made volatile
the fixed from the unfixed

terms.meaning: Agents relied on through 'Second qualities'; wrongly credited with the 'single combat'. The real agent is a specific virtue of loosening.

quotes.text: They err, therefore, who ascribe this single combat only to Corrosives

terms.meaning: Those who trust second qualities and neglect specific (appropriated) ones, which act only on their proper object, go astray.

equivalences.quote: specifical qualities, also appropriated ones (which are only extended on their proper object)

quotes.text: they too much trusting to Second qualities, as being ill secure, do sleep thereupon

terms.meaning: That whose 'bars and bolts' a specific virtue looses.

quotes.text: a virtue of loosing the bars and bolts of Tartar

terms.meaning: Where the Scriptural phrase is 'seen and proved'; there man may experiment, plough, plant and irrigate but cannot compel the Divine Blessing.

quotes.text: as seen and proved on the Divine Ground

terms.meaning: A fixed medicine that reaches the root of fixed disease, but only after all venomous impurity is removed. Atwood glosses that removal as purging the operator's mind of self-will and other vices.

quotes.text: Our Antimony, says Basil Valentine, which is fixed, searcheth out fixed diseases and eradicates them

terms.meaning: What the operator enters once self-will and the other vices are removed from his mind.

quotes.text: be removed from the mind of him who is to enter into the radical dissolution of Life

terms.meaning: Two domains, each with its Vulcan; the Vulcan of the Lesser World amends what that of the Greater Orb leaves crude.

quotes.text: Whatsoever the Vulcan in the Greater Orb leaves crude and perfects not, that in the Lesser World must be amended by a certain other Vulcan

terms.meaning: Instituted by one who has contracted friendship with Vulcan; only he can demonstrate the separation of venom from the Medicine. Not explained.

quotes.text: firmly contracted friendship with Vulcan, and instituted the Fiery bath of Love

terms.meaning: The subject to be placed equally within two elements in the vital heat-operation; said to be a middle Nature.

equivalences.quote: the Moon of the Firmament, which is a middle Nature

quotes.text: take the Moon of the Firmament, which is a middle Nature

terms.meaning: Two Mercuries, one planted in the other, cherished in the Alembic over a constant sun-like fire; not further explained.

quotes.text: the Solar and Lunar Mercury, and the plantation of the one in the other

terms.meaning: The vessel in which the Mercuries are cherished over fire.

quotes.text: cherish them over a fire in thy Alembic

terms.meaning: State of the earth after repeated extraction and return of its water: corrupted, without its Form, dead for a season.

quotes.text: until the earth is completely putrefied

terms.meaning: What the body loses in putrefaction; also what the Universal Element's invisible vapor is compressed into ('tangible Form').

quotes.text: to corrupt and to lose its Form
compress its invisible vapor into a tangible Form

terms.meaning: What the matter, brought to the right condition by action and reaction, attracts.

quotes.text: to supply the right condition for attracting the Divine Seed

terms.meaning: Paired principles raised successively by each other through action and reaction until spiritual ability is complete.

quotes.text: raising successively actives by passives, and, vice versa, passives by actives

terms.meaning: Ingredient (four parts) bearing the Magic Steel in its belly, conjoined to nine parts Lodestone; not explained here.

quotes.text: Take four parts of our Fiery Dragon, which bears in his belly the Magic Steel

terms.meaning: Carried in the belly of the Fiery Dragon; not explained here.

quotes.text: which bears in his belly the Magic Steel

terms.meaning: Ingredient (nine parts) conjoined with the Fiery Dragon; not explained here.

quotes.text: conjoin to nine parts of our Lodestone

terms.meaning: Product of the Dragon/Lodestone conjunction and purgations; a chaos containing all Arcana in virtue, not in act.

equivalences.quote: the Chamelion which is our Chaos

quotes.text: Hence comes the Chamelion which is our Chaos, in which all the Arcana are contained; not in act as yet, but in virtue

terms.meaning: The secrets contained in the Chaos potentially ('in virtue'), not yet actually.

quotes.text: in which all the Arcana are contained; not in act as yet, but in virtue

terms.meaning: The fire of the work; its action both destroys and maintains life.

quotes.text: Which Vulcanic action, to destroy life and to maintain it
placing it again upon the coals, stir Vulcan into it

terms.meaning: Material drawn out and worked on the coals in the Democritus passage until it appears Golden.

quotes.text: Drawing the fixed Brass out bodily

terms.meaning: The operator's motive, on which everything depends; the result corresponds to its virtue; the Work truly begins only when the right Motive is discovered.

equivalences.quote: the Motive, which is the true spiritual ferment

quotes.text: Everything depends upon the Motive, which is the true spiritual ferment
it is not until the right Motive is discovered

terms.meaning: The active, spiritualizing principle by whose virtue the result is obtained; the philosophic matter is purified by successive interchange of ferments, as sap becomes wine.

quotes.text: according to the virtue of the fermenting principle is the result obtained
is purified by successive interchanging of ferments

terms.meaning: The matter of the Hermetic art, drawn partly from air and the defiled breath of vitality, purified into an immortal Form of Light.

quotes.text: the philosophic matter, drawn in part from the heterogeneous air and defiled breath of vitality

terms.meaning: The consummate, immortal form into which the philosophic matter is finally rectified.

quotes.text: rectified into a consummate and immortal Form of Light

terms.meaning: The divine source obscured by the common elements and not identifiable by chemistry.

quotes.text: The common elements of Nature obscure their Divine Original

terms.meaning: What the Alchemists rectify: an invisible vapor compressed into tangible Form; contrasted with the common elements of chemistry.

quotes.text: to rectify the Universal Element, and compress its invisible vapor into a tangible Form

terms.meaning: The agent applied to obliterate the defilements of the Universal Element; first in a series with gentleness, beneficence and justice.

quotes.text: By applying the proper voluntary corrosive they teach to obliterate its defilements

terms.meaning: The product the Alchemists made sublime by actual subversion of the selfhood.

quotes.text: they made their Sublimate sublime

terms.meaning: That whose actual subversion completes the rectification and sublimation.

quotes.text: by an actual subversion of the selfhood

terms.meaning: The riddle whose solution is rationally penetrating the darkened essence of one's natural understanding; Mind is its Key.

equivalences.with: the darkened essence of his natural understanding (to be penetrated rationally)
equivalences.quote: to solve the Enigma of the Sphinx; in other words, to penetrate rationally the darkened essence of his natural understanding

quotes.text: For Mind is the Key of this Hermetic Enigma

terms.meaning: The Key of the Hermetic Enigma; attains Self Knowledge by inquiry within, whereupon the Efficient acts outward.

equivalences.quote: Mind is the Key of this Hermetic Enigma

quotes.text: no sooner does it attain to Self Knowledge, by proper inquiry within

terms.meaning: The effective power that, once Mind attains Self Knowledge, proceeds outward to image its motive in operation.

quotes.text: the Efficient proceeds out wards to image its motive in operation

terms.meaning: Cleansing of the Spirit, to be completed 'in both kinds' before the Philosophic Work truly begins.

quotes.text: until the mundification of the Spirit is completed in both kinds

terms.meaning: The transparent state to which all things must be reduced before the Work truly begins.

quotes.text: all things are reduced to a crystalline diaphaneity

terms.meaning: The work proper, which begins only after the right Motive, complete mundification and crystalline diaphaneity; what precedes is preparatory.

quotes.text: that the Philosophic Work has been said truly to being
The philosopher’s worke doe not begin Till all things be pure without and within

terms.meaning: A permanent fixing; if made or allowed prematurely, its immature offspring does not abide.

quotes.text: if any permanent confection is made or suffered to take place beforehand, the immature offspring does not abide

terms.meaning: What the seeker aims at; seeking it requires avoiding all things wild and vicious.

quotes.text: He that would seek Tincture most specious Must needly avoid all things wild and vicious.

terms.meaning: The Work treated in this chapter, with a threefold order of operation the Adepts concealed; distinct from the preliminary practice. Norton's verse calls it 'this Subtill Werke'.

equivalences.quote: Of the Philosophic or Subtle Work

quotes.text: in the Philosophic Work, preceding her, there is a threefold order of legitimate operation

terms.meaning: The concealment under which the Adepts kept the three operations.

this same Root of Reason is Wisdom, and that saving Salt
